title.zh: 卷三十一 志第七 曆一
title.raw: 卷三十一 志第七 曆一 Volume 31 Treatises 7: Calendar 1

sentences.zh: 志第七 曆一

translations.literal: Treatise 7, Calendar 1.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise Seven: Calendrics, Part One.

sentences.zh: 後世法勝於古，而屢改益密者，惟曆為最著。

translations.literal: In later ages methods surpass antiquity, and of those repeatedly revised to grow ever tighter, only the calendar is most conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: Among the sciences, calendrics alone shows most clearly how later methods surpass the ancient and how repeated revision makes computation ever tighter.

sentences.zh: 《唐志》謂天為動物，久則差忒，不得不屢變其法以求之。

translations.literal: The Tang Treatises say heaven is a moving thing; long use brings deviation, and one cannot but repeatedly change the method to seek it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang dynastic treatises hold that heaven is in motion and that, over long intervals, error accumulates—hence calendar law must be changed again and again.

sentences.zh: 此說似矣，而不然也。

translations.literal: This doctrine seems plausible, yet is not so.
translations.idiomatic: That argument sounds plausible; it is not correct.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「天地之道，貞觀者也。

translations.literal: The Yi says: "The Way of Heaven and Earth is constancy in correct observation."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "The Way of Heaven and Earth is constancy in correct observation."

sentences.zh: 」蓋天行至健，確然有常，本無古今之異。

translations.literal: Heaven's motion is supremely vigorous, firmly constant, and in essence has no ancient-versus-modern difference.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven moves with supreme vigor yet with firm constancy; in principle it does not differ between antiquity and the present.

sentences.zh: 其歲差盈縮遲疾諸行，古無今有者，因其數甚微，積久始著。

translations.literal: Its precession, elongation, fast-slow, and other motions—what antiquity lacked and the present has—are because their numbers are extremely small and only after long accumulation become visible.
translations.idiomatic: Precession, solar elongation, lunar anomaly, and the like—phenomena the ancients did not notice but we do—arise because the underlying quantities are minute and only become visible after centuries of accumulation.

sentences.zh: 古人不覺，而後人知之，而非天行之忒也。

translations.literal: The ancients did not perceive them, while later men know them; this is not heaven's motion going awry.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients did not perceive them; later astronomers did. That is not a deviation in heaven's motion itself.

sentences.zh: 使天果久動而差忒，則必差參淩替而無典耍，安從修改而使之益密哉？

translations.literal: If heaven truly moved long and deviated, then there would surely be chaotic disorder without canonical rule—how could revision make it ever tighter?
translations.idiomatic: If heaven truly drifted over long ages, observations would fall into chaotic disorder and no stable canon would remain—how then could repeated revision make calculation ever more precise?

sentences.zh: 觀傳志所書，歲失其次、日度失行之事，不見於近代，亦可見矣。

translations.literal: Observing what dynastic histories record, cases of the year losing its season or the sun's degree losing its course are not seen in recent times—this too is evident.
translations.idiomatic: Dynastic histories record years that lost their proper season and solar motion that missed its track; such failures do not appear in recent centuries—which itself tells the tale.

sentences.zh: 夫天之行度多端，而人之智力有限，持尋尺之儀錶，仰測穹蒼，安能洞悉無遺。

translations.literal: Heaven's degrees of motion are manifold, while human intelligence is limited; holding a foot-rule instrument and looking up to measure the vault—how can one penetrate all without omission?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's motions are manifold and human intellect finite; armed only with foot-scale instruments and gazing upward at the vault, who can compass every detail?

sentences.zh: 惟合古今人心思，踵事增修，庶幾符合。

translations.literal: Only by joining the minds of ancients and moderns and, following precedent, adding refinements, may one hope for agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Agreement is possible only when ancient and modern insight are combined and each generation, building on its predecessors, adds refinements.

sentences.zh: 故不能為一成不易之法也。

translations.literal: Therefore one cannot make an unchanging method for all time.
translations.idiomatic: Hence no calendar law can remain fixed for all time.

sentences.zh: 黃帝迄秦，曆凡六改。

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor through Qin, the calendar was changed six times in all.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor through Qin, the calendar was revised six times.

sentences.zh: 漢凡四改。

translations.literal: Han: four changes in all.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han: four revisions.

sentences.zh: 魏迄隋，十五改。

translations.literal: Wei through Sui: fifteen changes.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei through Sui: fifteen revisions.

sentences.zh: 唐迄五代，十五改。

translations.literal: Tang through the Five Dynasties: fifteen changes.
translations.idiomatic: From Tang through the Five Dynasties: fifteen revisions.

sentences.zh: 宋十七改。

translations.literal: Song: seventeen changes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song: seventeen revisions.

sentences.zh: 金迄元，五改。

translations.literal: Jin through Yuan: five changes.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin through Yuan: five revisions.

sentences.zh: 惟明之《大統曆》，實即元之《授時》，承用二百七十餘年，未嘗改憲。

translations.literal: Only Ming's Datong Calendar in fact is Yuan's Shoushi, employed for more than two hundred seventy years without ever changing the statute.
translations.idiomatic: Ming's Datong Calendar was in substance the Yuan Shoushi Calendar, kept in force for more than two hundred seventy years without statutory revision.

sentences.zh: 成化以後，交食往往不驗，議改曆者紛紛。

translations.literal: After Chenghua, eclipses and conjunctions often failed verification; those urging calendar reform were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chenghua reign, predicted eclipses and conjunctions repeatedly failed verification, and calls for calendar reform multiplied.

sentences.zh: 如俞正己、冷守中不知妄作者無論已，而華湘、周濂、李之藻、刑雲路之倫頗有所見。

translations.literal: Such as Yu Zhengji and Leng Shouzhong, ignorant fabricators, need not be discussed; yet Hua Xiang, Zhou Lian, Li Zhizao, Xing Yunlu, and their kind had considerable insight.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhengji and Leng Shouzhong, who wrote without understanding, may be passed over; but Hua Xiang, Zhou Lian, Li Zhizao, Xing Yunlu, and others of that company had real insight.

sentences.zh: 鄭世子載堉撰《律曆融通》，進《聖壽萬年曆》，其說本之南部御史何瑭，深得《授時》之意，而能補其不逮。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zheng, Zhu Zaiyu, compiled Harmonization of Pitch and Calendar, presented the Sacred Longevity Ten-Thousand-Year Calendar; his doctrine derives from the southern censor He Tang, deeply grasping Shoushi's intent and able to supply what it lacked.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zheng Zhu Zaiyu compiled the Harmonization of Pitch and Calendar and presented the Sacred Longevity Ten-Thousand-Year Calendar. His theory drew on the southern censor He Tang, grasped the intent of the Shoushi system, and remedied its gaps.

sentences.zh: 臺官泥於舊聞，當事憚於改作，並格而不行。

translations.literal: Observatory officials clung to old reports; those in charge feared to alter the work; all were rejected and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Observatory officers clung to received tradition; decision-makers shrank from reform; every proposal was blocked.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，議用西洋新法，命閣臣徐光啟、光祿卿李天經先後董其事，成《曆書》一百三十餘卷，多發古人所未發。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen period, Western new methods were debated; Grand Secretary Xu Guangqi and Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Li Tianjing were ordered in succession to direct the matter, producing more than one hundred thirty juan of Calendar Treatises, many points the ancients had not opened.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen, Western calendrical methods were adopted. Grand Secretary Xu Guangqi and Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Li Tianjing directed the project in turn and produced the Calendar Treatises in more than 130 juan, opening many questions the ancients had not addressed.

sentences.zh: 時布衣魏文魁上疏排之，詔立兩愕扒驗。

translations.literal: At the time the commoner Wei Wenkui memorialized to oppose it; an edict established two [bureaus] for comparative verification.
translations.idiomatic: The commoner Wei Wenkui then memorialized against the new methods; the throne ordered two bureaus to compare and verify them.

sentences.zh: 累年校測，新法獨密，然亦未及頒行。

translations.literal: After years of comparative testing, the new method alone was tight; yet it still was not promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: Years of comparative testing showed the new method alone to be precise, yet it was still not promulgated.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，曆固未有行之久而差者，烏可不隨時修改，以求合天哉。

translations.literal: Viewed thus, the calendar indeed has none that, long in use, goes awry—how can one not revise it with the times to seek agreement with heaven?
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that no calendar grows inaccurate merely from long use; revision must track the times so that computation again matches heaven.

sentences.zh: 今採扣家論說，有裨於曆法者，著於篇端。

translations.literal: Now collecting [various] schools' discussions useful to calendrics, they are set at the chapter's head.
translations.idiomatic: Here we collect discussions from various schools that bear on calendrics and place them at the head of the chapter.

sentences.zh: 而《大統曆》則述立法之原，以補《元志》之未備。

translations.literal: The Datong Calendar then narrates the origins of legislation, to supplement what the Yuan Treatises left incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: The Datong Calendar section sets out the origins of its rules, supplementing omissions in the Yuan dynastic treatises.

sentences.zh: 《回回曆》始終隸於欽天監，與《大統》參用無形之質，形而下為有形之物。

translations.literal: The Islamic calendar from first to last was subordinate to the Directorate of Astronomy, used together with the Datong; formless substance, below form are formed things.
translations.idiomatic: The Islamic (Huihui) calendar remained under the Imperial Observatory throughout and was employed alongside the Datong calendar. Qi lacks a formless substrate; what lies below form is the realm of embodied things.

sentences.zh: 南宋朱熹認為，理為形而上，亦附錄焉。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi of the Southern Song held that li is above form; this too is appended.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi of the Southern Song held that li (pattern) belongs to the realm above form; that doctrine is appended as well.

sentences.zh: ▲曆法沿革

translations.literal: ▲ Evolution of calendar methods
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Evolution of Calendar Methods

sentences.zh: 吳元年十一月乙未冬至，太史院使劉基率其屬高翼上戊申《大統曆》。

translations.literal: Wu year 1, eleventh month, day yimao at winter solstice: Director of the Astrological Academy Liu Ji led his subordinate Gao Yi to present the Datong Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wu, on the winter solstice (day yimao, eleventh month), Astrological Academy Director Liu Ji led his subordinate Gao Yi in presenting the Datong Calendar.

sentences.zh: 太祖諭曰：「古者季冬頒曆，太遲。

translations.literal: The Founder instructed: "Antiquity issued the calendar in last winter month—too late.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder instructed: "In antiquity the calendar was issued in the last month of winter—that is too late.

sentences.zh: 今於冬至，亦未善。

translations.literal: Now at winter solstice is also not good.
translations.idiomatic: Issuing it at the winter solstice is also unsatisfactory.

sentences.zh: 宜以十月朔，著為令。

translations.literal: It should be fixed by the first day of the tenth month and established as statute."
translations.idiomatic: Fix the first day of the tenth month as the date of issue and make it law."

sentences.zh: 」洪武元年改院為司天監，又置回回司天監。

translations.literal: Hongwu year 1 changed the Academy to the Directorate of Astronomy, and also established the Islamic Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 the Academy was renamed the Directorate of Astronomy, and an Islamic Directorate of Astronomy was also established.

sentences.zh: 詔徵元太史院使張佑、回回司天太監黑的兒等共十四人，尋召回回司天臺官鄭阿裡等十一有至京，議曆法。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Yuan Astrological Academy Director Zhang You, Islamic Chief Astronomical Supervisor Hei De'er, and fourteen others in all; soon the Islamic observatory officers Zheng Ali and eleven others arrived at the capital to discuss calendar methods.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned the Yuan Astrological Academy director Zhang You, the Islamic chief astronomical supervisor Hei De'er, and twelve others—fourteen in all. Soon eleven Islamic observatory officers including Zheng Ali reached the capital to deliberate on calendar methods.

sentences.zh: 三年改監為欽天，設四科：曰天文，曰漏刻，曰《大統曆》，曰《回回曆》。

translations.literal: Year 3 changed the Directorate to Imperial Astronomy, establishing four sections: called Astronomy, Clepsydra, Datong Calendar, and Islamic Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 the directorate was renamed the Imperial Observatory and divided into four sections: astronomy, clepsydra, the Datong calendar, and the Islamic calendar.

sentences.zh: 以監令、少監統之。

translations.literal: The Director and Vice Director supervised them.
translations.idiomatic: A director and deputy director supervised all four.

sentences.zh: 歲造《大統民曆》、《御覽月令曆》、《七政躔度曆》、《六壬遁甲曆》、《四季天象佔驗曆》、《御覽天象錄》，各以時上。

translations.literal: Each year were produced the Datong Popular Calendar, Imperial Monthly Command Calendar, Seven Luminaries Positions Calendar, Liuren Dunjia Calendar, Four Seasons Celestial Omens Verification Calendar, and Imperial Celestial Phenomena Record, each submitted at its season.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the observatory produced the Datong popular calendar, the imperial monthly-command calendar, the seven-luminaries ephemeris, the Liuren Dunjia calendar, the four-seasons omen-verification calendar, and the imperial celestial record, each submitted on schedule.

sentences.zh: 其日月交食分秒時刻、起復方位，先期以聞。

translations.literal: Solar and lunar eclipses' degrees, seconds, and times, and the directions of first contact and recovery, were reported in advance.
translations.idiomatic: For solar and lunar eclipses—magnitude, seconds, time, and the azimuths of first contact and recovery—reports were filed in advance.

sentences.zh: 十年三月，帝與羣臣論天與七政之行，皆以蔡氏旋之說對。

translations.literal: Year 10, third month: the Emperor discussed with ministers the motion of heaven and the seven luminaries; all answered with Master Cai's doctrine of rotation.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10, third month, the Emperor debated with his ministers the motion of heaven and the seven luminaries; all answered in terms of Master Cai's rotation theory.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕自起以來，仰觀乾象，天左旋，七政右旋，曆家之論，確然不易。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Since I rose, observing the heavenly signs, heaven turns left and the seven luminaries turn right—the astronomers' doctrine is firmly unchangeable.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Since I took power I have watched the sky: heaven rotates to the left and the seven luminaries to the right. The astronomers' doctrine is settled and not to be altered.

sentences.zh: 爾等猶守蔡氏之說，豈所謂格物致知學乎？

translations.literal: You still cling to Master Cai's doctrine—is this what is called the learning of investigating things to extend knowledge?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you still cling to Master Cai—is that what you call investigating things to extend knowledge?"

sentences.zh: 」十五年九月，詔翰林李翀、吳伯宗譯《回回曆書》。

translations.literal: Year 15, ninth month: ordered Hanlin Academicians Li Chong and Wu Bozong to translate the Islamic Calendar Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15, ninth month, Hanlin academicians Li Chong and Wu Bozong were ordered to translate the Islamic Calendar Treatise.

sentences.zh: 十七年閏十月，漏刻博士元統言：「曆以《大統》為名，而積分猶踵《授時》之數，非所以重始敬正也。

translations.literal: Year 17, intercalary tenth month, Clepsydra Doctor Yuan Tong said: "The calendar bears the name Datong, yet accumulated parts still follow Shoushi's numbers—not the way to honor the beginning and revere the correct.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17, intercalary tenth month, Clepsydra Doctor Yuan Tong said: "The calendar is called Datong, yet its accumulated parts still follow Shoushi numbers. That is not how to honor a new beginning and revere the correct alignment.

sentences.zh: 況《授時》以元辛巳為曆元，至洪武甲子積一百四年，年遠數盈，漸差天度，合修改。

translations.literal: Moreover Shoushi took the Yuan year xinsi as calendar origin; to Hongwu jiazi is an accumulation of one hundred four years—the years distant, numbers full, gradually diverging from heaven's degrees; revision is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Shoushi calendar took the Yuan year xinsi as its epoch; by Hongwu jiazi one hundred four years had elapsed. With time the parameters overflow and drift from celestial degrees; revision is due.

sentences.zh: 七政運行不齊，其理深奧。

translations.literal: The seven luminaries' motions are not uniform; their principle is profound and abstruse.
translations.idiomatic: The seven luminaries do not move uniformly; the theory is profound.

sentences.zh: 聞有郭伯玉者，精明九數之理，宜徵令推算，以成一代之制。

translations.literal: It is heard that Guo Boyu is skilled in the principles of the nine numbers; he should be summoned to calculate and complete a generation's system."
translations.idiomatic: I hear that Guo Boyu is expert in the mathematics of the Nine Chapters; summon him to compute and establish a system for this dynasty."

sentences.zh: 」報可。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 擢統為監令。

translations.literal: Tong was promoted to Director.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tong was promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 統乃取《授時曆》，去其歲實消長之說，析其條例，得四卷，以洪武十七年甲子為曆元，命曰《大統曆法通軌》。

translations.literal: Tong then took the Shoushi Calendar, removed its doctrine of varying the tropical year, analyzed its articles into four juan, took Hongwu 17 jiazi as calendar origin, and named it Comprehensive Tracks of Datong Calendar Methods.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tong took the Shoushi Calendar, discarded its theory of varying the tropical year, analyzed its rules into four juan, set Hongwu 17 jiazi as the epoch, and titled the work Comprehensive Tracks of Datong Calendar Methods.

sentences.zh: 二十二年改監令、丞為監正、副。

translations.literal: Year 22 changed Director and Assistant Director to Director and Deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 the titles director and assistant director were changed to director and deputy director.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，監副李德芳言：「監正統孜作洪武甲子曆元，不用消長之法，以考魯獻公十五年戊寅歲天正冬至，比辛巳為元，差四日半強。

translations.literal: Year 26, Deputy Director Li Defang said: "Director [Yuan] Tong made the Hongwu jiazi epoch and did not use the variation method; examining Duke Ai of Lu year 15 wuyin year's celestial winter solstice, compared with xinsi as origin, the difference is four and a fraction days strong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 Deputy Director Li Defang said: "Director Yuan Tong set the Hongwu jiazi epoch and abandoned the variation method. Reckoning the celestial winter solstice of Duke Ai of Lu's fifteenth year (wuyin), against an xinsi epoch the discrepancy is four and a fraction days.

sentences.zh: 今當復用辛巳為元及消長之法。

translations.literal: Now one should restore xinsi as origin and the variation method."
translations.idiomatic: The xinsi epoch and the variation method should be restored."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，元統奏辨。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; Yuan Tong memorialized in rebuttal.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received; Yuan Tong rebutted it in a counter-memorial.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「二說皆難憑，但驗七政交會行度無差者為是。

translations.literal: The Founder said: "Both doctrines are hard to rely on; only verify that the seven luminaries' conjunctions and motions have no discrepancy—that is correct."
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said: "Neither argument can be trusted on its own; accept whichever yields no error in the conjunctions and motions of the seven luminaries."

sentences.zh: 」自是《大統曆》元以洪武甲子，而推算仍依《授時》法。

translations.literal: From this the Datong Calendar's origin was Hongwu jiazi, while computation still followed Shoushi methods.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Datong epoch remained Hongwu jiazi, but computation still followed Shoushi procedure.

sentences.zh: 三十一年在罷回回欽天監，其《回回曆》科仍舊。

translations.literal: Year 31 again abolished the Islamic Imperial Observatory; its Islamic Calendar section remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 31 the Islamic Imperial Observatory was abolished again; the Islamic calendar section continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 永樂遷都順天，仍用應天冬夏晝夜時刻，至正統十四年始改用順天之數。

translations.literal: Yongle moved the capital to Shuntian, still using Yingtian's winter-summer day-night clepsydra divisions; only in Zhengtong 14 were Shuntian's numbers adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongle moved the capital to Shuntian, the observatory still used Yingtian's winter and summer day-length divisions; Shuntian values were adopted only in Zhengtong 14.

sentences.zh: 其冬，景帝即位，天文生馬軾奏，晝夜時刻不宜改。

translations.literal: That winter the Jing Emperor succeeded; astronomy student Ma Shi memorialized that day-night divisions should not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the Jing Emperor succeeded, astronomy student Ma Shi argued that the day-night divisions should not be altered.

sentences.zh: 下廷臣集議。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down for ministers to deliberate in assembly.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the ministries for joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 監正許惇等言：「前監正彭德清測驗得北京北極出地四十度，比南京高七度有奇，冬至晝三十八刻，夏至晝六十二刻。

translations.literal: Director Xu Dun and others said: "Former Director Peng Deqing's testing found Beijing's north pole altitude forty degrees, seven odd degrees higher than Nanjing; winter solstice day forty-eight clepsydra divisions, summer solstice sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Director Xu Dun and others said: "Former director Peng Deqing measured Beijing's polar altitude at forty degrees—more than seven degrees higher than Nanjing—with winter-solstice daylength of thirty-eight clepsydra divisions and summer of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 奏準改入《大曆》，永為定式。

translations.literal: Memorial approved for insertion into the Great Calendar, forever as fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved incorporating these values into the great calendar as a permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 軾言誕妄，不足聽。

translations.literal: Shi's words are wild and absurd, not worth heeding."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi's claims are absurd and should not be followed."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「太陽出入度數，當用四方之中。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The sun's degrees of rising and setting should use the center among the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Degrees of sunrise and sunset should be reckoned from the geographic center of the realm.

sentences.zh: 今京師在堯幽都之地，寧可為準。

translations.literal: Now the capital is in the land of Yao's Youdu—how can it serve as standard?
translations.idiomatic: The capital stands in the region of Yao's Youdu—how can it be the standard?

sentences.zh: 此後造曆，仍用洪、永舊制。」

translations.literal: Hereafter in making calendars, still use the Hongwu and Yongle old system."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth calendar-making shall follow the Hongwu and Yongle conventions."

sentences.zh: 景泰元年正月辛卯，卯正三刻月食。

translations.literal: Jingtai year 1, first month, day xinmao: at mao upright third quarter, lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 1, first month, day xinmao: lunar eclipse at the third quarter of mao upright.

sentences.zh: 監官誤推辰初初刻，致失救護。

translations.literal: Observatory officers wrongly computed chen initial first quarter, causing failure of the rescue rites.
translations.idiomatic: Observatory officers had predicted chen initial first quarter and failed the ritual response.

sentences.zh: 下法司，論徒。

translations.literal: Sent down to the judiciary; sentenced to penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the judiciary; they were sentenced to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 詔宥之。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 成化十年，以監官多不職，擢雲南提學童軒為太常寺少卿，掌監事。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 10, because many observatory officers were derelict, Yunnan Education Intendant Tong Xuan was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to manage observatory affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 10: with many observatory officers negligent, Yunnan education intendant Tong Xuan was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to oversee the observatory.

sentences.zh: 十五年十一月戊戍望，月食，監推又誤，帝以天象微渺，不之罪也。

translations.literal: Year 15, eleventh month, day wuxu at full moon, lunar eclipse; the observatory's computation again erred; the Emperor, because celestial phenomena are subtle, did not punish.
translations.idiomatic: Year 15, eleventh month, full moon (day wuxu): lunar eclipse; the observatory erred again. The Emperor held celestial phenomena too subtle for blame and imposed no punishment.

sentences.zh: 十七年，真定教論俞正己上《改曆議》，詔禮部及軒參考。

translations.literal: Year 17, Zhending Instructor Yu Zhengji submitted Discussion on Calendar Reform; ordered the Ministry of Rites and Tong Xuan to consult.
translations.idiomatic: Year 17: Zhending instructor Yu Zhengji submitted his Discussion on Calendar Reform; the Ministry of Rites and Tong Xuan were ordered to review it.

sentences.zh: 尚書周洪謨等言：「正己止據《皇極經世書》及歷代天文、曆志推算氣朔，又以己意創為八十七年約法，每月大小相間。

translations.literal: Minister Zhou Hongmo and others said: "Zhengji relies only on the Huangji Jingshi and successive astronomical and calendrical treatises to compute qi and new moon, and on his own intent invents an eighty-seven-year approximation, large and small months alternating.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhou Hongmo and others said: "Zhengji relies only on the Huangji Jingshi and successive astronomical treatises to compute qi and syzygy, then on his own authority devises an eighty-seven-year rule with alternating long and short months.

sentences.zh: 輕率狂妄，宜正其罪。

translations.literal: Rash and arrogant—his crime should be corrected."
translations.idiomatic: This is rash and presumptuous; he should be punished."

sentences.zh: 」遂下正己詔獄。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhengji was sent to imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhengji was thereupon imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 十九年，天文生張升上言改曆。

translations.literal: Year 19, astronomy student Zhang Sheng memorialized on calendar reform.
translations.idiomatic: Year 19: astronomy student Zhang Sheng memorialized for calendar reform.

sentences.zh: 欽天監謂祖制不可變，升說遂寢。

translations.literal: The Imperial Observatory said ancestral institutions cannot be changed; Sheng's proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Observatory held that ancestral institutions must not change; Zhang Sheng's proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，月食屢不應，日食亦舛。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi period, lunar eclipses repeatedly failed to match; solar eclipses also erred.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi, lunar eclipses repeatedly failed verification; solar eclipses were wrong as well.

sentences.zh: 正德十二、三年，連推日食起復，皆弗合。

translations.literal: Zhengde years 12–13, successive computations of solar eclipse first contact and recovery all failed to agree.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 12–13, successive predictions of solar-eclipse first contact and recovery all missed.

sentences.zh: 於是漏刻博士硃裕上言：「至元辛巳距今二百三十七年，歲久不能無差，若不量加損益，恐愈久愈舛。

translations.literal: Thereupon Clepsydra Doctor Zhu Yu memorialized: "From Yuan xinsi to now is two hundred thirty-seven years; long years cannot be without discrepancy—if one does not adjust by measured increase and decrease, fear ever longer, ever more wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Clepsydra Doctor Zhu Yu then memorialized: "From the Yuan epoch xinsi to the present is 237 years; error cannot but accumulate. Without measured adjustments, the drift will only worsen.

sentences.zh: 乞簡大臣總理其事，令本監官生半推古法，半推新法，兩相交驗，回回科推驗西域《九執曆法》。

translations.literal: Beg to select a senior minister to oversee the matter, order this observatory's officers and students half to compute by old method, half by new, mutually verify in comparison; the Islamic section to verify the Western Regions' Nine Executions calendar methods.
translations.idiomatic: Select a senior minister to direct the project; let half the observatory staff compute by the old method and half by the new, cross-checking the results; let the Islamic section verify the Western Regions' Nine Executions methods.

sentences.zh: 仍遣官至各省，候土圭以測節氣早晚。

translations.literal: Still dispatch officers to each province to await the earth gnomon and measure the earliness or lateness of the solar terms.
translations.idiomatic: Send officers to each province to set up gnomons and measure whether the solar terms arrive early or late.

sentences.zh: 往復參較，則交食可正，而七政可齊。

translations.literal: Going and returning in mutual comparison, then eclipses can be corrected and the seven luminaries aligned.
translations.idiomatic: With repeated comparison back and forth, eclipses can be corrected and the seven luminaries brought into agreement."

sentences.zh: 」部覆言：「裕及監官曆學未必皆精，今十月望月食，中官正周濂等所推算，與古法及裕所奏不同，請至期考驗。

translations.literal: The ministry replied: "Yu and observatory officers' calendrical learning are not necessarily all refined; now the tenth-month full-moon eclipse—Central Palace Corrector Zhou Lian and others' computation differs from the old method and Yu's memorial; request verification at the due date."
translations.idiomatic: The ministry replied: "Yu and the observatory staff are not all experts. For the coming tenth-month eclipse, central palace corrector Zhou Lian's figures differ from both the old method and Yu's proposal; verify on the day."

sentences.zh: 」既而濂等言： 「日躔歲退之差一分五十秒。

translations.literal: Soon Lian and others said: "The sun's annual retreat differs one minute fifty seconds.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhou Lian and others said: "The sun's annual precession amounts to one minute fifty seconds.

sentences.zh: 今正德乙亥，距至元辛巳二百三十五年，赤道歲差，當退天三度五十二分五十秒。

translations.literal: Now Zhengde yihai, distant from Yuan xinsi two hundred thirty-five years, equatorial precession should retreat heaven three degrees fifty-two minutes fifty seconds.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde yihai, 235 years from Yuan xinsi, equatorial precession should amount to 3°52′50″ of retreat.

sentences.zh: 不經改正，推步豈能有合。

translations.literal: Without correction, how can stepwise computation agree?
translations.idiomatic: Without correction, how can sequential computation ever agree?

sentences.zh: 臣參較德驗，得正德丙子歲前天正冬至氣應二十七日四百七十五分，命得辛卯日醜初初刻，日躔赤道箕宿六度四十七五十秒，黃道箕宿五度九十六分四十三秒為曆元。

translations.literal: Your servant compared and obtained verification: Zhengde bingzi year's prior celestial winter solstice qi responded day 27, 475 parts; fate obtained day xinmao, chou initial first quarter; sun at equator Lodge six degrees 47′50″, ecliptic Lodge five degrees 96′43″ as calendar origin.
translations.idiomatic: We compared and verified: for the winter solstice before Zhengde bingzi, qi fell on day 27 with 475 parts; syzygy fell on xinmao, chou initial first quarter; the sun stood at equatorial Lodge 6°47′50″ and ecliptic Lodge 5°96′43″ as the new epoch.

sentences.zh: 其氣閏轉交四應，並周天黃赤道，諸類立成，悉從歲差，隨時改正。

translations.literal: Its qi, intercalation, rotation, conjunction four responses, together with full-circle yellow and equator, all kinds of ready tables—altogether follow precession, corrected with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, intercalation, rotation, and conjunction tables, together with full-circle ecliptic and equatorial parameters, should all incorporate precession and be revised as times require.

sentences.zh: 望敕禮臣並監正董其事。

translations.literal: Hope to command ritual ministers together with the Director to oversee the matter."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that ritual officials and the observatory director jointly oversee the work."

sentences.zh: 」部奏：「古法未可輕變，請仍舊法。

translations.literal: The ministry memorialized: "The old method must not be lightly changed; request still the old method.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry replied: "The old method must not be changed lightly; continue the established system.

sentences.zh: 別選精通曆學者，同濂等以新法參驗，更為奏請。

translations.literal: Separately select those thoroughly versed in calendrics, together with Lian and others to verify by the new method, and again memorialize for decision."
translations.idiomatic: Separately select experts in calendrics to cross-check with Zhou Lian's new method and report again."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 十五年，禮部員外郎鄭善夫言：「日月交食，日食最為難測。

translations.literal: Year 15, Ministry of Rites Outer Section Officer Zheng Shanfu said: "Solar and lunar eclipses—solar eclipse is hardest to measure.
translations.idiomatic: Year 15: Ministry of Rites outer-section officer Zheng Shanfu said: "Of solar and lunar eclipses, the solar is hardest to predict.

sentences.zh: 蓋月食分數，但論距交遠近，別無四時加減，且月小暗虛大，八方所見皆同。

translations.literal: Lunar eclipse magnitude only discusses distance from conjunction, with no four-season additions or subtractions; moreover the moon is small, the shadow large, and the eight directions all see the same.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar eclipse magnitude depends only on distance from the node, without seasonal corrections; the moon is small and the earth's shadow large, so observers everywhere see essentially the same event.

sentences.zh: 若日為月所掩，則日大而月小，日上而月下，日遠而月近。

translations.literal: If the sun is obscured by the moon, then the sun is large and the moon small, the sun above and the moon below, the sun far and the moon near.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun is veiled by the moon, the sun is the larger body and the moon the smaller; the sun lies above and the moon below, the sun distant and the moon near.

sentences.zh: 日行有四時之異，月行有九道之分。

translations.literal: The sun's motion has the variations of the four seasons; the moon's motion has the divisions of the nine paths.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's course varies with the four seasons; the moon's course divides among the nine paths.

sentences.zh: 故南北殊觀，時刻亦異。

translations.literal: Hence north and south see differently, and the times also differ.
translations.idiomatic: North and south therefore behold different sights, and the hours differ as well.

sentences.zh: 必須據地定表，因時求合。

translations.literal: One must fix the gnomon according to place and seek accord according to time.
translations.idiomatic: One must set the shadow-table according to locality and seek agreement according to season.

sentences.zh: 如正德九年八月辛卯日食，曆官報食八分六十七秒，而閩、廣之地，遂至食既。

translations.literal: For example, on the xinmao day of the solar eclipse in the eighth month of Zhengde 9, the calendar officials reported an eclipse of eight parts and sixty-seven seconds, yet in Fujian and Guangdong it reached totality.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao solar eclipse of the eighth month, Zhengde 9, the calendar officers reported an obscuration of eight parts and sixty-seven seconds—yet in Fujian and Guangdong the eclipse ran to totality.

sentences.zh: 時刻分秒，安得而同？

translations.literal: How could the hours, minutes, and seconds be the same?
translations.idiomatic: How could the hours, minutes, and seconds be one and the same?

sentences.zh: 今宜按交食以更曆元，時刻分秒，必使奇零剖析詳盡。

translations.literal: Now we should adjust the calendar era according to eclipses, and the hours, minutes, and seconds must be parsed to the last odd fraction in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar origin should now be revised from eclipse data, and every hour, minute, and second parsed down to the last odd fraction.

sentences.zh: 不然，積以歲月，躔離朓朒，又不合矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise, as months and years accumulate, lodge motion and waxing and waning of the moon will again fail to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, as the years pile up, solar lodges, lunar distance, and the moon's waxing and waning will again fall out of accord.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No reply was made.
translations.idiomatic: " No reply was made.

sentences.zh: 十六年以南京戶科給事中樂頀、工部主事華湘通曆法，俱擢光祿少卿，管監事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Yue Bin, supervising secretary of the Nanjing Household Section, and Hua Xiang, principal secretary of the Ministry of Works, both versed in calendrical methods, were together promoted to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices to oversee the directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, Yue Bin of the Nanjing Household Section and Hua Xiang, principal secretary of the Ministry of Works—both skilled in calendrical computation—were alike promoted to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and charged with supervising the directorate.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，湘言：「古今善治曆者三家，漢《太初》以鐘律，唐《大衍》以蓍策，元《授時》以晷景為近。

translations.literal: Jiajing 2, Xiang said: "Among those skilled in governing the calendar in antiquity and today are three schools: the Han Taichu relied on pitch pipes and regulations; the Tang Dayan on yarrow stalks; the Yuan Season Granting on gnomon shadows comes nearest."
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 2: Xiang memorialized, "Of those who have truly mastered the calendar, antiquity and the present offer three exemplars: the Han Taichu rested on pitch-pipes and musical regulation; the Tang Dayan on yarrow-casting; the Yuan Season Granting, grounded in gnomon shadows, comes nearest the mark."

sentences.zh: 欲正曆而不登臺測景，皆空言臆見也。

translations.literal: To rectify the calendar without mounting the terrace to measure shadows is all empty talk and private opinion.
translations.idiomatic: "To set the calendar right without ascending the terrace to measure shadows is mere empty talk and private fancy."

sentences.zh: 望許臣暫朝參，督中官正周濂等，及冬至前詣觀象臺，晝夜推測，日記月書，至來年冬至，以驗二十四氣、分至合朔、日躔月離、黃赤二道、昏旦中星、七政四餘之度，視元辛巳所測，離合何如，差次錄聞。

translations.literal: He asked permission to attend court briefly, supervise the senior director Zhou Lian and others, and before the winter solstice proceed to the Observatory to observe by day and night, record sun and moon daily, until the winter solstice of the following year, to verify the twenty-four qi, equinoxes and solstices and new-moon conjunctions, solar lodge motion and lunar distance, the yellow and red paths, stars culminating at dusk and dawn, and the degrees of the seven rulers and four residuals—compare with what was measured at the xinsi year of the Yuan origin and record the discrepancies for report.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to attend court for a time, to oversee the senior director Zhou Lian and his colleagues, and before the winter solstice to take up station at the Observatory for day-and-night measurement, recording sun and moon day by day until the next winter solstice—there to test the twenty-four qi, the equinoxes and solstices and their new moons, solar lodge motion and lunar distance, the yellow and red paths, the stars culminating at dusk and dawn, and the degrees of the seven luminaries and four residuals; to compare these with the Yuan xinsi measurements, note agreement and divergence, and report each discrepancy in order.

sentences.zh: 更敕禮部延訪精通理數者徵赴京師，令詳定歲差，以成一代之制。

translations.literal: Further order the Ministry of Rites to seek out and invite those who excel in principle and numbers to the capital and have them fix the precession in detail to complete a regulation for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Further, let the Ministry of Rites seek out masters of principle and number and summon them to the capital to fix the annual difference in full, and so complete a calendar for the age.

sentences.zh: 」下禮部集議，而護謂曆不可改，與湘頗異。

translations.literal: " It was sent to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation; Yue Bin held the calendar must not be changed, differing considerably from Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial went to the Ministry of Rites for joint deliberation; Yue Bin held that the calendar must not be altered—a view at odds with Xiang's.

sentences.zh: 禮部言：「湘欲自行測候，不為無識。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said: "Xiang's wish to conduct observations himself is not without insight.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites replied, "Xiang's wish to conduct observations himself is not without insight.

sentences.zh: 請二臣各盡所見，窮極異同，以協天道。

translations.literal: Let the two ministers each present their views to the utmost, exhaust differences and agreements, to harmonize with Heaven's way."
translations.idiomatic: Let the two ministers each lay out their views to the limit, exhaust every point of agreement and difference, and so bring the work into harmony with Heaven's way."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 七年，欽天監奏：「閏十月朔，《回回曆》推日食二分四十七秒，《大統曆》推不食。

translations.literal: Seventh year, the Directorate of Astronomy memorialized: "On the first day of the intercalary tenth month, the Hui Calendar predicted a solar eclipse of two parts forty-seven seconds; the Grand Concordance predicted no eclipse."
translations.idiomatic: The seventh year: the Directorate of Astronomy reported, "On the new moon of the intercalary tenth month, the Hui Calendar computed a solar eclipse of two parts and forty-seven seconds; the Grand Concordance computed none."

sentences.zh: 」已而不食。

translations.literal: Thereafter no eclipse occurred.
translations.idiomatic: In the event, there was no eclipse.

sentences.zh: 十九年三月癸巳朔，臺官言日當食，已而不食。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year, third month guisi new moon: the observatory officials said the sun would be eclipsed, but it was not eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: The nineteenth year, on the guisi new moon of the third month, the observatory officers declared that the sun would be eclipsed; it was not.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，以為天眷，然實由推步之疏也。

translations.literal: The emperor rejoiced, taking it as Heaven's favor, but in truth it was due to the laxity of computation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejoiced, taking this as Heaven's favor; in truth it owed to the looseness of the computation.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年，掌監事順天府丞周相刊《大統曆法》，其曆原曆敘古今諸曆異同。

translations.literal: Longqing 3, Zhou Xiang, Shuntian prefectural vice prefect in charge of the directorate, published Methods of the Grand Concordance Calendar, with origins and treatise on how past and present calendars differ.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing 3: Zhou Xiang, Shuntian vice prefect in charge of the directorate, published the Methods of the Grand Concordance Calendar, with an origin-treatise setting forth how calendars past and present differ.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十二年十一有癸酉朔《大統曆》推日食九十二秒，《回回曆》推不食，已而《回回曆》驗。

translations.literal: Wanli 12, eleventh month guiyou new moon: the Grand Concordance predicted solar eclipse ninety-two seconds; the Hui Calendar predicted none; the Hui Calendar was verified.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 12, on the guiyou new moon of the eleventh month: the Grand Concordance predicted a solar eclipse of ninety-two seconds; the Hui Calendar predicted none—and the Hui Calendar was borne out.

sentences.zh: 禮科給事中侯先春因言：「邇年月食在酉而曰戌，月食將既而曰未九分，差舛甚矣。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Hou Xianchun thereupon said: "Recently lunar eclipses occurred in you hour but were announced as xu; an eclipse about to reach totality was called not yet nine-tenths—the errors are grave.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Hou Xianchun thereupon said, "Of late, lunar eclipses have fallen in the you hour yet been announced for xu; eclipses on the verge of totality have been called 'not yet nine-tenths'—the errors are grave.

sentences.zh: 《回回曆》科推算日月交食，五星淩犯，最為精密，何妨纂人《大統曆》中，以備考驗。

translations.literal: The Hui Calendar desk's calculations of solar and lunar eclipses and five-planet encroachments are the most precise; why not compile them into the Grand Concordance for reference and verification?"
translations.idiomatic: The Hui Calendar desk's reckonings of solar and lunar eclipses and the five planets' encroachments are the most exact; why not weave them into the Grand Concordance for reference and proof?"

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved.

sentences.zh: 二十年五月戌夜月食，監官推算差一日。

translations.literal: Wanli 20, fifth month, on the xu night there was a lunar eclipse; the observatory officials' calculation was off by one day.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 20, fifth month: on the xu night a lunar eclipse occurred, and the observatory officers' computation missed by a full day.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，鄭世子載堉進《聖壽萬年曆》、《律曆融通》二書。

translations.literal: Wanli 23, the Prince of Zheng, Zhu Zaiyu, presented two books: Sacred Longevity Perpetual Calendar and Concordance of Pitch Standards and Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 23: the Prince of Zheng, Zhu Zaiyu, presented two works—the Sacred Longevity Perpetual Calendar and the Concordance of Pitch Standards and Calendar.

sentences.zh: 疏略曰：「高皇帝革命時，元曆未久，氣朔未差，故不改作，但討論潤色而已。

translations.literal: Memorial summary said: "When the Founding Emperor revolutionized, the Yuan calendar had not been long in use and qi and new moon had not yet drifted, so he did not remake but only discussed and polished.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial in brief said, "When the Founding Emperor seized the mandate, the Yuan calendar had not long been in use; qi and new moon had not yet drifted—so he did not undertake a new creation but only revised and polished.

sentences.zh: 積年既久，氣朔漸差。

translations.literal: As years accumulated, qi and new moon gradually drifted.
translations.idiomatic: As the years piled up, qi and new moon gradually fell away.

sentences.zh: 《後漢志》言『三百年鬥曆改憲』。

translations.literal: The Later Han Treatise says 'every three hundred years the dipper calendar must revise the constitution.'
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise of Later Han says, 'Every three hundred years the Dipper Calendar must revise the constitution.'

sentences.zh: 今以萬曆為元，而九年辛巳歲適當『鬥曆改憲』之期，又協『乾元用九』之義，曆元正在是矣。

translations.literal: Now take Wanli as the origin, and the ninth year xinsi exactly falls in the period of 'dipper calendar revision,' also matching the meaning of 'Qianyuan employs nine'—the calendar origin is precisely here.
translations.idiomatic: Let Wanli serve as the origin: the xinsi year of the ninth reign-year falls exactly in the season when 'the Dipper Calendar revises the constitution,' and it accords with the principle that 'the Qian Origin employs nine'—the calendar origin lies here.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗取《大統》與《授時》二曆較之，考古則氣差三日，推今則時差九刻。

translations.literal: Your servant once compared the Grand Concordance and Season Granting calendars: examining antiquity, qi differ by three days; projecting to today, time differs by nine quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has compared the Grand Concordance and Season Granting calendars: tested against antiquity, the qi differ by three days; projected to the present, the time differs by nine quarters.

sentences.zh: 夫差雖九刻，處夜半之際，所差便隔一日。

translations.literal: Though the difference is only nine quarters, at the midnight junction it amounts to a full day.
translations.idiomatic: Though the discrepancy is but nine quarters, at the midnight turning it spans a full day.

sentences.zh: 節氣差天一日，則置閏差一月。

translations.literal: If solar terms are off by one day, intercalation is off by one month.
translations.idiomatic: If the solar terms slip one day, intercalation slips one month.

sentences.zh: 閏差一月，則時差一季。

translations.literal: If intercalation is off by one month, seasons are off by one quarter.
translations.idiomatic: If intercalation slips one month, the seasons slip one quarter.

sentences.zh: 時差一季，則歲差一年。

translations.literal: If seasons are off by one quarter, the year is off by one year.
translations.idiomatic: If the seasons slip one quarter, the year slips one year.

sentences.zh: 其失豈小小哉？

translations.literal: Can the error be trivial?
translations.idiomatic: Can such error be called small?

sentences.zh: 蓋因《授時》減分太峻，失之先天；

translations.literal: This is because the Season Granting reduced parts too sharply, erring to the prenatal side;
translations.idiomatic: This is because the Season Granting pared its fractions too sharply, erring on the side of prematurity;

sentences.zh: 《大統》不減，失之後天。

translations.literal: the Grand Concordance did not reduce, erring to the postnatal side.
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Concordance did not pare them, erring on the side of lateness.

sentences.zh: 因和會兩家，酌取中數，立為新率，編撰成書，大旨出於許衡，而與曆不同。

translations.literal: Harmonizing the two schools and taking the middle figure as the new ratio, compiling into a book—the gist derives from Xu Heng, yet differs from the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonizing the two schools and taking the middle number for a new ratio, I have compiled a book whose main lines follow Xu Heng, yet diverge from the received calendar.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘乃律曆本原，而舊曆罕言之。

translations.literal: The yellow bell is the root of pitch and calendar, yet old calendars rarely speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: The yellow bell is the root of pitch-pipes and calendar alike, yet the old calendars seldom treat it.

sentences.zh: 新法則以步律呂爻象為首。

translations.literal: The new method puts stepping pitch pipes and hexagram images first.
translations.idiomatic: The new method places the stepping of pitch-pipes and hexagram images foremost.

sentences.zh: 堯時冬至日躔宿次，何承天推在須、女十度左右，一行推在女、虛間，元人曆議亦云在女、虛之交。

translations.literal: At Yao's time the winter solstice sun's lodge; He Chengtian placed it about 10° in Xu and Nu; Yi Xing between Nu and Xu; Yuan calendar deliberations likewise at the junction of Nu and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: At Yao's era the winter-solstice solar lodge: He Chengtian placed it some ten degrees into Xu and Nu; Yi Xing between Nu and Xu; the Yuan calendar deliberations likewise at the juncture of Nu and Xu.

sentences.zh: 而《授時曆》考之，乃在牛宿二度。

translations.literal: But the Season Granting examining it placed it at 2° in Ox.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Season Granting, tested against the record, places it at two degrees in the Ox.

sentences.zh: 《大統曆》考之，乃在危宿一度。

translations.literal: The Grand Concordance examining it placed it at 1° in Rooftop.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Concordance, tested likewise, places it at one degree in the Rooftop.

sentences.zh: 相差二十六度，皆不與《堯典》合。

translations.literal: They differ by 26 degrees—all fail to accord with the Canon of Yao.
translations.idiomatic: They differ by twenty-six degrees—none accord with the Canon of Yao.

sentences.zh: 新法上考堯元年甲辰歲，夏至午中，日在柳宿十二度左右，冬至午中，日在女宿十度左右，心昴昏中，各去午正不逾半次，與承天、一行二家之說合。

translations.literal: The new method looking up to Yao year 1 jiachen: at summer solstice noon south the sun at about 12° Willow; winter solstice noon south about 10° Woman; Heart and Mao culminating at dusk, each no more than half a lodge from noon—matching He and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The new method, projected to Yao's first year jiachen: at summer solstice, sun south at noon near twelve degrees in the Willow; at winter solstice, sun south at noon near ten degrees in the Woman; Heart and Mao culminating at dusk—each no more than half a lodge from the noon meridian—agreeing with He Chengtian and Yi Xing.

sentences.zh: 此皆與舊曆不同大者，其餘詳見《曆議》。

translations.literal: These are the greatest points differing from the old calendar; the rest are detailed in Calendar Deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: These are the chief points on which it departs from the old calendar; the rest are set out in full in the Calendar Deliberations.

sentences.zh: 望敕大臣名儒參訂採用。」

translations.literal: Hope the throne will order great ministers and renowned scholars to collate and adopt."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the throne command great ministers and eminent scholars to collate and adopt it."

sentences.zh: 其法首曰步發斂。

translations.literal: Its method first is called Stepping Accumulation and Contraction.
translations.idiomatic: Its method opens with a section called Stepping Accumulation and Contraction.

sentences.zh: 取嘉靖甲寅歲為曆元，元紀四千五百六十，期實千四百六十一，節氣歲差一秒七十五忽，歲周氣策無定率，各隨歲差求而用之。

translations.literal: Take Jiajing jiayin as calendar origin, era count 4560, period solid 1461, solar term precession 1 second 75 huz, year circuit and qi policy without fixed ratio, each sought according to precession.
translations.idiomatic: It takes the jiayin year of Jiajing as calendar origin, with era count 4560, period solid 1461, and solar-term precession of one second and seventy-five huz; the year's circuit and qi policy have no fixed ratio, each being sought according to the annual difference.

sentences.zh: 律應即氣應五十五日六十刻八十九分，律總旬週六十日。

translations.literal: Pitch pipes respond—that is qi responds 55 days 60 quarters 89 parts; total pitch pipes equal ten-day cycle 60 days.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch-pipes' response is the qi's response: fifty-five days, sixty quarters, and eighty-nine parts; the pitch-pipes' total cycle equals the ten-day week of sixty days.

sentences.zh: 次曰步朔閏。

translations.literal: Next Stepping New Moon and Intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: Next: Stepping New Moon and Intercalation.

sentences.zh: 朔望弦策與《授時》同，閏應十九日三十六刻十九分。

translations.literal: New, full, and quarter moon policies same as Season Granting; intercalation response 19 days 36 quarters 19 parts.
translations.idiomatic: The policies for new moon, full moon, and quarters match the Season Granting; the intercalation response is nineteen days, thirty-six quarters, and nineteen parts.

sentences.zh: 次曰步日躔。

translations.literal: Next Stepping Solar Lodge Motion.
translations.idiomatic: Next: Stepping Solar Lodge Motion.

sentences.zh: 日平行一度，躔周即天週三百六十五度二十五分，躔中半之，象策又半之，辰策十二分躔周之一。

translations.literal: Sun daily parallel 1 degree, lodge circuit equals celestial circuit 365.25 degrees, lodge center half thereof, image policy half again, chen policy one-twelfth of lodge circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's daily parallel is one degree; the lodge circuit is the celestial circuit of 365.25 degrees; the lodge center is half of this, the image policy half again, and the chen policy one-twelfth of the lodge circuit.

sentences.zh: 黃、赤道歲差，盈初縮末限，縮初盈末限，俱與《授時》同，周應二百三十八度二十二分三十九秒。

translations.literal: Yellow and red paths annual difference: fullness at start contraction at end limit, contraction at start fullness at end limit—all same as Season Granting, cycle response 238° 22' 39".
translations.idiomatic: For the yellow and red paths' annual difference—the fullness-at-start, contraction-at-end limit and the contraction-at-start, fullness-at-end limit—all match the Season Granting; the cycle response is 238 degrees, 22 minutes, and 39 seconds.

sentences.zh: 按《授時》求日度法，以周應加積度，命起虛七，其周應為自虛七度至箕寸十度之數。

translations.literal: Per Season Granting method for solar degree: add accumulated degrees to cycle response, command from Void 7; its cycle response is the number from Void 7 to Winnowing Basket 10 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: By the Season Granting's method for solar degree: add the cycle response to accumulated degrees and command from seven degrees in the Void; its cycle response is the count from seven degrees in the Void to ten degrees in the Winnowing Basket.

sentences.zh: 《萬年曆法》以周應減積度，命起角初，其周應為箕十度至角初度之數，當為二百八十六度四十五分。

translations.literal: Perpetual Calendar method subtracts cycle response from accumulated degrees, command from Horn start; its cycle response is Winnowing Basket 10 to Horn start, should be 286° 45'.
translations.idiomatic: The Perpetual Calendar method subtracts the cycle response from accumulated degrees and commands from the start of the Horn; its cycle response is the count from ten degrees in the Winnowing Basket to the start of the Horn—which should be 286 degrees and 45 minutes.

sentences.zh: 今數不合，似誤。

translations.literal: Now the numbers do not agree—seeming error.
translations.idiomatic: The figures now given do not agree—an apparent error.

sentences.zh: 次曰步晷漏。

translations.literal: Next Stepping Gnomon and Clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: Next: Stepping Gnomon and Clepsydra.

sentences.zh: 北極出地度分，冬、夏至中晷恆數，並二至晝夜長短刻數，俱以京師為準。

translations.literal: North pole altitude degrees, winter/summer solstice noon gnomon constants, and the day-night length in quarters at both solstices—all based on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The north pole's altitude in degrees, the constant noon gnomon lengths at winter and summer solstice, and the day-and-night lengths in quarters at both solstices—all take the capital as standard.

sentences.zh: 參以嶽臺，以見隨處裡差之數。

translations.literal: Compare with the Yue Terrace to see the li-difference numbers for each place.
translations.idiomatic: These are checked against the Yue Terrace to show the li-difference for each locality.

sentences.zh: 次曰步月離。

translations.literal: Next Stepping Lunar Distance.
translations.idiomatic: Next: Stepping Lunar Distance.

sentences.zh: 月平行、轉周、轉中，與《授時》同。

translations.literal: Moon daily parallel, rotation circuit, rotation center—same as Season Granting.
translations.idiomatic: The moon's daily parallel, rotation circuit, and rotation center match the Season Granting.

sentences.zh: 離周即遲疾限三百三十六限十六分六十秒，離中半之，離象又半之。

translations.literal: Distance circuit is the slow-fast limit 336 limits 16 parts 60 seconds; distance center halves it, distance image halves again.
translations.idiomatic: The distance circuit is the slow-and-fast limit of 336 limits, 16 parts, and 60 seconds; the distance center halves it, and the distance image halves again.

sentences.zh: 轉差一日九十刻六十分。

translations.literal: Rotation difference one day 90 quarters 60 parts.
translations.idiomatic: The rotation difference is one day, ninety quarters, and sixty parts.

sentences.zh: 轉應七日五十刻三十四分。

translations.literal: Rotation response seven days 50 quarters 34 parts.
translations.idiomatic: The rotation response is seven days, fifty quarters, and thirty-four parts.

sentences.zh: 次曰步交道。

translations.literal: Next Stepping Crossing Paths.
translations.idiomatic: Next: Stepping Crossing Paths.

sentences.zh: 正交、中交與《授時》同。

translations.literal: True cross and central cross same as Season Granting.
translations.idiomatic: The true cross and central cross match the Season Granting.

sentences.zh: 距交十四度六十六分六十六秒。

translations.literal: Distance from crossing 14° 66' 66".
translations.idiomatic: The distance from the crossing is 14 degrees, 66 minutes, and 66 seconds.

sentences.zh: 交周、交中、交差，與《授時》同。

translations.literal: Crossing circuit, crossing center, crossing difference—same as Season Granting.
translations.idiomatic: The crossing circuit, crossing center, and crossing difference match the Season Granting.

sentences.zh: 交應二十日四十七刻三十四分。

translations.literal: Crossing response twenty days 47 quarters 34 parts.
translations.idiomatic: The crossing response is twenty days, forty-seven quarters, and thirty-four parts.

sentences.zh: 次曰步交食。

translations.literal: Next Stepping Eclipse Crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Next: Stepping Eclipse Crossing.

sentences.zh: 日食交外限六度，定法六十一，交內限八度定法八十一。

translations.literal: Solar eclipse outside-cross limit six degrees, fixed method sixty-one; inside-cross limit eight degrees fixed method eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: For solar eclipse: outside the crossing, the limit is six degrees and the fixed method sixty-one; inside the crossing, the limit is eight degrees and the fixed method eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 月食限定法與《授時》同。

translations.literal: Lunar eclipse limits and fixed methods same as Season Granting.
translations.idiomatic: For lunar eclipse, the limits and fixed methods match the Season Granting.

sentences.zh: 次曰步五緯。

translations.literal: Next Stepping Five Luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: Next: Stepping the Five Luminaries.

sentences.zh: 合應：土星二百六十二日三千二十六分，木星三百一十一千八百三十七分，火星三百四十三日五千一百七十六分，金星二百三十八千三百四十七分，水星九十一日七千六百二十八分。

translations.literal: Conjunction responses: Saturn 262 days 3026 parts, Jupiter 311 days 1837 parts, Mars 343 days 5176 parts, Venus 238 days 8347 parts, Mercury 91 days 7628 parts.
translations.idiomatic: Conjunction responses: Saturn 262 days and 3026 parts; Jupiter 311 days and 1837 parts; Mars 343 days and 5176 parts; Venus 238 days and 8347 parts; Mercury 91 days and 7628 parts.

sentences.zh: 曆應：土星八千六百四日五千三百三十八分，木星四千一十八日六千七十三分，火星三百一十四日四十九分，金星六十日一千九百七十五分，水星二百五十三日七千四百九十七分。

translations.literal: Calendar responses: Saturn 8604 days 5338 parts, Jupiter 4018 days 6073 parts, Mars 314 days 49 parts, Venus 60 days 1975 parts, Mercury 253 days 7497 parts.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar responses: Saturn 8604 days and 5338 parts; Jupiter 4018 days and 6073 parts; Mars 314 days and 49 parts; Venus 60 days and 1975 parts; Mercury 253 days and 7497 parts.

sentences.zh: 周率、度率及晨夕伏見度，俱與《授時》同。

translations.literal: Cycle rates, degree rates, and morning/evening visibility degrees—all same as Season Granting.
translations.idiomatic: Cycle rates, degree rates, and the degrees of morning and evening visibility—all match the Season Granting.

sentences.zh: 其議歲餘也，曰：「陰陽消長之理，以漸而積，未有不從秒起。

translations.literal: Its deliberation on year remainder: "The principle of yin-yang waxing and waning accumulates by gradual steps—none that does not begin from seconds.
translations.idiomatic: Its deliberation on the year remainder runs: "The principle of yin and yang's waxing and waning accumulates by fine steps—none that does not begin from seconds.

sentences.zh: 《授時》考古，於百年之際頓加一分，於理未安。

translations.literal: The Season Granting in examining antiquity suddenly added one part at the century mark—logically unsound.
translations.idiomatic: The Season Granting, in examining antiquity, suddenly adds one part at the century mark—sound in form, unsound in reason.

sentences.zh: 假如魯隱公三年酉歲，下距至元辛巳二千年，以《授時》本法算之，於歲實當加二十分，得庚午日六刻，為其年天正冬至。

translations.literal: Suppose Duke Yin year 3 you year, down 2000 years to Yuan xinsi; by the Season Granting original method, to the year solid should add 20 parts, obtaining gengwu day six quarters as that year's celestial winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose the third year of Duke Yin, a you year, two thousand years down to the Yuan xinsi: by the Season Granting's original method the year solid should gain twenty parts, yielding the gengwu day at six quarters as that year's celestial winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 次年壬戌歲，下距至元辛巳一千九百九十年，本法當加十九分，得乙亥日五十刻四十四分，為其年天正冬至。

translations.literal: Next year renxu, down 1990 years to xinsi, original method should add 19 parts, obtaining yihai day 50 quarters 44 parts as celestial winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, renxu, nineteen hundred and ninety years down to xinsi: the original method should add nineteen parts, yielding the yihai day at fifty quarters and forty-four parts as the celestial winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 兩冬至相減，得相距三百六十五日四十四刻四十四分，則是歲餘九分日之四，非四分日之一也。

translations.literal: Subtracting the two winter solstices, the interval is 365 days 44 quarters 44 parts—so the year remainder is nine-fourths of a day, not one-fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Subtracting the two winter solstices leaves an interval of 365 days, forty-four quarters, and forty-four parts—so the year remainder is nine-fourths of a day, not one-fourth.

sentences.zh: 曆法之廖，莫甚於此。

translations.literal: No calendar flaw is worse than this.
translations.idiomatic: No flaw in calendar reckoning runs deeper than this.

sentences.zh: 新法酌量，設若每年增損二秒，推而上之，則失昭公己丑；

translations.literal: The new method estimates: if each year adds/subtracts two seconds, projecting upward, Duke Zhao jichou is missed;
translations.idiomatic: The new method weighs the matter thus: if each year gains or loses two seconds, projecting upward misses Duke Zhao's jichou;

sentences.zh: 增損一秒至一秒半，則失僖公辛亥。

translations.literal: add/subtract one to one-and-a-half seconds, then Duke Xi xinhai is missed.
translations.idiomatic: if it gains or loses one to one-and-a-half seconds, Duke Xi's xinhai is missed.

sentences.zh: 今約取中數，其法置定距自相乘，七因八歸，所得百，約之為分，得一秒七十五忽，則辛亥、己丑皆得矣。」

translations.literal: Now taking the middle figure, the method sets fixed interval self-multiplied, seven times eight returns, obtaining 100, reduced to parts yields one second 75 huz—then both xinhai and jichou are obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Taking the middle figure, the method sets the fixed interval multiplied by itself, applies the seven-eights reduction, obtains one hundred, and reduces to parts to yield one second and seventy-five huz—then both xinhai and jichou are secured."

sentences.zh: 其議日躔也，曰：「古曆見於《六經》，灼然可考者莫如日躔及中星。

translations.literal: Its deliberation on solar lodge motion: "Ancient calendars seen in the Six Classics that can clearly be verified are none more than solar lodge motion and culminating stars.
translations.idiomatic: Its deliberation on solar lodge motion says, "Among ancient calendars attested in the Six Classics, none are more clearly verifiable than solar lodge motion and culminating stars.

sentences.zh: 而推步家鮮有達者，蓋由不知夏時、周正之異也。

translations.literal: Yet few among computists have mastered it—mostly because they do not know the difference between Xia months and Zhou correct months.
translations.idiomatic: Yet few computists have mastered them—chiefly because they do not grasp the difference between Xia months and Zhou correct months.

sentences.zh: 大抵夏曆以節氣為主，周曆以中氣為主。

translations.literal: Broadly, the Xia calendar takes solar terms as primary; the Zhou takes major qi as primary.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, the Xia calendar takes solar terms as primary; the Zhou takes the major qi as primary.

sentences.zh: 何承天以正月甲子夜半合朔雨水為上元，進乖夏朔，退非周正。

translations.literal: He Chengtian took first month jiazi midnight conjunction at Rain Water as upper origin, advancing astray from Xia new moon, retreating short of Zhou correctness.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian took the first month, jiazi, midnight conjunction at Rain Water as upper origin—too far forward for the Xia new moon, too far back for Zhou correctness.

sentences.zh: 故近代推《月令》、《小正》者、皆不與古合。

translations.literal: Hence recent times' reconstructions of Monthly Ordinance and Lesser Correct Month all fail to agree with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the recent reconstructions of the Monthly Ordinance and the Lesser Correct Month all fail to agree with antiquity.

sentences.zh: 嘗以新法歲差，上考《堯典》中星，則所謂四仲月，蓋自節氣之始至於中氣之終，三十日內之中星耳後世執者於二分二至，是亦誤矣。」

translations.literal: Once with the new method's precession, looking up to Yao Canon culminating stars, the so-called four mid-season months are merely the stars culminating at midnight within thirty days from the start of a solar term to the end of a major qi; later generations who rigidly apply the two equinoxes and two solstices are likewise mistaken."
translations.idiomatic: When I apply the new method's precession and look up to the culminating stars of the Canon of Yao, the so-called four mid-season months are simply the stars culminating at midnight within the thirty days from a solar term's opening to a major qi's close; later ages that fix rigidly on the two equinoxes and two solstices err likewise."

sentences.zh: 其議侯極也，曰：「自漢至齊、梁，皆謂紐星即不動處。

translations.literal: Its deliberation on polar culminating stars: "From Han through Qi and Liang all held the pivot star is the fixed point.
translations.idiomatic: Its deliberation on polar culminating stars says, "From Han through Qi and Liang, all held that the pivot star was the fixed point.

sentences.zh: 惟祖恆之測知紐星去極一度有餘。

translations.literal: Only Zu Chongzhi's measurements knew the pivot star is more than one degree from the pole.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zu Chongzhi's measurements showed the pivot star standing more than one degree from the pole.

sentences.zh: 自唐至宋，又測紐星去極三度有餘。

translations.literal: From Tang through Song, measurements again found the pivot star more than three degrees from the pole.
translations.idiomatic: From Tang through Song, measurement again found the pivot star more than three degrees from the pole.

sentences.zh: 《元志》從三度，蓋未有說也。

translations.literal: The Yuan History follows three degrees—probably there has been no explanation.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan History adopts a figure of three degrees, for which there is likely no adequate explanation.

sentences.zh: 新法不測紐星，以日景驗之，於正方案上，周天度內權指一度為北極，自此度右旋，數至六十七度四十一分，為夏至日躔所在。

translations.literal: The new method does not measure the pivot star; it verifies by the sun's shadow. On the upright azimuth plate, within the degrees of the full circuit one provisionally marks one degree as the pole; from that degree, counting rightward to 67 degrees 41 minutes, is where the sun stands at the summer solstice.
translations.idiomatic: The new method does not measure the pivot star directly; it checks by the sun's shadow. On the upright azimuth plate, within the full circuit of degrees one provisionally designates one degree as the pole, then counts rightward to 67°41′ for the sun's position at the summer solstice.

sentences.zh: 復至一百一十五度二十一分，為冬至日躔所在。

translations.literal: Again to 115 degrees 21 minutes is where the sun stands at the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Counting onward to 115°21′ gives the sun's position at the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 左旋，數亦如之。

translations.literal: Leftward rotation—the count is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Rotating leftward, one counts in the same way.

sentences.zh: 四處並中心五處，各識一針。

translations.literal: At the four places and the center—five places in all—each is marked with a needle.
translations.idiomatic: At the four corners and the center—five points in all—each is marked with a needle.

sentences.zh: 於二至日午中，將案直立向南取景，使三針景合，然後縣繩界取中綿，又取方十字界之，視橫界上距極出地度分也，即極出地度分也。」

translations.literal: On the two solstice days at noon, set the plate upright facing south to catch the image; make the three needle-shadows meet, then hang cords to take the center thread, also lay a square cross to bound it; observe on the horizontal line the degrees and minutes of polar altitude above the horizon—that is the polar altitude.
translations.idiomatic: On the solstice days at noon, stand the plate upright facing south to catch the shadow, align the three needle-shadows, then suspend cords to find the center line and mark a square cross; read on the horizontal line the degrees and minutes of polar altitude above the horizon—that is the polar altitude.

sentences.zh: 其議晷景也，曰：「何承天立表測景，始知自漢以來，冬至皆後天三日。

translations.literal: His discussion of gnomon shadows says: "He Chengtian erected a table to measure shadows and first learned that since Han times the winter solstice had always lagged Heaven by three days.
translations.idiomatic: In his discussion of gnomon shadows he says: "He Chengtian set up a gnomon to measure shadows and first discovered that since Han times the winter solstice had consistently fallen three days behind Heaven.

sentences.zh: 然則推步晷景，乃治曆之耍也。

translations.literal: Thus computing and stepping gnomon shadows is the crux of making calendars.
translations.idiomatic: Computing and advancing gnomon shadows is therefore the essential task of calendar-making.

sentences.zh: 《授時曆》亦憑晷景為本，而《曆經》不載推步晷景之術，是為缺略，今用北極出地度數，兼弧矢二術以求之，庶盡其原。

translations.literal: The Shoushi calendar also took gnomon shadows as its foundation, but the Calendar Classic does not record the method of computing gnomon shadows—this is a gap; now using polar altitude above the horizon together with arc and versed-sine methods to seek it, one may exhaust its origin.
translations.idiomatic: The Shoushi calendar likewise rests on gnomon shadows, yet the Calendar Classic does not record how to compute them—a serious omission. The new method uses polar altitude together with arc and versed-sine techniques to derive them fully.

sentences.zh: 又隨地形高下，立差以盡變，前此所未有也。

translations.literal: Also according to terrain high and low, establishing corrections to exhaust variation—something never done before.
translations.idiomatic: It also sets corrections according to local elevation, accounting for every variation—something no earlier method had done.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「《授時曆》議據《前漢志》魯獻公十五年戊寅歲正月甲寅朔旦冬至，引用為首。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The Shoushi calendar's discussion relies on the Former Han Treatise: Duke Xian of Lu's fifteenth year, year wuyin, first month jiayin new moon at dawn winter solstice, citing this as the head.
translations.idiomatic: " He also writes: "The Shoushi calendar's discussion takes as its starting point the Former Han Treatise entry for Duke Xian of Lu's fifteenth year (wuyin): new moon on jiayin at dawn on the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 夫獻公十五年下距隱西元年己未，歲百六十一年，其非春秋時明矣。

translations.literal: From Duke Xian's fifteenth year down to the first year of Duke Yin of the western line, year jiwei—it is 161 years; that it is not the Spring and Autumn period is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xian's fifteenth year is 161 years before the first year of Duke Yin (jiwei) in the western chronology—clearly not the Spring and Autumn era at all.

sentences.zh: 而《元志》乃云『自春秋獻公以來』，又云『昭公冬至，乃日度失行之驗』，誤矣。

translations.literal: Yet the Yuan History says 'since Duke Xian of Spring and Autumn times' and also says 'Duke Zhao's winter solstice was proof of the sun's degree having lost its course'—erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Yuan History says 'since Duke Xian of the Spring and Autumn period' and also that 'Duke Zhao's winter solstice proves the sun's motion had gone astray'—both are mistaken.

sentences.zh: 夫獻公甲寅冬至，別無所據，惟劉歆《三統曆》言之。

translations.literal: Duke Xian's jiayin winter solstice has no other evidence—only Liu Xin in the Santong calendar states it.
translations.idiomatic: The jiayin winter solstice of Duke Xian's year rests on no other authority than Liu Xin's Santong calendar.

sentences.zh: 豈左傳不足信，而歆乃可信乎？

translations.literal: Is the Zuo Commentary insufficiently trustworthy while Xin is trustworthy?
translations.idiomatic: Is the Zuo Commentary untrustworthy while Liu Xin alone is to be believed?

sentences.zh: 太初元年冬至在辛酉，歆乃以為甲子，差天三日，尚不能知，而能逆知上下數百年乎？

translations.literal: In the Taichu era year one the winter solstice was in xinyou; Xin took it to be jiazi, off Heaven by three days—if he could not know that, how could he know backwards and forwards several hundred years?
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Taichu era the winter solstice fell in xinyou, yet Liu Xin placed it in jiazi—three days off Heaven. If he could not get that right, how could he know events centuries before or after?

sentences.zh: 故凡春秋前後千載之間，氣朔交食，《長曆》、《大衍》所推近是，劉歆、班固所說全非也。

translations.literal: Therefore for the thousand years before and after Spring and Autumn, solar terms, new moons, and eclipses—the Chang calendar and Dayan pushings are close to right; Liu Xin and Ban Gu's statements are entirely wrong.
translations.idiomatic: For the millennium surrounding the Spring and Autumn period, solar terms, new moons, and eclipses computed in the Chang calendar and Dayan system are roughly correct; what Liu Xin and Ban Gu asserted is wholly wrong.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「《大衍曆》議謂宋元嘉十三年一月甲戌，景長為日度變行，《授時曆》議亦云，竊以為過矣。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The Dayan calendar discussion holds that in Yuanjia reign year thirteen, month one day jiaxu, the long shadow was proof of the sun's degree changing course; the Shoushi calendar discussion says the same—I hold this excessive.
translations.idiomatic: " He also writes: "The Dayan calendar's discussion claims that in Yuanjia 13, on the first month, day jiaxu, an unusually long shadow proved the sun's motion had shifted; the Shoushi discussion repeats this—I believe both go too far.

sentences.zh: 苟日度失行，當如歲差，漸漸而移。

translations.literal: If the sun's degree lost its course, it should be like precession, moving gradually.
translations.idiomatic: If the sun's motion truly went astray, it ought to shift gradually, as with precession.

sentences.zh: 今歲既已不合，來歲豈能復合耶？

translations.literal: If this year already does not fit, how can next year fit again?
translations.idiomatic: If it fails to match this year, how could it match again the next?

sentences.zh: 蓋前人所測，或未密耳。

translations.literal: Probably the ancients' measurements were not yet exact.
translations.idiomatic: Presumably the earlier measurements were simply not precise enough.

sentences.zh: 夫冬至之景一丈有餘，表高晷長，則景虛而淡，或設望筒、副表、景符之類以求實景。

translations.literal: At winter solstice the shadow is more than one zhang; when the table is high the gnomon long, the shadow is faint and pale—or one sets sighting tubes, auxiliary tables, shadow markers and the like to seek the true shadow.
translations.idiomatic: At winter solstice the shadow exceeds one zhang; with a tall gnomon the shadow grows long, faint, and diffuse, so observers use sighting tubes, auxiliary tables, shadow markers, and similar devices to capture the true shadow.

sentences.zh: 然望筒或一低昂，副表、景符或一前卻，所據之表或稍有傾欹，圭面或稍有斜側，二至前後數日之景，進退只在毫釐之間，耍亦難辨。

translations.literal: Yet the sighting tube may tilt slightly high or low; auxiliary tables and shadow markers may shift slightly forward or back; the table relied on may lean slightly; the jade face may tilt slightly. Shadows several days before and after the solstices advance and retreat only within hairs and millimeters—the crux is hard to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a sighting tube may sit slightly high or low; auxiliary tables and markers may be placed slightly forward or back; the gnomon itself may lean; the measuring surface may tilt. Shadows a few days before and after the solstices differ by only hairs and millimeters—the decisive point is nearly impossible to tell apart.

sentences.zh: 況委託之人，未智當否。

translations.literal: Moreover, those commissioned may not know whether they are correct.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the officials entrusted with the work may not even know whether their readings are right.

sentences.zh: 九服之遠，既非自摯，所報晷景，寧足信乎？」

translations.literal: As far as the nine domains—since one did not measure in person, can reported gnomon shadows be fully trusted?
translations.idiomatic: Across the nine domains, since no one measured in person everywhere, how can reported gnomon shadows be fully trusted?

sentences.zh: 其議漏刻也，曰：「日月帶食出入，五星晨昏伏見，曆家設法悉因晷漏為準。

translations.literal: His discussion of clepsydra gradations says: "When sun and moon are near eclipse at rising and setting, when the five planets appear and hide at dawn and dusk and at culmination—calendar makers' methods all take gnomon and clepsydra as standard.
translations.idiomatic: In his discussion of clepsydra gradations he says: "Whether the sun and moon rise or set near an eclipse, or the five planets appear, hide, or culminate at dawn or dusk—calendar-makers always base their methods on gnomon shadows and water-clock readings.

sentences.zh: 而晷漏則隨地勢南北，辰極高下為異焉。

translations.literal: Yet gnomon and clepsydra differ according to terrain north and south and the height of the polar pivot.
translations.idiomatic: Yet gnomon and clepsydra readings vary with latitude and with the altitude of the celestial pole.

sentences.zh: 元人都燕，其《授時曆》七曜出沒之早晏，四時晝夜之永短，皆準大都晷漏。

translations.literal: The Yuan capital was Yan; its Shoushi calendar's early and late rising and setting of the seven luminaries, and length of day and night through the four seasons—all followed the Dadu gnomon and clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan capital was at Yan; the Shoushi calendar's times of rising and setting for the seven luminaries and the lengths of day and night through the four seasons all followed the gnomon and clepsydra of Dadu.

sentences.zh: 國初都金陵，《大統曆》晷漏改徒南京，冬夏至相差三刻有奇。
