translations.literal: At the dynasty's founding the capital was Jinling; the Datong calendar changed the gnomon and clepsydra to Nanjing—winter and summer solstice differ by more than three ke.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was founded the capital was Jinling; the Datong calendar shifted the gnomon and clepsydra standard to Nanjing, so winter and summer solstice times differ by more than three ke.

sentences.zh: 今推交食分秒，南北東西等差及五星定伏定見，皆因元人舊法，而獨改其漏刻，是以互神舛誤也。

translations.literal: Now in computing eclipse minutes, north-south and east-west equal corrections, and fixed culmination and appearance of the five planets—all follow Yuan people's old methods; yet alone the clepsydra gradation was changed—hence conflicting errors.
translations.idiomatic: Today eclipse minutes, north-south and east-west corrections, and the fixed times of planetary appearance and hiding all still follow Yuan methods—yet the clepsydra gradations alone were changed, producing inconsistent errors throughout.

sentences.zh: 故新法晷漏，照依元舊。」

translations.literal: Therefore the new method's gnomon and clepsydra follow the Yuan original.
translations.idiomatic: The new method therefore restores gnomon and clepsydra standards to the Yuan originals.

sentences.zh: 其議日食也，曰：「日道與月道相交處有二，若正會於交，則食既，若但在交前後相近者，則食而不既。

translations.literal: His discussion of solar eclipses says: "Where the sun's path and moon's path meet there are two [limits]. If they meet exactly at the crossing, the eclipse is total; if only near the crossing before or after, there is eclipse but not totality.
translations.idiomatic: In his discussion of solar eclipses he says: "The sun's path and the moon's path cross at two nodes. If they meet exactly at the node, the eclipse is total; if they only approach the node, there is a partial eclipse but not totality.

sentences.zh: 此天之交限也。

translations.literal: This is heaven's eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: This is the celestial eclipse limit.

sentences.zh: 又有人之交限，假令中國食既，戴日之下，所虧才半，化外之地，則交而不食。

translations.literal: There is also man's eclipse limit—suppose within China the eclipse is total; under the sun-crowning region only half is obscured; in outer lands there is conjunction but no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: There is also a terrestrial eclipse limit: suppose the eclipse is total in China, yet beneath the subsolar point only half the disk is obscured, while beyond the frontier the conjunction occurs but no eclipse is seen.

sentences.zh: 易地反觀，亦如之。

translations.literal: Changing place and looking back is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Change vantage point and the same principle applies in reverse.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 日如大赤丸，月如小黑丸，共縣一綿，日上而下，即其下正望之，黑丸必掩赤丸，似食之既；

translations.literal: The sun is like a great red ball, the moon like a small black ball, both hung on one cord. Looking straight up from below when the sun is above, the black ball must cover the red ball, like a total eclipse;
translations.idiomatic: Imagine the sun as a large red sphere and the moon as a small black sphere on the same string. Viewed straight up from below when the sun is overhead, the black sphere fully covers the red one, like a total eclipse;

sentences.zh: 及旁觀有遠近之差，則食數有多寡矣。

translations.literal: when viewing from the side with distance difference, eclipse amount has more and less.
translations.idiomatic: but viewed obliquely from a distance, the eclipsed fraction varies.

sentences.zh: 春分已後，日行赤道北畔，交外偏多，交內偏少。

translations.literal: After the spring equinox the sun travels the north side of the equator—outside the node more, inside less.
translations.idiomatic: After the spring equinox the sun runs along the northern side of the equator: eclipses outside the node predominate, inside the node are fewer.

sentences.zh: 秋分已後，日行赤道南畔，交外偏少，交內偏多。

translations.literal: After the autumn equinox the sun travels the south side—outside less, inside more.
translations.idiomatic: After the autumn equinox it runs along the southern side: outside the node are fewer, inside more.

sentences.zh: 是故有南北差。

translations.literal: Hence there is a north-south correction.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the north-south correction arises.

sentences.zh: 冬至已後，日行黃道東畔，午前偏多，午後偏少。

translations.literal: After winter solstice the sun travels the east side of the ecliptic—before noon more, after noon less.
translations.idiomatic: After the winter solstice the sun travels the eastern side of the ecliptic: eclipses before noon are more frequent, after noon fewer.

sentences.zh: 夏至已後，日行黃道西畔，午前偏少，午後偏多。

translations.literal: After summer solstice the sun travels the west side—before noon less, after noon more.
translations.idiomatic: After the summer solstice it travels the western side: before noon fewer, after noon more.

sentences.zh: 是故有東西差。

translations.literal: Hence there is an east-west correction.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the east-west correction arises.

sentences.zh: 日中仰視則高，旦暮平視則低。

translations.literal: Looking up at noon it is high; looking level at dawn and dusk it is low.
translations.idiomatic: At noon one looks upward and the path is high; at dawn and dusk one looks level and it appears low.

sentences.zh: 是有距午差。

translations.literal: Hence there is a distance-from-noon correction.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the correction for distance from noon.

sentences.zh: 食於中前見早，食於中後見遲。

translations.literal: Eclipse before noon is seen early; after noon seen late.
translations.idiomatic: An eclipse before noon is seen early; after noon, late.

sentences.zh: 是故有時差，凡此諸差，唯日有之，月則無也。

translations.literal: Hence there is a time correction—all these corrections the sun alone has; the moon does not.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the time correction. All these corrections apply only to the sun; the moon has none.

sentences.zh: 故推交食，惟日頗難。

translations.literal: Thus computing eclipses—only the sun is quite difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Computing eclipses is therefore especially difficult for the sun.

sentences.zh: 欲推九服之變，必各據其處，考晷景之短長，揆辰極之高下，庶幾得之。

translations.literal: To compute variation across the nine domains one must take each place separately, examine gnomon shadow length, gauge polar height—then perhaps obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: To calculate variations across the nine domains, one must work from each locality, measuring gnomon shadows and determining polar altitude—only then can one approximate the truth.

sentences.zh: 《曆經》推定之數，徒以燕都所見者言之耳。

translations.literal: The numbers fixed in the Calendar Classic speak only of what was seen at the Yan capital.
translations.idiomatic: The fixed figures in the Calendar Classic describe only what was observed at the Yan capital.

sentences.zh: 舊云：『月行內道，食多有驗。

translations.literal: Old saying: 'When the moon travels the inner path, eclipses mostly verify.
translations.idiomatic: An old rule says: "When the moon travels the inner path, eclipses usually prove accurate.

sentences.zh: 月行外道，食多不驗。

translations.literal: When the moon travels the outer path, eclipses mostly do not verify.
translations.idiomatic: When it travels the outer path, eclipses usually fail to match."

sentences.zh: 』又云：『天之交限，雖系內道，若在人之交限之外，類同外道，日亦不食。

translations.literal: Also old saying: 'Heaven's eclipse limit, though tied to the inner path—if outside man's eclipse limit, like the outer path, the sun also does not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Another old rule says: "Even when the celestial limit lies on the inner path, if it falls outside the terrestrial limit—like the outer path—the sun may not eclipse at all."

sentences.zh: 』此說似矣，而未盡也。

translations.literal: This saying seems right but is not complete.
translations.idiomatic: This view sounds plausible but does not go far enough.

sentences.zh: 假若夏到前後，日食於寅卯酉戌之間，人向東北、西北觀之，則外道食分反多於內道矣。

translations.literal: Suppose around summer solstices an eclipse between yin mao you xu hours; one looks northeast or northwest—then outer-path eclipse fraction is actually greater than inner path.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose an eclipse around the summer solstice falls between the yin, mao, you, and xu hours; an observer facing northeast or northwest may see a greater obscuration on the outer path than on the inner.

sentences.zh: 日體大於月，月不能盡掩之，或遇食既，而日光四溢，形如金環，故日無食十分之理。

translations.literal: The sun's body is larger than the moon; the moon cannot fully cover it; sometimes at totality sunlight spills on all sides like a gold ring—thus the sun has no principle of eclipse of ten tenths.
translations.idiomatic: The sun is larger than the moon and cannot be fully covered; even at totality light may spill around the rim in a golden ring—so a solar eclipse can never reach ten-tenths obscuration.

sentences.zh: 雖既，亦止九分八十秒。

translations.literal: Even at totality it stops at nine-tenths eighty seconds.
translations.idiomatic: Even at totality the maximum is nine parts and eighty seconds.

sentences.zh: 《授時曆》日食，陽曆限六度，定法六十，陰曆限八度，定法八十。

translations.literal: Shoushi solar eclipses: yang calendar limit six degrees, fixed divisor sixty; yin calendar limit eight degrees, fixed divisor eighty.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shoushi calendar for solar eclipses, the yang limit is six degrees with a fixed divisor of sixty, and the yin limit eight degrees with a fixed divisor of eighty.

sentences.zh: 各置其限度，如其定法而一，皆得十分。

translations.literal: Each set its limit and divided by its fixed divisor to unity—all yielded ten-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Each applied its limit and divisor to unity, yielding ten-tenths in every case.

sentences.zh: 今於其定法下，各加一數以除限度，則得九分八十餘秒也。」

translations.literal: Now below each fixed divisor add one number to divide the limit—then obtain nine-tenths eighty-odd seconds.
translations.idiomatic: The new method adds one to each divisor before dividing the limit, producing nine parts and eighty-odd seconds.

sentences.zh: 其議月食也，曰：「暗虛者，景也。

translations.literal: His discussion of lunar eclipses says: "Dark void is shadow.
translations.idiomatic: In his discussion of lunar eclipses he says: "The dark void is simply the earth's shadow.

sentences.zh: 景之蔽月，無早晚高卑之異，四時九服其之殊。

translations.literal: Shadow obscuring the moon has no difference of early or late or high or low; four seasons and nine domains have no such variation.
translations.idiomatic: When shadow covers the moon there is no difference of morning or evening, height or depth, season or region.

sentences.zh: 譬如縣一黑丸於暗室，其左燃燭，其右縣一白丸，若燭光為黑丸所蔽，則白丸不受其光矣。

translations.literal: It is like hanging a black ball in a dark room: left a candle burns, right a white ball is hung—if candlelight is blocked by the black ball the white ball receives no light.
translations.idiomatic: It is like hanging a black sphere in a dark room with a candle on the left and a white sphere on the right: if the black sphere blocks the candle, the white sphere receives no light.

sentences.zh: 人在四旁觀之，所見無不同也。

translations.literal: People watching from four sides see no difference.
translations.idiomatic: Observers on any side see the same thing.

sentences.zh: 故月食無時差之說。

translations.literal: Therefore lunar eclipse has no time-correction theory.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar eclipses therefore admit no time correction.

sentences.zh: 自《紀元曆》妄立時差，《授時》因之，誤矣。」

translations.literal: From the Jiyuan calendar wrongly establishing time correction, Shoushi followed—it was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiyuan calendar wrongly introduced a time correction, which the Shoushi calendar adopted in turn—both were mistaken.

sentences.zh: 其議五緯也，曰：「古法推步五緯，不如變數之加減。

translations.literal: His discussion of the five planets says: "Ancient methods pushing the five planets are inferior to variable-number addition and subtraction.
translations.idiomatic: In his discussion of the five planets he says: "Ancient methods for advancing the five planets are inferior to variable increment and decrement.

sentences.zh: 北齊張子信仰觀歲久，知五緯有盈縮之變，當加減以求逐日之躔。

translations.literal: Northern Qi Zhang Zixin observed for years and knew the five planets have expansion-contraction variation—one must add and subtract to seek their daily stations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zixin of Northern Qi, observing over many years, saw that the five planets undergo accelerating and slowing variation and must be corrected day by day to track their true positions.

sentences.zh: 蓋五緯出入黃道內外，各自有其道，視日遠近為遲疾，其變數之加減，如裡路之徑直斜曲也。

translations.literal: For the five planets enter and exit inside and outside the ecliptic, each has its own path; viewed near or far from the sun for slow and fast—the variable addition and subtraction are like inner road straight versus slanted and curved.
translations.idiomatic: The five planets move inside and outside the ecliptic, each on its own path, appearing faster or slower as they approach or recede from the sun; their corrective increments resemble the difference between a straight inner road and a winding outer one.

sentences.zh: 宋人有言曰：『五星行度，惟留退之際最多差。

translations.literal: A Song man said: 'The five stars' traveling degrees—only at station and retreat is difference greatest.
translations.idiomatic: A Song scholar wrote: "Among the five planets' motions, the greatest discrepancies occur at stations and retrogradations.

sentences.zh: 自內而進者，其退必向外，自外而進者，其退必由內。

translations.literal: Advancing from inside, retreat must go outside; advancing from outside, retreat must go inside.
translations.idiomatic: A planet advancing from inside the path must retreat outward; one advancing from outside must retreat inward.

sentences.zh: 其跡臺循柳葉，兩末銳於中間，往還之道相去甚遠。

translations.literal: Their tracks are like loop around willow leaf—both ends sharp, middle broad; going and returning paths are far apart.
translations.idiomatic: Its track loops like a willow leaf—pointed at both ends, broad in the middle—with the outbound and return paths far apart.

sentences.zh: 故星行兩末度稍遲，以其斜行故也。

translations.literal: Hence at both ends the star's motion is somewhat slow, because the path is oblique.
translations.idiomatic: Hence at both ends the planet moves somewhat slowly because the path is oblique.

sentences.zh: 中間行度稍速，以其徑捷故也。

translations.literal: Middle motion somewhat fast, because the path is direct and quick.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle it moves somewhat faster because the path is direct and short.

sentences.zh: 』前代修曆，止增損舊法而已，未嘗實考天度。

translations.literal: Earlier dynasties revising calendars only increased or decreased old methods—never truly examined celestial degrees.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier dynasties, when revising calendars, only adjusted old formulas and never truly measured celestial positions.

sentences.zh: 其法須測驗每夜昏曉夜半，月及五星所在度秒，置簿錄之。

translations.literal: The method requires testing each night at dusk, dawn, and midnight the degrees and seconds where moon and five planets stand, and recording in a register.
translations.idiomatic: The proper method is to observe each night at dusk, dawn, and midnight the degrees and seconds of the moon and five planets and record them in a ledger.

sentences.zh: 滿五年，其間去陰雲晝見日數外，可行三年實行，然後可以算術綴之也。」

translations.literal: After five years, apart from cloudy nights and daytime sightings, three years of actual motion can proceed—then one may thread them with calculation.
translations.idiomatic: After five years—excluding cloudy nights and daytime observations—three years of reliable data will suffice to fit them by calculation.

sentences.zh: 書上，禮部尚書范謙奏：「歲差之法，自虞喜以來，代有差法之議，竟無晝一之規。

translations.literal: When the book was submitted, Minister of Rites Fan Qian memorialized: "The precession method—since Yu Xi each generation has had discussions of difference methods, yet ultimately no single rule for all.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was submitted, Fan Qian, Minister of Rites, memorialized: "The method of precession has been debated since Yu Xi, yet no generation has settled on a single uniform rule.

sentences.zh: 所以求之者，大約有三：考月令之中星，測二至之日景，驗交食之分秒。

translations.literal: Ways to seek it are roughly three: examine the monthly ordinances' meridian stars; measure the two solstices' sun shadows; verify eclipse minutes and seconds.
translations.idiomatic: Approaches to determining it fall roughly into three: checking the meridian stars in the Monthly Ordinances, measuring solstice shadows, and verifying eclipse times to the second.

sentences.zh: 考以衡管，測以臬表，驗以漏刻，斯亦危得之矣。

translations.literal: Examine with the pitch-pipe and balance tube, measure with gnomon table, verify with clepsydra—not easy to obtain safely.
translations.idiomatic: One examines with pitch-pipes and sighting tubes, measures with gnomons, and verifies with clepsydras—none of which yields secure results easily.

sentences.zh: 曆家以周天三百六十五度四分度之一，紀七政之行，又析度為百分，分為百秒，可謂密矣。

translations.literal: Calendar makers mark the full circuit at 365¼ degrees for the seven luminaries' motion, also split degrees into hundred parts, parts into hundred seconds—can be called exact.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar-makers reckon the full circuit at 365¼ degrees for the seven luminaries, subdividing each degree into a hundred parts and each part into a hundred seconds—precision on paper, at least.

sentences.zh: 然渾象之體，徑僅數尺，布周天度，每度不及指許，安所置分秒哉？

translations.literal: Yet the armillary sphere's body is only a few chi across, spreading full-circuit degrees—each degree not even a finger's width; where place seconds?
translations.idiomatic: Yet an armillary sphere is only a few feet across; spread the full circuit upon it and each degree is narrower than a finger—where can seconds be marked?

sentences.zh: 至於臬表之樹不過數尺，刻漏之籌不越數寸。

translations.literal: As for the gnomon table erected—no more than a few chi; clepsydra tallies no more than a few cun.
translations.idiomatic: Gnomons stand no taller than a few feet; clepsydra rods measure no more than a few inches.

sentences.zh: 以天之高且廣也，而以寸之物求之，欲其纖微不爽，不亦難乎？

translations.literal: Heaven is high and vast yet one seeks it with cun-sized things—wanting hair-fine accuracy, is it not hard?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is immeasurably high and wide, yet we seek it with inch-scale instruments—can hair-fine accuracy be anything but elusive?

sentences.zh: 故方其差在公秒之間，無可驗者，至蹬逾一度，乃可以管窺耳。

translations.literal: When the discrepancy is between tenths of a second it cannot be verified; only when it exceeds one degree can it be glimpsed through a tube.
translations.idiomatic: When the error lies within fractions of an arcsecond it cannot be confirmed; only when it exceeds a full degree can it be glimpsed through a sighting tube.

sentences.zh: 此所以窮古今之智七巧，不能盡其變歟？

translations.literal: Is this why exhausting the wisdom and seven crafts of all ages cannot exhaust its variation?
translations.idiomatic: Is this why all the ingenuity ever brought to the problem still cannot exhaust its variations?

sentences.zh: 即如世子言，以《大統》、《授時》二曆相較，考古則氣差三日，推今則時差必刻。

translations.literal: As the Prince of Zheng said, comparing Datong and Shoushi—examining antiquity the qi differ by three days; pushing the present the time correction must be ke.
translations.idiomatic: As the Prince of Zheng argues, comparing the Datong and Shoushi calendars: looking backward, solar terms differ by three days; projecting forward, the time correction would have to be several ke.

sentences.zh: 夫時差九刻，在亥子之間則移一日，在晦朔之交則移一月，此可驗之於近也。

translations.literal: A nine-ke time correction: between hai and zi shifts one day; at new-moon junction shifts one month—this can be verified in the near term.
translations.idiomatic: A nine-ke time shift would move the calendar one day if it fell between hai and zi, or one month if it crossed a new-moon boundary—effects one could verify immediately.

sentences.zh: 設移而前，則生明在二日之昏，設移而後，則生明在四日之夕矣。

translations.literal: If shifted forward, the first crescent would be dusk of day two; if shifted backward, first crescent evening of day four.
translations.idiomatic: Shifted forward, the first crescent would appear on the evening of the second day; shifted back, on the evening of the fourth.

sentences.zh: 今似未至此也。

translations.literal: Now it seems not yet to that point.
translations.idiomatic: At present we do not seem to have reached that stage.

sentences.zh: 其書應發欽天監參訂測驗。

translations.literal: His book should be sent to the Directorate of Astronomy for collating and testing.
translations.idiomatic: His book should be forwarded to the Directorate of Astronomy for collation and empirical testing.

sentences.zh: 世子留心曆學，博通今古，宜賜獎諭。

translations.literal: The Prince is attentive to calendar learning, broadly versed in past and present—appropriate to grant commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince is deeply versed in calendrical learning and broadly learned in past and present methods; he should receive an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 河南僉事刑雲路上書言：「治曆之耍治曆之耍，無逾觀象、測景、候時、籌策四事。

translations.literal: Henan Branch Vice Commissioner Xing Yunlu memorialized: "The crux of calendar-making, the crux of calendar-making—nothing surpasses observing phenomena, measuring shadows, awaiting time, and reckoning with counters—four affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Yunlu, Vice Commissioner of the Henan Branch, memorialized: "In calendar-making, nothing surpasses four tasks: observing phenomena, measuring shadows, awaiting the right moment, and computing with counting rods.

sentences.zh: 今丙申年日至，臣測得乙未日未正一刻，而《大統》推在申正二刻，相差九刻。

translations.literal: Now at this bingchen year's solstice I measured it on yiwei day at wei zheng first ke; Datong places it at shen zheng second ke—a difference of nine ke.
translations.idiomatic: At this year's solstice (bingchen), I measured the moment on yiwei day at the first ke of wei zheng, whereas the Datong calendar places it at the second ke of shen zheng—a discrepancy of nine ke.

sentences.zh: 且今年立春、夏至、立冬皆適直子半之交。

translations.literal: Moreover this year's beginning of spring, summer solstice, and beginning of winter all fall right at the jiaozi midnight crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, this year's beginning of spring, summer solstice, and beginning of winter all fall precisely at the midnight jiaozi boundary.

sentences.zh: 臣推立春乙亥，而《大統》推丙子；

translations.literal: I compute beginning of spring yi hai; Datong computes bing zi;
translations.idiomatic: I compute the beginning of spring as yi hai; the Datong calendar gives bing zi;

sentences.zh: 夏至壬辰，而《大統》推癸巳；

translations.literal: Summer solstice ren chen; Datong gui si;
translations.idiomatic: summer solstice as ren chen; the Datong gives gui si;

sentences.zh: 立冬巳酉，而《大統》推庚戌。

translations.literal: Beginning of winter si you; Datong geng xu.
translations.idiomatic: beginning of winter as si you; the Datong gives geng xu.

sentences.zh: 相隔皆一日。

translations.literal: Each differed by one day.
translations.idiomatic: In each case the discrepancy was a full day.

sentences.zh: 若或直元日於子半，則當退履端於月窮，而朝賀大禮在月正二日矣。

translations.literal: If New Year's Day fell exactly at midnight, then the start of the year ought to be moved back to the end of the month, and the great court congratulation would fall on the second day of the first month.
translations.idiomatic: If New Year's Day were placed exactly at the midnight boundary, the year's beginning would have to be pushed back to month's end and the great New Year audience would fall on the second day of the first month.

sentences.zh: 豈細故耶？

translations.literal: Is this a trifling matter?
translations.idiomatic: Could that be dismissed as a trifling matter?

sentences.zh: 閏八月朔，日食，《大統》推初虧巳正二刻，食幾既，而臣候初虧巳正一刻，食止七分餘。

translations.literal: On the first day of the intercalary eighth month there was a solar eclipse. The Grand Concordance predicted first contact at the second quarter of si, nearly total eclipse; but when your subject observed, first contact was at the first quarter of si and the eclipse reached only a little over seven-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the intercalary eighth month there was a solar eclipse. The Grand Concordance predicted first contact in the second quarter of the si double-hour, with the eclipse nearly total; yet when I observed, first contact came in the first quarter of si and the eclipse reached only a little over seven-tenths.

sentences.zh: 《大統》實後天幾二刻，則閏應及轉應、交應，各宜增損之矣。

translations.literal: The Grand Concordance was in fact nearly two quarters behind heaven; then the intercalation correspondence, rotation correspondence, and nodal correspondence should each be increased or decreased accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Concordance was in fact nearly two quarters behind heaven; the intercalation, rotation, and nodal correspondences should each be adjusted accordingly.

sentences.zh: 」欽天監見雲路疏，甚惡之。

translations.literal: 」When the Directorate of Astronomy saw Yunlu's memorial, it detested it deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When the Directorate of Astronomy saw Yunlu's memorial, it detested it deeply.

sentences.zh: 監正張應候奏詆，謂其僭妄惑世。

translations.literal: Director Zhang Yinghou memorialized in denunciation, calling him presumptuous, reckless, and a deceiver of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhang Yinghou memorialized in denunciation, calling him presumptuous, reckless, and a deceiver of the world.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書范謙乃言：「曆為國家大事，士夫所當講求，非曆士之所得私。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Fan Qian then said: "The calendar is a great affair of state; scholars ought to pursue it— it is not something calendar officers may monopolize.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Fan Qian then said, "The calendar is a great affair of state, which scholars ought to pursue; it is not something calendar officers may monopolize.

sentences.zh: 律例所禁，乃妄言妖祥者耳。

translations.literal: What the statutes forbid is only reckless talk of omens and prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: What the statutes forbid is only reckless talk of omens and prodigies.

sentences.zh: 監官拘守成法，不能修改合天。

translations.literal: The observatory officers cling to established methods and cannot revise them to match heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The observatory officers cling to established methods and cannot revise them to match heaven.

sentences.zh: 幸有其人，所當和衷共事，不宜妒忌。

translations.literal: Fortunately there is such a man; they ought to work together in good faith and not be jealous.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately there is such a man; they ought to work together in good faith and not be jealous.

sentences.zh: 乞以雲路提叔欽天監事，督率官屬，精心測候，以成鉅典。

translations.literal: I beg that Yunlu be put in charge of Directorate of Astronomy affairs, to lead the officials in careful observation and complete the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Yunlu be put in charge of Directorate of Astronomy affairs, to lead the officials in careful observation and complete the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 」議上，不報。

translations.literal: 」The proposal went up but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal went up but received no response.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，監推十一月壬寅朔日食分秒及虧圓之候，職方郎範守己疏駁其誤。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year the Directorate predicted the degree, seconds, and phases of obscuration and fullness for the solar eclipse on the renyin new moon of the eleventh month; Bureau of Appointments director Fan Shouji memorialized to refute its errors.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-eight the Directorate predicted the magnitude in degrees and seconds and the phases of obscuration and fullness for the solar eclipse on the renyin new moon of the eleventh month; Bureau of Appointments director Fan Shouji memorialized to refute its errors.

sentences.zh: 禮官因請博求知曆學者，令與監官晝夜推測，庶幾曆法靡差。

translations.literal: The ritual officials therefore asked to seek broadly those versed in calendrical learning and have them push and observe day and night with the observatory officers, so that the calendar might be without error.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials therefore asked to seek broadly those versed in calendrical learning and have them compute and observe day and night with the observatory officers, so that the calendar might be without error.

sentences.zh: 於是五官正周子愚言：「大西洋歸化遠臣龐迪峨、熊三撥等，攜有彼國曆法，多中國典籍所未備者。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Five Offices Director Zhou Ziyu said: "The distant subjects from the Great Western Ocean who have submitted, Pang Di'e, Xiong Sanbo, and others, have brought their country's calendar methods, many of which are not found in Chinese classics.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Five Offices Director Zhou Ziyu said, "The distant subjects from the Great Western Ocean who have submitted, Pang Di'e, Xiong Sanbo, and others, have brought their country's calendar methods, many of which are not found in Chinese classics.

sentences.zh: 乞視洪中譯西域曆法例，取知曆儒臣率同監官，將諸書盡譯，以補典籍之缺。

translations.literal: I beg that, following the precedent of Hong Zhong's translation of Western Region calendar methods, calendar-learned scholar-officials be taken to lead the observatory officers in translating all these books fully, to supply what the classics lack.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that, following the precedent of Hong Zhong's translation of Western Region calendar methods, calendar-learned scholar-officials be taken to lead the observatory officers in translating all these books fully, to supply what the classics lack.

sentences.zh: 」先是，大西洋人利瑪竇進貢土物，而迪峨、三撥及能華同、鄧玉函、湯若望等先後至，俱精究天文曆法。

translations.literal: 」Earlier the man of the Great Western Ocean Matteo Ricci had presented native products as tribute, and Di'e, Sanbo, Neng Huatong, Deng Yuhan, Adam Schall, and others had arrived in succession, all deeply versed in astronomy and the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the man of the Great Western Ocean Matteo Ricci had presented native products as tribute, and Di'e, Sanbo, Neng Huatong, Deng Yuhan, Adam Schall, and others had arrived in succession, all deeply versed in astronomy and the calendar.

sentences.zh: 禮部因奏：「精通曆法，如雲路、守己為時所推，請改授京卿，共理曆事。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites therefore memorialized: "Those expert in the calendar, such as Yunlu and Shouji, are acclaimed by the age; I beg that they be transferred to capital ministerial posts to administer calendar affairs jointly.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites therefore memorialized, "Those expert in the calendar, such as Yunlu and Shouji, are acclaimed by the age; I beg that they be transferred to capital ministerial posts to administer calendar affairs jointly.

sentences.zh: 翰林院檢討徐光啟、南京工部員外郎李之藻亦皆精心曆理，可與迪峨、三撥等同譯西洋法，俾雲路等參訂修改。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Xu Guangqi and Nanjing Works Bureau vice director Li Zhizao are also both deeply versed in calendrical principles and may translate the Western methods together with Di'e and Sanbo, so that Yunlu and others may consult, revise, and amend.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Xu Guangqi and Nanjing Works Bureau vice director Li Zhizao are also both deeply versed in calendrical principles and may translate the Western methods together with Di'e and Sanbo, so that Yunlu and others may consult, revise, and amend.

sentences.zh: 然曆法疏密，莫顯於交食，欲議修曆，必重測驗。

translations.literal: Yet whether a calendar is coarse or fine is nowhere clearer than in eclipses and planetary encroachments; if one wishes to discuss revising the calendar, testing must be heavily emphasized.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whether a calendar is coarse or fine is nowhere clearer than in eclipses and planetary encroachments; if one wishes to discuss revising the calendar, testing must be heavily emphasized.

sentences.zh: 乞敕所司修治儀器，以便從事。

translations.literal: I beg that the responsible offices be ordered to repair and prepare instruments for convenient use in the work.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the responsible offices be ordered to repair and prepare instruments for convenient use in the work.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，留中。

translations.literal: 」The memorial entered but was held at court.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial entered but was held at court.

sentences.zh: 未幾雲路、之藻皆召至京，參預曆事。

translations.literal: Before long Yunlu and Zhizao were both summoned to the capital to take part in calendar affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yunlu and Zhizao were both summoned to the capital to take part in calendar affairs.

sentences.zh: 雲路據其所學，之藻則以西法為宗。

translations.literal: Yunlu relied on his own learning; Zhizao took Western methods as his school.
translations.idiomatic: Yunlu relied on his own learning; Zhizao took Western methods as his school.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，之藻已改銜南京太僕少卿，奏上西洋曆法，略言臺監推算日月交食時刻虧分之謬。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year Zhizao, having changed his title to Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud vice minister, memorialized presenting Western calendar methods, briefly stating the errors of the observatory and directorate in calculating the times, degrees of obscuration, and magnitudes of solar and lunar eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year Zhizao, having changed his title to Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud vice minister, memorialized presenting Western calendar methods, briefly stating the errors of the observatory and directorate in calculating the times, degrees of obscuration, and magnitudes of solar and lunar eclipses.

sentences.zh: 而力薦迪峨、三撥及華民、陽瑪諾等，言：「其所論天文曆數，有中國昔賢所未及者，不徒論其數，又能明其所以然之理。

translations.literal: He strongly recommended Di'e, Sanbo, Alphonse Vagnoni, and others, saying: "What they discuss in astronomy and calendrical numbers reaches what China's ancient worthies never attained; they do not merely discuss the numbers but can also clarify the reasons why they are so.
translations.idiomatic: He strongly recommended Di'e, Sanbo, Alphonse Vagnoni, and others, saying, "What they discuss in astronomy and calendrical numbers reaches what China's ancient worthies never attained; they do not merely discuss the numbers but can also clarify the reasons why they are so.

sentences.zh: 其所制窺天、窺日之器，種種精絕。

translations.literal: The instruments they have made for viewing heaven and viewing the sun are in every kind exquisitely perfected.
translations.idiomatic: The instruments they have made for viewing heaven and viewing the sun are in every kind exquisitely perfected.

sentences.zh: 今迪峨等年齡向衰，乞敕禮部開局，取其曆法，譯出成書。

translations.literal: Now Di'e and the others are growing old in years; I beg that the Ministry of Rites be ordered to open a bureau, take their calendar methods, and translate them into completed books.
translations.idiomatic: Now Di'e and the others are growing old in years; I beg that the Ministry of Rites be ordered to open a bureau, take their calendar methods, and translate them into completed books.

sentences.zh: 」禮科姚永濟亦以為言。

translations.literal: 」The Ministry of Rites censor Yao Yongji also spoke to the same effect.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites censor Yao Yongji also spoke to the same effect.

sentences.zh: 時庶務因循，未暇開局也。

translations.literal: At the time routine affairs dragged on and there was no leisure to open a bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the time routine affairs dragged on and there was no leisure to open a bureau.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，雲路獻《七政真數》，言：「步曆之法，必以兩交相對。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year Yunlu presented the True Numbers of the Seven Regulators, saying: "The method of pacing the calendar must take the two nodes in mutual opposition.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year Yunlu presented the True Numbers of the Seven Regulators, saying, "The method of pacing the calendar must take the two nodes in mutual opposition.

sentences.zh: 兩交正，而中間時刻分秒之度數，一一可按。

translations.literal: When the two nodes are correct, the degrees of the intermediate times, moments, and seconds can each be checked off one by one.
translations.idiomatic: When the two nodes are correct, the degrees of the intermediate times, moments, and seconds can each be checked off one by one.

sentences.zh: 日月之交食，五星之淩犯，皆日月五星之相交也。

translations.literal: Solar and lunar eclipses and the five planets' encroachments are all intersections of sun, moon, and the five planets.
translations.idiomatic: Solar and lunar eclipses and the five planets' encroachments are all intersections of sun, moon, and the five planets.

sentences.zh: 兩交相對，互相發明，七政之能事畢矣。

translations.literal: The two nodes in mutual opposition illuminate each other; the full capability of the seven regulators is then complete.
translations.idiomatic: The two nodes in mutual opposition illuminate each other; the full capability of the seven regulators is then complete.

sentences.zh: 」天啟元年春，雲路復詳述古今時刻，與欽天監所推互異。

translations.literal: 」In the spring of the first year of Tianqi, Yunlu again set forth ancient and modern times in detail, which differed from what the Directorate of Astronomy calculated.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Tianqi 1, Yunlu again set forth ancient and modern times in detail, which differed from what the Directorate of Astronomy calculated.

sentences.zh: 症新法至密，章下禮部。

translations.literal: He proved the new method most precise; the memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He proved the new method most precise; the memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四月壬申朔日食，雲路所推食分時刻，與欽天監所推互異。

translations.literal: On the ren shen new moon of the fourth month there was a solar eclipse; the eclipse magnitude and time Yunlu calculated differed from what the Directorate of Astronomy calculated.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen new moon of the fourth month there was a solar eclipse; the eclipse magnitude and time Yunlu calculated differed from what the Directorate of Astronomy calculated.

sentences.zh: 自言新法至密，至期考驗，皆與天下不合。

translations.literal: He himself said the new method was most precise, but when the day came for testing, none matched what was seen under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He himself said the new method was most precise, but when the day came for testing, none matched what was seen under heaven.

sentences.zh: 雲路又嘗論《大統》宮度交界，當以歲差考定，不當仍用《授時》三百年前所測之數。

translations.literal: Yunlu also once argued that the Grand Concordance's lodge-degree boundaries ought to be fixed by precession and ought not still to use numbers measured three hundred years earlier in the Season Granting Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Yunlu also once argued that the Grand Concordance's lodge-degree boundaries ought to be fixed by precession and ought not still to use numbers measured three hundred years earlier in the Season Granting Calendar.

sentences.zh: 又月建月關半杓所指，鬥杓有歲差，而月建無改移。

translations.literal: He also held that the monthly establishment and monthly barrier indicated by half the Dipper's handle show precession in the Dipper's handle but no shift in the monthly establishment— sound doctrines all.
translations.idiomatic: He also held that the monthly establishment and monthly barrier indicated by half the Dipper's handle show precession in the Dipper's handle but no shift in the monthly establishment—sound doctrines all.

sentences.zh: 皆篤論也。

translations.literal: All were sound doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: All were sound doctrines.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年五月乙酉朔日食，禮部侍郎徐光啟依西法預推，順天府見食二分有奇，瓊州食既，大寧以北不食。

translations.literal: On the yiyou new moon of the fifth month in the second year of Chongzhen there was a solar eclipse. Vice Minister of Rites Xu Guangqi predicted by Western methods in advance: Shuntian Prefecture would see a little over two-tenths obscured, Qiongzhou total eclipse, and north of Daining no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou new moon of the fifth month in Chongzhen 2 there was a solar eclipse. Vice Minister of Rites Xu Guangqi predicted by Western methods in advance: Shuntian Prefecture would see a little over two-tenths obscured, Qiongzhou total eclipse, and north of Daining no eclipse.

sentences.zh: 《大統》、《回回》所推，順天食分時刻，與光啟妻異。

translations.literal: What the Grand Concordance and Huihui calendars predicted for Shuntian's magnitude and time differed from Guangqi's.
translations.idiomatic: What the Grand Concordance and Huihui calendars predicted for Shuntian's magnitude and time differed from Guangqi's.

sentences.zh: 已而光啟法驗，餘皆疏。

translations.literal: Afterward Guangqi's method was verified; the rest were all coarse.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Guangqi's method was verified; the rest were all coarse.

sentences.zh: 帝切責監官。

translations.literal: The emperor sharply rebuked the observatory officers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sharply rebuked the observatory officers.

sentences.zh: 時五官正戈豐年等言：「《大統》乃國初所定，寮即郭守敬《授時曆》也，二百六十年毫未增損。

translations.literal: At the time Five Offices Director Ge Fengnian and others said: "The Grand Concordance was fixed at the dynasty's founding; it is namely Guo Shoujing's Season Granting Calendar, and for two hundred sixty years not a hair's breadth has been added or subtracted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Five Offices Director Ge Fengnian and others said, "The Grand Concordance was fixed at the dynasty's founding; it is namely Guo Shoujing's Season Granting Calendar, and for two hundred sixty years not a hair's breadth has been added or subtracted.

sentences.zh: 自至元十八年造曆，越十八年為大德三年八月，已當食不食，六年六月又食而失推。

translations.literal: From the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan when the calendar was made, after eighteen years came the eighth month of the third year of Dade, when an eclipse ought to have occurred but did not; in the sixth month of the sixth year there was an eclipse but it was not predicted.
translations.idiomatic: From the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan when the calendar was made, after eighteen years came the eighth month of the third year of Dade, when an eclipse ought to have occurred but did not; in the sixth month of the sixth year there was an eclipse but it was not predicted.

sentences.zh: 是時守敬方知院事，亦付之無可奈佑，況斤斤守法者哉？

translations.literal: At that time Shoujing had only just learned of the Academy's affairs and likewise had no remedy— how much less those who fuss over guarding the law?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shoujing had only just learned of the Academy's affairs and likewise had no remedy—how much less those who fuss over guarding the law?

sentences.zh: 今若循舊，向後不能無差。

translations.literal: If we now follow the old ways, hereafter there cannot fail to be discrepancies.
translations.idiomatic: If we now follow the old ways, hereafter there cannot fail to be discrepancies.

sentences.zh: 」於是禮部奏開局修改。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon the Ministry of Rites memorialized to open a bureau for revision.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Ministry of Rites memorialized to open a bureau for revision.

sentences.zh: 乃以光啟督修曆法。

translations.literal: Guangqi was then put in charge of supervising revision of the calendar law.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi was then put in charge of supervising revision of the calendar law.

sentences.zh: 光啟言：近世言曆諸家，大都宗郭守敬法，至若歲差環轉，歲實參差，天有緯度，地有經度，列宿有本行，月五星有本輪，日月有真會、視會，皆古所未聞，惟西曆有之。

translations.literal: Guangqi said: Recent schools that discuss the calendar mostly take Guo Shoujing's method as their ancestor; but as for precession's cyclical rotation, the true year's fractional discrepancies, heaven having latitude, earth having longitude, lodges having proper motion, moon and five planets having deferent circles, sun and moon having true conjunction and apparent conjunction—all were unheard of in antiquity and exist only in the Western calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi said: Recent schools that discuss the calendar mostly take Guo Shoujing's method as their ancestor; but as for precession's cyclical rotation, the true year's fractional discrepancies, heaven having latitude, earth having longitude, lodges having proper motion, moon and five planets having deferent circles, sun and moon having true conjunction and apparent conjunction—all were unheard of in antiquity and exist only in the Western calendar.

sentences.zh: 而舍此數法，則交食淩犯，終無密合理。

translations.literal: Yet if one sets aside these several methods, eclipses and encroachments will in the end have no close-fitting principle.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if one sets aside these several methods, eclipses and encroachments will in the end have no close-fitting principle.

sentences.zh: 宜取其法參互考訂，使與《大統》法會同歸一。」

translations.literal: One ought to take their methods, consult and cross-check them, and make them meet and return to one with the Grand Concordance method."
translations.idiomatic: One ought to take their methods, consult and cross-check them, and make them meet and return to one with the Grand Concordance method."

sentences.zh: 已而光啟上曆法修正十事：其一，議歲差，每歲東行漸長短之數，以正古來百年、五十年、六十年多寡互異之說。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Guangqi submitted ten items for calendar revision: first, discuss precession—the yearly eastward motion and the numbers of gradual lengthening and shortening—to correct the ancient divergent theories of one hundred, fifty, and sixty years.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Guangqi submitted ten items for calendar revision: first, discuss precession—the yearly eastward motion and the numbers of gradual lengthening and shortening—to correct the ancient divergent theories of one hundred, fifty, and sixty years.

sentences.zh: 其二，議歲實小餘，昔多今少，漸次改易，及日景長短歲歲不同之因，以定冬至，以正氣明朔。

translations.literal: Second, discuss the true year's small remainder—more in the past, less now, gradually changing, and the reason the sun's shadow length differs year by year—to fix the winter solstice and correct the qi and clarify the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Second, discuss the true year's small remainder—more in the past, less now, gradually changing, and the reason the sun's shadow length differs year by year—to fix the winter solstice and correct the qi and clarify the new moon.

sentences.zh: 其三，每日測驗日行經度，以定盈縮加減真率，東西南北高下之差，以步月離。

translations.literal: Third, test daily the sun's motion in longitude to fix the true rates of addition and subtraction for surplus and deficit, and the differences of east, west, south, north, high, and low, to pace lunar departure.
translations.idiomatic: Third, test daily the sun's motion in longitude to fix the true rates of addition and subtraction for surplus and deficit, and the differences of east, west, south, north, high, and low, to pace lunar departure.

sentences.zh: 其四，夜測月行經緯度數，以定交轉遲疾真率，東西北高下之差，以步月離。

translations.literal: Fourth, at night measure the moon's motion in longitude and latitude to fix the true rates of nodal rotation's slow and fast phases, and the differences of east, west, north, high, and low, to pace lunar departure.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, at night measure the moon's motion in longitude and latitude to fix the true rates of nodal rotation's slow and fast phases, and the differences of east, west, north, high, and low, to pace lunar departure.

sentences.zh: 其五，密測列宿以緯行度，以定七政盈縮、遲疾、順逆、違離、遠近之數。

translations.literal: Fifth, closely measure the lodges to fix latitude motion in degrees, to fix the seven regulators' numbers of surplus, deficit, slow, fast, direct, retrograde, departure, and approach.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, closely measure the lodges to fix latitude motion in degrees, to fix the seven regulators' numbers of surplus, deficit, slow, fast, direct, retrograde, departure, and approach.

sentences.zh: 其六，密測五星經緯行度，以定小輪行度遲疾、留逆、伏見之數，東西南北高下之差，以推步淩犯。

translations.literal: Sixth, closely measure the five planets' motion in longitude and latitude to fix the epicycle's degrees of slow and fast motion, station, retrogradation, and hiding and appearance, and the differences of east, west, south, north, high, and low, to compute and pace encroachments.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, closely measure the five planets' motion in longitude and latitude to fix the epicycle's degrees of slow and fast motion, station, retrogradation, and hiding and appearance, and the differences of east, west, south, north, high, and low, to compute and pace encroachments.

sentences.zh: 其七，推變黃道、赤道廣狹度數，密測二道距度，及月五星各道與黃道相距之度，以定交轉。

translations.literal: Seventh, deduce changes in the ecliptic's and equator's breadth and narrowness in degrees, closely measure the two paths' separation in degrees and each of the moon and five planets' paths' distance from the ecliptic in degrees, to fix nodal rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, deduce changes in the ecliptic's and equator's breadth and narrowness in degrees, closely measure the two paths' separation in degrees and each of the moon and five planets' paths' distance from the ecliptic in degrees, to fix nodal rotation.

sentences.zh: 其八，議日月去交遠近及真會、視會之因，以定距午時差之真率，以正交食。

translations.literal: Eighth, discuss the reasons for sun and moon's distance from the node and for true and apparent conjunction, to fix the true rate of the difference from noon, to correct eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, discuss the reasons for sun and moon's distance from the node and for true and apparent conjunction, to fix the true rate of the difference from noon, to correct eclipses.

sentences.zh: 其九，測日行，考知二極出入地度數，以定周天緯度，以齊七政。

translations.literal: Ninth, measure the sun's motion and examine the degrees by which the two poles enter and leave the earth, to fix the degrees of the circuit of heaven's latitude and align the seven regulators.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, measure the sun's motion and examine the degrees by which the two poles enter and leave the earth, to fix the degrees of the circuit of heaven's latitude and align the seven regulators.

sentences.zh: 因月食考知東西相距地輪經度，以定交食時刻。

translations.literal: From lunar eclipses examine the terrestrial longitude separating east and west, to fix eclipse times.
translations.idiomatic: From lunar eclipses examine the terrestrial longitude separating east and west, to fix eclipse times.

sentences.zh: 其十，依唐、元法，隨地測驗二極出入地度數，地輪經緯，以求晝夜晨昏永短，以正交食有無、先後、多寡之數。

translations.literal: Tenth, following Tang and Yuan methods, test locally the degrees by which the two poles enter and leave the earth and the earth's longitude and latitude, to seek the lengths of day, night, dawn, and dusk, and correct the numbers of whether eclipses occur, their priority, lateness, and magnitude.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, following Tang and Yuan methods, test locally the degrees by which the two poles enter and leave the earth and the earth's longitude and latitude, to seek the lengths of day, night, dawn, and dusk, and correct the numbers of whether eclipses occur, their priority, lateness, and magnitude.

sentences.zh: 因舉南京太僕少卿李之藻、西洋人能華民、鄧玉涵。

translations.literal: He also recommended Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud vice minister Li Zhizao and Westerners Alphonse Vagnoni and Deng Yuhan.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud vice minister Li Zhizao and Westerners Alphonse Vagnoni and Deng Yuhan.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 九月癸卯開曆局。

translations.literal: In the ninth month on guimao the Calendar Bureau was opened.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month on guimao the Calendar Bureau was opened.

sentences.zh: 三年，玉函卒，又徵西洋人湯若望、羅雅穀譯書演算。

translations.literal: In the third year Yuhan died; Westerners Adam Schall and Giacomo Rho were again summoned to translate books and perform calculations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Yuhan died; Westerners Adam Schall and Giacomo Rho were again summoned to translate books and perform calculations.

sentences.zh: 光啟進本部尚書，仍督修曆法。

translations.literal: Guangqi was promoted to minister of his department and still supervised revision of the calendar law.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi was promoted to minister of his department and still supervised revision of the calendar law.

sentences.zh: 時巡按四御史馬如蚊薦資縣諸生冷守中精曆學以所呈曆書送局。

translations.literal: At the time touring censor of the four circuits Ma Ruwen recommended Zi county scholar Leng Shouzhong, expert in calendrical learning, and sent the calendar book he presented to the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the time touring censor of the four circuits Ma Ruwen recommended Zi county scholar Leng Shouzhong, expert in calendrical learning, and sent the calendar book he presented to the bureau.

sentences.zh: 光啟力駁其謬，並預推次年四月川食時刻，令其臨時比測。

translations.literal: Guangqi forcefully refuted its errors and also predicted in advance the time of the Sichuan eclipse in the fourth month of the following year, ordering him to compare and test on the spot when the time came.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi forcefully refuted its errors and also predicted in advance the time of the Sichuan eclipse in the fourth month of the following year, ordering him to compare and test on the spot when the time came.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，光啟進《曆書》二十四卷。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year Guangqi presented twenty-four juan of the Calendar Book.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year Guangqi presented twenty-four juan of the Calendar Book.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊午，夜望月食，光啟預推分秒時刻方位。

translations.literal: In summer, on the night of wuwu in the fourth month, there was a lunar eclipse; Guangqi predicted in advance the degrees, seconds, time, and direction.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the night of wuwu in the fourth month, there was a lunar eclipse; Guangqi predicted in advance the degrees, seconds, time, and direction.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「日食隨地不同，則用地緯度算其食分多少，用地經度算其加時早晏。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Solar eclipses differ by place; therefore use terrestrial latitude to calculate how great the obscuration is, and use terrestrial longitude to calculate whether the additive time is early or late.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, saying, "Solar eclipses differ by place; therefore use terrestrial latitude to calculate how great the obscuration is, and use terrestrial longitude to calculate whether the additive time is early or late.

sentences.zh: 月食分秒，海內並同，止用地經度推求先後時刻。

translations.literal: Lunar eclipse degrees and seconds are the same throughout the realm; only terrestrial longitude is used to seek the prior and posterior times.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar eclipse degrees and seconds are the same throughout the realm; only terrestrial longitude is used to seek the prior and posterior times.

sentences.zh: 臣從輿地圖約略推步，開載各布政司月食初虧度分，蓋食分多少既天下皆同，則餘率可以類推，不若日食之經緯各殊，心須詳備也。

translations.literal: Your subject roughly computed from the terrestrial map and set out the initial obscuration degrees for each provincial administration commission's lunar eclipse; since the magnitude is the same everywhere under heaven, the remaining rates can be inferred by analogy, unlike solar eclipses where longitude and latitude each differ and all must be set out in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject roughly computed from the terrestrial map and set out the initial obscuration degrees for each provincial administration commission's lunar eclipse; since the magnitude is the same everywhere under heaven, the remaining rates can be inferred by analogy, unlike solar eclipses where longitude and latitude each differ and all must be set out in detail.

sentences.zh: 又月體一十五分，則盡入暗虛亦十五分止耳。

translations.literal: Again, the moon's body is fifteen parts; fully entering the earth's shadow is also only fifteen parts.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the moon's body is fifteen parts; fully entering the earth's shadow is also only fifteen parts.

sentences.zh: 今推二十六分六十六十秒者，蓋暗虛體大於月，若食時去交稍遠，即月體不能全入暗虛，止從月體論其分數。

translations.literal: What is now computed as twenty-six parts, six tens, and ten seconds is because the earth's shadow is larger than the moon; if at eclipse the distance from the node is slightly far, the moon's body cannot fully enter the earth's shadow, and one counts only from the moon's body for the fraction.
translations.idiomatic: What is now computed as twenty-six parts, six tens, and ten seconds is because the earth's shadow is larger than the moon; if at eclipse the distance from the node is slightly far, the moon's body cannot fully enter the earth's shadow, and one counts only from the moon's body for the fraction.

sentences.zh: 是夕之食，極近於交，故月入暗虛十五分方為食既，更進一十一分有奇，乃得生光，故為二十六分有奇。

translations.literal: That night's eclipse was extremely close to the node; therefore the moon had to enter the earth's shadow fifteen parts before total eclipse, and advancing a further eleven-odd parts before light reappeared— hence a little over twenty-six parts.
translations.idiomatic: That night's eclipse was extremely close to the node; therefore the moon had to enter the earth's shadow fifteen parts before total eclipse, and advancing a further eleven-odd parts before light reappeared—hence a little over twenty-six parts.

sentences.zh: 如《回回曆》推十八分四十七秒，略同此法也。

translations.literal: As the Huihui Calendar predicts eighteen parts, four tens, and forty-seven seconds, it is roughly the same as this method.
translations.idiomatic: As the Huihui Calendar predicts eighteen parts, four tens, and forty-seven seconds, it is roughly the same as this method.

sentences.zh: 」已四川報次序守中所推月食實差二時，而新法密合。

translations.literal: 」Already Sichuan had reported; by comparison Shouzhong's predicted lunar eclipse was actually two hours off, while the new method matched closely.
translations.idiomatic: Already Sichuan had reported; by comparison Shouzhong's predicted lunar eclipse was actually two hours off, while the new method matched closely.

sentences.zh: 光啟又進《曆書》二十一卷。

translations.literal: Guangqi again presented twenty-one juan of the Calendar Book.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi again presented twenty-one juan of the Calendar Book.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛丑朔日食，新法預順天見食二分一十二秒，應天以南下食，大漢以北食既，例以京師見食不及三分，不救護。

translations.literal: In winter, on the xinchou new moon of the tenth month there was a solar eclipse. The new method predicted in advance that Shuntian would see two parts and twelve seconds obscured; south of Yingtian the eclipse would be below, north of Dahan total eclipse. By precedent, because the capital's eclipse was less than three-tenths, no protective rites were performed.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the xinchou new moon of the tenth month there was a solar eclipse. The new method predicted in advance that Shuntian would see two parts and twelve seconds obscured; south of Yingtian the eclipse would be below, north of Dahan total eclipse. By precedent, because the capital's eclipse was less than three-tenths, no protective rites were performed.

sentences.zh: 光啟言：

translations.literal: Guangqi said:
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi said:

sentences.zh: 月食在夜，加時早晚，若無定據。

translations.literal: Lunar eclipses occur at night; whether the additive time is early or late has no fixed basis.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar eclipses occur at night; whether the additive time is early or late has no fixed basis.

sentences.zh: 惟日食按晷定時，無可遷就。

translations.literal: Only solar eclipses fix time by the gnomon and cannot be accommodated.
translations.idiomatic: Only solar eclipses fix time by the gnomon and cannot be accommodated.

sentences.zh: 故曆法疏密，此為的症。

translations.literal: Therefore whether a calendar is coarse or fine— this is the decisive test.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore whether a calendar is coarse or fine—this is the decisive test.

sentences.zh: 臣等纂輯新法，漸次就緒，而向生交食為期尚遠，此時不與監臣共見，至成曆後，將何徵信？

translations.literal: Your subjects are compiling the new method, gradually nearing completion, yet the next eclipses are still far off and we will not be with the observatory officers to witness them; when the calendar is finished, what shall we take as proof?
translations.idiomatic: Your subjects are compiling the new method, gradually nearing completion, yet the next eclipses are still far off and we will not be with the observatory officers to witness them; when the calendar is finished, what shall we take as proof?

sentences.zh: 且是食之必當測俟，更有說焉。

translations.literal: Moreover this eclipse must be observed and tested— there is more to say.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover this eclipse must be observed and tested—there is more to say.

sentences.zh: 舊法食在正中，則無時差。

translations.literal: In the old method, when the eclipse was at the center there was no time difference.
translations.idiomatic: In the old method, when the eclipse was at the center there was no time difference.

sentences.zh: 今此食既在日中，而新法仍有時差者，蓋以七政運行皆依黃道，不由赤道。

translations.literal: Now this eclipse is at midday, yet the new method still has a time difference— because the seven regulators' motion all follows the ecliptic and not the equator.
translations.idiomatic: Now this eclipse is at midday, yet the new method still has a time difference—because the seven regulators' motion all follows the ecliptic and not the equator.

sentences.zh: 舊法所謂中乃道之午中，非黃道之正中也。

translations.literal: What the old method calls "center" is noon on the path, not true ecliptic center.
translations.idiomatic: What the old method calls "center" is noon on the path, not true ecliptic center.

sentences.zh: 黃赤道二道之中，獨冬夏至加時正午，乃得同度。

translations.literal: Only at winter and summer solstice do the centers of the ecliptic and equator coincide at noon and attain the same degree.
translations.idiomatic: Only at winter and summer solstice do the centers of the ecliptic and equator coincide at noon and attain the same degree.

sentences.zh: 今十月朔去冬至度數尚遠，兩中之差，二下三度有奇，豈可因加時近午，不加不減乎？

translations.literal: Now the first day of the tenth month is still far in degrees from the winter solstice; the difference between the two centers is a little over two or three degrees— how can one, because the additive time is near noon, add or subtract nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Now the first day of the tenth month is still far in degrees from the winter solstice; the difference between the two centers is a little over two or three degrees—how can one, because the additive time is near noon, add or subtract nothing?

sentences.zh: 適際此日，又值此時，足可驗時差之正術，二也。

translations.literal: To meet this day and this time is enough to verify the correct method of time difference— second point.
translations.idiomatic: To meet this day and this time is enough to verify the correct method of time difference—second point.

sentences.zh: 本方之地經度，未得真率，則加時難定，其法心從交食時測驗數次，乃可較勘晝一。

translations.literal: This region's terrestrial longitude has not obtained its true rate, so the additive time is hard to fix; the method must rely on testing at several eclipses before one can compare them fully.
translations.idiomatic: This region's terrestrial longitude has not obtained its true rate, so the additive time is hard to fix; the method must rely on testing at several eclipses before one can compare them fully.

sentences.zh: 今此食依新術測候，其加時刻分，或後未合，當取從前所記地經度分，斟酌改定，此可以求裡差之真率，二也。

translations.literal: For this eclipse, if tested by the new method the additive time's degrees and minutes are afterward not in agreement, one should take the terrestrial longitude degrees recorded before and adjust them by deliberation— this can seek the true rate of local difference— second point.
translations.idiomatic: For this eclipse, if tested by the new method the additive time's degrees and minutes are afterward not in agreement, one should take the terrestrial longitude degrees recorded before and adjust them by deliberation—this can seek the true rate of local difference—second point.

sentences.zh: 時差一法，但知中無加減，而不知中分黃赤，今一經目見，人人知加時之因黃道，因此推彼，他術皆然，足以知學習之甚易，三也。

translations.literal: The method of time difference only knew that at center there is no addition or subtraction, but did not know that center divides yellow and red; now once seen with the eyes, everyone knows the additive time comes from the ecliptic; extending this to other methods, all are likewise easy to learn— third point.
translations.idiomatic: The method of time difference only knew that at center there is no addition or subtraction, but did not know that center divides yellow and red; now once seen with the eyes, everyone knows the additive time comes from the ecliptic; extending this to other methods, all are likewise easy to learn—third point.

sentences.zh: 即分數甚少，宜詳加測候，以求顯驗。

translations.literal: Even if the magnitude fraction is very small, one should observe and measure in detail to seek clear verification.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the eclipse magnitude is very small, one should observe and measure it carefully to obtain clear verification.

sentences.zh: 帝是其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 至期，光啟率監臣預點日晷，調壺漏，用測高儀器測食甚日晷高度。

translations.literal: When the day came, Guangqi led the supervising officials to mark the sundial, adjust the clepsydra, and use altitude-measuring instruments to measure the gnomon height at greatest eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: When the day arrived, Guangqi led the supervising officials to mark the sundial, adjust the clepsydra, and use altitude instruments to measure the gnomon height at greatest eclipse.

sentences.zh: 又於密室中斜開一隙，置窺筒、遠鏡以測虧圓，晝日體分板分數圖板以定食分，其時刻、高度悉合，惟食甚分數未及二分。

translations.literal: Also in a dark room he cut an oblique slit, placed a sighting tube and telescope to measure the crescent of deficiency, and used daytime solar-body fraction boards and fraction charts to fix the eclipse magnitude; the time and altitude all matched, but the magnitude at greatest eclipse fell short of two-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: In a darkened room he also cut an oblique slit and set up a sighting tube and telescope to measure the crescent of deficiency, using solar fraction boards and charts to fix the eclipse magnitude; the time and altitude all agreed, but the magnitude at greatest eclipse fell short of two-tenths.

sentences.zh: 於是光啟言：「今食甚之度分密合，則經度裡差已無煩更定矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guangqi said: "Now the degrees and minutes at greatest eclipse match closely, so there is no need further to adjust the longitude for local difference.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi then said, "Now the degrees and minutes at greatest eclipse match closely, so there is no need to adjust terrestrial longitude further.

sentences.zh: 獨食分未合，原推者蓋因太陽光大，能減月魄，必食及四五分以上，乃得與原推相合，然此測，用密室窺筒，故能得此分數，倘止憑目力，或水盆照映，則眩耀不定，恐少尚不止此也。」

translations.literal: Only the eclipse magnitude does not agree; the original reckoner probably because the sun's light is great and can reduce the moon's disk, only when the eclipse reaches four or five tenths or more does it agree with the original computation—yet this measurement used a sighting tube in a dark room, hence could obtain this fraction; if one relied only on the naked eye or a basin reflection, the glare would be unstable and the shortfall might be even greater."
translations.idiomatic: Only the eclipse magnitude does not agree. The original calculator probably assumed that the sun's great light can diminish the moon's disk, so only when the eclipse reached four or five tenths or more would it match his computation—yet this measurement used a sighting tube in a dark room and therefore obtained this fraction; if one relied only on the naked eye or a basin reflection, the glare would be unstable and the shortfall might be even greater."

sentences.zh: 時有滿城布衣魏文魁，著《曆元》、《曆測》二書，令其子象乾進《曆元》於朝，通政司送局考驗。

translations.literal: At the time there was commoner Wei Wenkuai of Mancheng, author of Calendar Origin and Calendar Measurement, two books; he had his son Xiangqian present Calendar Origin at court, and the Secretariat of Transmission sent it to the Bureau for examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the commoner Wei Wenkuai of Mancheng had written two books, Calendar Origin and Calendar Measurement, and had his son Xiangqian present Calendar Origin at court; the Secretariat of Transmission sent it to the Bureau for examination.

sentences.zh: 光啟摘當極論者七事：其一，歲實自漢以來，代有減差，到《授時》減為二十四分二十五秒。

translations.literal: Guangqi picked out seven matters for utmost debate: first, since Han times the surplus of the tropical year has had diminishing correction, reaching in the Season Granting twenty-four parts twenty-five seconds.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi selected seven points for decisive debate. First: since Han times the tropical year's surplus has been progressively reduced, until in the Season Granting it stood at twenty-four parts and twenty-five seconds.

sentences.zh: 依郭法百年消一，今當為二十一秒有奇。

translations.literal: By Guo's method one part consumed per century, it should now be twenty-one-odd seconds.
translations.idiomatic: By Guo Shoujing's method of one part consumed per century, it should now be twenty-one-odd seconds.

sentences.zh: 而《曆元》用趙知微三十六秒，翻覆驟加。

translations.literal: Yet Calendar Origin uses Zhao Zhiwei's thirty-six seconds, suddenly adding again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Calendar Origin uses Zhao Zhiwei's thirty-six seconds and suddenly adds to it again and again.

sentences.zh: 其一，弧背求弦矢，宜用密率。

translations.literal: Second, for arc back seeking chord and sagitta, one should use fine ratio.
translations.idiomatic: Second: in seeking chord and sagitta from arc, one should use a fine ratio.

sentences.zh: 今《曆測》中猶用徑一圍三之法，不合弧矢真數。

translations.literal: Now in Calendar Measurement they still use diameter one circumference three, not matching the true arc-sagitta numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar Measurement still uses the ratio diameter one to circumference three, which does not match the true arc-sagitta numbers.

sentences.zh: 其一，盈縮之限，不在冬夏至，宜在冬夏至後六度。

translations.literal: Third, the limits of slow-fast (equation) are not at winter and summer solstice but six degrees after winter and summer solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Third: the limits of the equation of center are not at the winter and summer solstices but six degrees after them.

sentences.zh: 今考日躔，春分迄夏至，夏至迄秋分，此兩限中，日時刻分不等。

translations.literal: Now examining solar motion, from spring equinox to summer solstice, summer solstice to autumn equinox—in these two limits the sun's hours minutes and parts are unequal.
translations.idiomatic: Examining solar motion now, from spring equinox to summer solstice and from summer solstice to autumn equinox—in these two limits the sun's hours, minutes, and parts are unequal.

sentences.zh: 又立春迄立夏，立秋迄立冬，此兩限中，日時刻分亦不等。

translations.literal: Also from beginning of spring to beginning of summer, beginning of autumn to beginning of winter—in these two limits too the sun's hours minutes and parts are unequal.
translations.idiomatic: From beginning of spring to beginning of summer, and from beginning of autumn to beginning of winter—in these two limits too the sun's hours, minutes, and parts are unequal.

sentences.zh: 測量可見。

translations.literal: Measurement can show it.
translations.idiomatic: Measurement makes this plain.

sentences.zh: 其一，言太陰最高得疾，最低得遲，且以圭表測而得之，非也。

translations.literal: Fourth, saying the moon at highest gets fast and at lowest gets slow, and that this was obtained by gnomon measurement—is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: the claim that the moon is fastest at highest altitude and slowest at lowest, and that this was obtained by gnomon measurement, is wrong.

sentences.zh: 太陰遲疾是入轉內事，表測高下是入交內事，豈容混推。

translations.literal: Lunar anomaly fast-slow is a matter within revolution; gnomon measuring high-low is a matter within nodal passage—how can they be mixed in one computation?
translations.idiomatic: Lunar anomaly belongs within the revolution cycle; gnomon measurement of altitude belongs within nodal passage—how can the two be mixed in one computation?

sentences.zh: 而月行轉周之上，又復左旋，所以最高向西行極遲，最低向東行乃極疾，舊法正相反。

translations.literal: Moreover above the moon's revolution cycle it again rotates leftward, so at highest moving westward is extremely slow, at lowest moving eastward is extremely fast—the old method is exactly opposite.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, above the revolution cycle the moon again rotates leftward, so at highest altitude it moves westward and is extremely slow, while at lowest it moves eastward and is extremely fast—the old method has this exactly reversed.

sentences.zh: 其一，言日食正午無時差，非也。

translations.literal: Fifth, saying at solar eclipse at noon center there is no time difference—is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: the claim that a solar eclipse at noon on the central meridian has no time difference is wrong.

sentences.zh: 時差言距，非距赤道之午中，乃距黃道限東西各九十度之中也。

translations.literal: Time difference speaks of distance; it is not distance from the equator's noon center but from the ecliptic limit's east and west each ninety degrees center.
translations.idiomatic: Time difference concerns distance—not distance from the equator's noon meridian, but from the center of the ecliptic's eastern and western limits, each ninety degrees from the node.

sentences.zh: 黃道限之中，有距午前後二十餘度者，但依午正加減，焉能必合。

translations.literal: Within the ecliptic limit there are cases more than twenty degrees before or after noon; merely adding and subtracting by true noon, how can it necessarily agree?
translations.idiomatic: Within the ecliptic limits there are cases more than twenty degrees before or after noon; merely adding and subtracting by true noon, how can the result necessarily agree?

sentences.zh: 其一，言交食定限，陰曆八度，陽曆六度，非也。

translations.literal: Sixth, saying the fixed limit for eclipses—eight degrees in the lunar calendar, six in the solar—is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: the claim that the fixed eclipse limit is eight degrees on the lunar path and six on the solar path is wrong.

sentences.zh: 日食，陰曆當十七度，陽曆當八度。

translations.literal: For solar eclipse, lunar calendar should be seventeen degrees, solar eight degrees.
translations.idiomatic: For a solar eclipse the lunar path should allow seventeen degrees and the solar eight.

sentences.zh: 月食則陰陽曆俱十二度。

translations.literal: For lunar eclipse, both lunar and solar calendars twelve degrees each.
translations.idiomatic: For a lunar eclipse both paths should allow twelve degrees.

sentences.zh: 其一，《曆測》云：「宋文帝元嘉六年十一月己丑朔，日食不盡如鉤，晝星見。

translations.literal: Seventh, Calendar Measurement says: "Song Emperor Wen Yuanjia year 6, 11th month jichou new moon, solar eclipse not fully like a hook, daytime stars visible.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: Calendar Measurement says, "In the sixth year of Emperor Wen's Yuanjia reign, on the jichou new moon of the eleventh month, the solar eclipse was incomplete like a hook and daytime stars were visible.

sentences.zh: 今以《授時》推之，止食六分九十六秒，郭曆舛矣。

translations.literal: Now computed by Season Granting, only six parts ninety-six seconds eclipse—Guo's calendar is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Computed now by the Season Granting, the eclipse would be only six parts ninety-six seconds—Guo's calendar is in error.

sentences.zh: 」夫月食天下皆同，日食九服各異。

translations.literal: Yet lunar eclipse is the same throughout the realm; solar eclipse differs in each of the nine domains.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lunar eclipses are the same throughout the realm, while solar eclipses differ in each of the nine domains.

sentences.zh: 南宋都於金陵，郭曆造於燕地，北極出地差八度，時在十一月則食差當得二分弱，其云「不盡如鉤」，當在九分左右。

translations.literal: Southern Song capital was at Jinling; Guo's calendar was made at Yan capital; north pole altitude differs eight degrees; at the eleventh month the eclipse difference ought to be about two-tenths weak; what they call "not fully like hook" should be about nine-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Song capital was at Jinling, while Guo's calendar was made at the Yan capital; polar altitude there differs by eight degrees; in the eleventh month the eclipse difference ought to be about two-tenths less, so what they call "incomplete like a hook" should be about nine-tenths.

sentences.zh: 郭曆推得七分弱，乃密合，非舛也。

translations.literal: Guo's calendar computed seven-tenths weak—that is a close match, not wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Guo's calendar computed seven-tenths weak—that is a close match, not an error.

sentences.zh: 本局今定日食分數，首言交，次言地，次言時，一不可闕。

translations.literal: This Bureau now fixes solar eclipse magnitude: first speak of nodal passage, next terrestrial, next time—none may be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: This Bureau now fixes solar-eclipse magnitude by speaking first of nodal passage, next of terrestrial position, next of time—none of these may be omitted.

sentences.zh: 已而文魁反覆論難，光啟更申前說，著為《學曆濁辨》。

translations.literal: Before long Wenkuai repeatedly debated in refutation; Guangqi again stated his prior views and wrote them as Clarifying Muddled Calendar Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wenkuai repeatedly debated in refutation; Guangqi restated his earlier views and set them down in Clarifying Muddled Calendar Learning.

sentences.zh: 其論歲實小餘及日食變差尤明晰。

translations.literal: His discussion of the tropical year's small remainder and solar eclipse parallax variation was especially clear.
translations.idiomatic: His discussion of the tropical year's small remainder and of parallax variation in solar eclipses was especially clear.

sentences.zh: 曰：「歲實小餘，自漢迄元漸次消減。

translations.literal: He said: "The tropical year's small remainder from Han through Yuan was gradually reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The tropical year's small remainder from Han through Yuan was gradually reduced.

sentences.zh: 今新法定用歲實，更減於元。

translations.literal: The new method now fixes the tropical year, reducing further from Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The new method now fixes the tropical year, reducing it still further from the Yuan figure.

sentences.zh: 不知者必謂不惟先天，更先《大統》。

translations.literal: The uninformed will surely say it is not only before Heaven but even before the Grand Concordance.
translations.idiomatic: The uninformed will surely say it is not only ahead of Heaven but even ahead of the Grand Concordance.

sentences.zh: 乃以推壬申冬至，《大統》得已亥寅正一刻，而新法得辰初一刻十八分。

translations.literal: Yet computing the renshen winter solstice—Grand Concordance got hai hour yin quarter first quarter; new method got chen first quarter eighteen parts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet computing the renshen winter solstice—the Grand Concordance gave hai hour, yin quarter, first quarter, while the new method gave chen, first quarter, eighteen parts.

sentences.zh: 何也？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How can this be?

sentences.zh: 蓋正歲年與步月離相似，冬至無定率，與定朔、定望無定率一也。

translations.literal: Because the proper year's length resembles pacing lunar departure; winter solstice has no fixed rate, just as mean new and full moons have no fixed rate.
translations.idiomatic: Because the proper year's length resembles pacing lunar departure: the winter solstice has no fixed rate, just as mean new and full moons have no fixed rate.

sentences.zh: 朔望無定率，宜以平朔望加減之，冬至無定率，宜以平年加減之。

translations.literal: Mean new and full moons have no fixed rate—one should add and subtract from mean conjunction and opposition; winter solstice has no fixed rate—one should add and subtract from the mean year.
translations.idiomatic: When new and full moons have no fixed rate, one should add and subtract from mean conjunction and opposition; when the winter solstice has no fixed rate, one should add and subtract from the mean year.

sentences.zh: 故新法之平冬至，雖在《大統》前，而定冬至恆在《大統》後也。

translations.literal: Thus the new method's mean winter solstice, though before the Grand Concordance, the true winter solstice is always after the Grand Concordance."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the new method's mean winter solstice, though it falls before the Grand Concordance, the true winter solstice always falls after it."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「宋仁宗天聖二年甲子歲，五月丁亥朔，曆官推當食不食，諸曆推算皆云當食。

translations.literal: He also said: "Song Emperor Renzong Tiansheng year 2 jiazi year, 5th month dinghai new moon, calendar officers computed eclipse but no eclipse; all calendars computed there should be eclipse.
