translations.idiomatic: He also said, "In the second year of Emperor Renzong's Tiansheng reign, a jiazi year, on the dinghai new moon of the fifth month, the calendar officers computed an eclipse but there was none; every calendar computed that there should be an eclipse.

sentences.zh: 夫於法則實當食，而於時則實不食。

translations.literal: By the method there should indeed be eclipse; by the time there was indeed no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: By the method there should indeed have been an eclipse; by observation there was indeed none.

sentences.zh: 今當何以解之？

translations.literal: How shall this be explained now?
translations.idiomatic: How is this to be explained?

sentences.zh: 蓋日食有變差一法，月在陰曆，距交十度強，於法當食。

translations.literal: Because solar eclipse has a parallax-variation method: moon in lunar calendar within ten-odd degrees of the node—by method should eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Because solar eclipses have a parallax-variation method: on that day the moon on the lunar path was a little over ten degrees from the node—by method an eclipse should occur.

sentences.zh: 而獨此日此之南北差，變為東西差，故論天行，則地心與日月相參直，實不失食。

translations.literal: But on this day alone the north-south difference became east-west difference; speaking of celestial motion, earth center and sun-moon were truly in line—indeed no failure of eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: But on this day alone the north-south parallax became an east-west parallax; in terms of celestial motion, the earth's center and the sun and moon were truly aligned—there was indeed no failure of eclipse.

sentences.zh: 而從人目所見，則日月相距近變為遠，實不得食。

translations.literal: But as seen by human eyes, sun-moon distance near became far—truly no eclipse visible.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as seen by human eyes, what had been a near alignment became a distant one—no eclipse was truly visible.

sentences.zh: 顧獨汴京為然，若從汴以東數千里，則漸見食，至東北萬餘裡外，則全見食也。

translations.literal: Only Bianjing was so; from Bian eastward several thousand li, eclipse would gradually appear; at ten-thousand-odd li northeast, total eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Only at Bianjing was this so; from Bian eastward for several thousand li the eclipse would gradually appear, and ten-thousand-odd li to the northeast it would be total.

sentences.zh: 夫變差時不同，或多變為少，或少變為多，或有變為無，或無變為有。

translations.literal: Parallax variation differs by time—sometimes much becomes little, little much, some becomes none, none some.
translations.idiomatic: Parallax variation differs by time—sometimes much becomes little, or little much; sometimes eclipse becomes none, or none eclipse.

sentences.zh: 推曆之難，全在此等。

translations.literal: The difficulty of calendar computation lies entirely in such matters."
translations.idiomatic: The whole difficulty of calendar computation lies in matters such as these."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，光啟入愉閣。

translations.literal: Before long Guangqi entered the Yuyin Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Guangqi entered the Yuyin Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 五年九月十五日，月食，監推初虧在卯初一刻，光啟等推在卯初三刻，回回科推在辰初初刻。

translations.literal: Year 5, 9th month 15th, lunar eclipse: Directorate computed first obscuration at mao first quarter; Guangqi et al. at mao third quarter; Huihui section at chen first quarter.
translations.idiomatic: In year five, on the fifteenth day of the ninth month, there was a lunar eclipse. The Directorate computed first obscuration at mao, first quarter; Guangqi and his colleagues at mao, third quarter; the Huihui section at chen, first quarter.

sentences.zh: 三法異同，致奉詰問。

translations.literal: Three methods differed; the throne sent inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The three methods disagreed, and the throne sent an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 至期測候，陰雲不見，無可徵驗。

translations.literal: At the date observation, overcast clouds—nothing to verify.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came, clouds hid the sky and nothing could be verified.

sentences.zh: 光啟具陳三法不同之故，言：

translations.literal: Guangqi fully stated the reasons for the three methods' difference, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi fully explained why the three methods differed, saying:

sentences.zh: 時刻之加減，由於盈縮、遲疾兩差。

translations.literal: Addition and subtraction of time comes from equation and anomaly slow-fast differences.
translations.idiomatic: The addition and subtraction of time come from the equation of center and from the lunar anomaly's fast-slow difference.

sentences.zh: 而盈縮差，舊法起冬夏至，新法起最高，最高有行分，惟宋紹興間與夏至同度。

translations.literal: Equation difference: old method starts at winter-summer solstice; new at apogee; apogee has motion in degrees—only during Song Shaoxing did it coincide with summer solstice.
translations.idiomatic: As for the equation difference, the old method starts at the winter and summer solstices, the new at the apogee; the apogee has motion in degrees—it coincided with the summer solstice only during the Shaoxing period of Song.

sentences.zh: 郭守敬後此百年，去離一度有奇，故未覺。

translations.literal: A century after Guo Shoujing it was more than one degree from departure—hence not noticed.
translations.idiomatic: A century after Guo Shoujing it had moved more than one degree from that point, and so the change went unnoticed.

sentences.zh: 今最高在夏至後六度。

translations.literal: Now apogee is six degrees after summer solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Now the apogee lies six degrees after the summer solstice.

sentences.zh: 此兩法之盈縮差所不同也。

translations.literal: This is how the two methods' equation differences differ.
translations.idiomatic: This is how the equation differences of the two methods diverge.

sentences.zh: 遲疾差，舊法只用一轉周，新法謂之自行輪。

translations.literal: Anomaly difference: old used only one revolution cycle, new calls it self-motion wheel.
translations.idiomatic: As for the anomaly difference, the old method used only one revolution cycle; the new calls it the self-motion wheel.

sentences.zh: 自行之外，又有兩次輪。

translations.literal: Outside self-motion are again two secondary wheels.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the self-motion wheel there are again two secondary wheels.

sentences.zh: 此兩法之遲疾差所以不同也。

translations.literal: This is why the two methods' anomaly differences differ.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the anomaly differences of the two methods differ.

sentences.zh: 至於《回回曆》又異者，或由於四應，或由於裡差，臣實未曉其故。

translations.literal: As for Huihui calendar differing again—it may be from four responses or from local difference; your subject truly does not know the reason.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Huihui calendar differing again, it may be from the four responses or from local difference; your subject truly does not know the reason.

sentences.zh: 總之，三傢俱依本法推步，不能變法遷就也。

translations.literal: In sum, all three schools compute by their own methods and cannot change method to accommodate.
translations.idiomatic: In sum, all three schools compute by their own methods and cannot alter their methods to accommodate one another.

sentences.zh: 將來有宜講求者二端：一曰食分多寡。

translations.literal: There are two matters worth pursuing later: first, eclipse magnitude more or less.
translations.idiomatic: There are two matters worth pursuing in future: first, whether the eclipse magnitude is greater or smaller.

sentences.zh: 日食時，陽晶晃耀，每先食而後見。

translations.literal: At solar eclipse the yang crystal dazzles—always eclipse before then visible.
translations.idiomatic: At a solar eclipse the sun's bright disk dazzles the eye—one always perceives obscuration too early and the return of light too late.

sentences.zh: 月食時，遊氣紛侵，每先見而後食。

translations.literal: At lunar eclipse wandering vapors invade—always visible before then eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At a lunar eclipse wandering vapors intrude—one always perceives brightness too early and obscuration too late.

sentences.zh: 其差至一分以上。

translations.literal: The discrepancy reaches more than one part.
translations.idiomatic: The discrepancy can exceed one part.

sentences.zh: 今欲灼見實分，有近造窺筒，日食時，於密室中取其光景，映照尺素之上，初虧至復圓。

translations.literal: To see true magnitude clearly, there is a newly made sighting tube; at solar eclipse in a dark room take its light and project on silk from first obscuration to full light.
translations.idiomatic: To see the true magnitude clearly, a newly made sighting tube is used: at a solar eclipse, in a dark room one takes its light and projects it onto silk from first obscuration to full return of light.

sentences.zh: 分數真確，書然不爽。

translations.literal: The fraction exact, written without error.
translations.idiomatic: The fraction is exact and can be recorded without error.

sentences.zh: 月食用以仰觀二體離合之際，鄞鄂著明。

translations.literal: At lunar eclipse use it to observe overhead when the two bodies join or part—obscure and clear.
translations.idiomatic: At a lunar eclipse one uses it to observe overhead when the two bodies join or part—the boundary stands out clearly.

sentences.zh: 與目測迥異。

translations.literal: Far unlike naked-eye observation.
translations.idiomatic: This is far unlike naked-eye observation.

sentences.zh: 此定分法也。

translations.literal: This is the method of fixing magnitude.
translations.idiomatic: This is the method of fixing magnitude.

sentences.zh: 一曰加時早晚。

translations.literal: Second, early or late additive time.
translations.idiomatic: Second, whether the additive time is early or late.

sentences.zh: 定時之術，壺漏為古法，輪鐘為新法，然不若求端於日星，晝則用日，夜則任用一星。

translations.literal: Fixing time: clepsydra is ancient method, wheel-clock is new—yet better to seek the end-point in sun and stars; by day use sun, by night any one star.
translations.idiomatic: For fixing time, the clepsydra is the ancient method and the wheel-clock the new—yet it is better to seek the reference in the sun and stars: by day use the sun, by night any one star.

sentences.zh: 皆以儀器測取經緯度數，推算得之。

translations.literal: All use instruments to measure longitude and latitude and compute thereby.
translations.idiomatic: In every case one uses instruments to measure longitude and latitude and computes the time thereby.

sentences.zh: 此定時法也。

translations.literal: This is the method of fixing time.
translations.idiomatic: This is the method of fixing time.

sentences.zh: 二法既立，則諸術之疏密，毫末莫遁矣。

translations.literal: Once these two methods are established, coarse and fine of all techniques—no trace escapes.
translations.idiomatic: Once these two methods are established, whether any technique is coarse or fine—nothing can escape detection.

sentences.zh: 古今月食，諸史不載。

translations.literal: Lunar eclipses ancient and modern—the various histories do not record.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar eclipses ancient and modern—the various histories do not record them.

sentences.zh: 日食，自漢至隋，凡二百九十三，而食於晦者七十七，晦前一日者三，初二日者三，其疏如此。

translations.literal: Solar eclipses from Han through Sui, 293 in all—eclipse on last day of month 77, day before last 3, second day 3—so coarse.
translations.idiomatic: Solar eclipses from Han through Sui number 293 in all—seventy-seven on the last day of the month, three on the day before last, three on the second day—so coarse.

sentences.zh: 唐至五代凡一百一十，而食於晦者一，初二日者一，初三日者一，稍密矣。

translations.literal: Tang through Five Dynasties 110—eclipse on last day 1, second day 1, third day 1—somewhat finer.
translations.idiomatic: From Tang through the Five Dynasties there are 110—one on the last day, one on the second, one on the third—somewhat finer.

sentences.zh: 宋凡一百四十八人，無晦食者，更密矣。

translations.literal: Song 148, none on last day—finer still.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song there are 148, with none on the last day—finer still.

sentences.zh: 猶有推食而不食者一。

translations.literal: Still one case computed eclipse but no eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Yet there is still one case where an eclipse was computed but none occurred.

sentences.zh: 至加時差至四五刻者，當其時已然。

translations.literal: Where additive-time error reached four or five quarters—it was already so at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Where the additive-time error reached four or five quarters, that was already evident at the time.

sentences.zh: 可知高速無窮之事，必積時累世，仍稍見其端兒。

translations.literal: One can know that matters of extreme speed without limit must accumulate time and generations before one slightly sees the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: From this one may know that matters of boundless extreme speed must accumulate through ages and generations before one can slightly glimpse their beginning.

sentences.zh: 故漢至今千七百歲，立法者十有三家，而守敬為最優，尚不能無刻之差，而況於沿習舊法者，何能現其精密哉？

translations.literal: Hence from Han to now 1700 years, thirteen schools of calendar makers, Shou Jing finest—still not without quarter error; how much less those following old methods—how could they show precision now?
translations.idiomatic: Hence from Han to the present, across seventeen hundred years and thirteen schools of calendar-makers, Guo Shoujing was finest—yet even he was not without quarter error; how much less those who merely follow old methods—how could they display precision now?

sentences.zh: 是年，光啟又進《曆書》三千卷。

translations.literal: That year Guangqi again presented Calendar Book 3000 juan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Guangqi again presented three thousand juan of the Calendar Book.

sentences.zh: 明年冬十月，光啟以病辭曆務，以山東參政李天經代之。

translations.literal: Next year winter 10th month Guangqi resigned calendar duties for illness; Shandong surveillance vice censor Li Tianjing replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the tenth month of winter, Guangqi resigned his calendar duties on grounds of illness, and Li Tianjing, surveillance vice censor of Shandong, replaced him.

sentences.zh: 逾月而光啟卒。

translations.literal: A month later Guangqi died.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Guangqi died.

sentences.zh: 七年，魏文魁上言，曆官所推交食節氣皆非是。

translations.literal: Year 7 Wei Wenkuai memorialized that calendar officers' eclipse and solar term computations were all wrong.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven Wei Wenkuai memorialized that the calendar officers' computations of eclipses and solar terms were all wrong.

sentences.zh: 於是命魁入京測驗。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wenkuai was ordered to the capital for testing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wenkuai was ordered to the capital for testing.

sentences.zh: 是時言曆者四家，《大統》、《回回》外、別立西洋為西局，文魁為炙局。

translations.literal: At the time four schools of calendar: Grand Concordance, Huihui, separately Western as Western Bureau, Wenkuai as Wei Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the time four schools of calendrics were contending: the Grand Concordance and the Huihui, and besides these the Western method was set up as the Western Bureau while Wenkuai headed the Wei Bureau.

sentences.zh: 言人人殊，紛若聚訟焉。

translations.literal: Each man his own view, noisy as a crowd at lawsuit.
translations.idiomatic: Each man had his own view, noisy as a crowd at lawsuit.

sentences.zh: 天經繕進《曆書》凡二十九卷，並星屏一具，俱故輔光啟督率西人所造也。

translations.literal: Tianjing edited and presented Calendar Book 29 juan total, and a star screen one set—all formerly supervised by Guangqi with Westerners.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjing edited and presented twenty-nine juan of the Calendar Book in all, together with one star screen—all formerly supervised by Guangqi with the Westerners.

sentences.zh: 天經預推五星淩犯會合行度，言：「閏八月二十四，木犯積履屍氣。

translations.literal: Tianjing pre-computed five planets' conjoining violations and motion degrees, saying: "Intercalary 8th month 24th, Jupiter violates Accumulated Corpse Star.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjing pre-computed the five planets' conjunctions, violations, and motion in degrees, saying, "On the twenty-fourth day of the intercalary eighth month, Jupiter will violate the Accumulated Corpse star.

sentences.zh: 九月初四昏初，火土同度。

translations.literal: 9th month 4th at dusk beginning, Mars and Saturn same degree.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the ninth month, at the beginning of dusk, Mars and Saturn will share the same degree.

sentences.zh: 初七卯正，金土同度。

translations.literal: 7th day mao exact, Venus and Saturn same degree.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day, at mao exact, Venus and Saturn will share the same degree.

sentences.zh: 十一昏初，金火同度。

translations.literal: 11th at dusk beginning, Venus and Mars same degree.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh, at the beginning of dusk, Venus and Mars will share the same degree.

sentences.zh: 舊法推火土同度，在初七，是後天三日。

translations.literal: Old method pushes Mars-Saturn conjunction on 7th day—that is three days after heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The old method places the Mars–Saturn conjunction on the seventh day—that is three days after heaven."

sentences.zh: 金火同度在初三，是先天八日。

translations.literal: Venus and Mars in conjunction fell on the third day; this was eight days ahead of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Venus and Mars in conjunction fell on the third day—eight days ahead of heaven.

sentences.zh: 」而文魁則言，天經所報，木星犯積屍不合。

translations.literal: 」But Wen Kui said that what Tianjing reported—Jupiter encroaching on Piled Corpse—did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: But Wen Kui said that Tianjing's report of Jupiter encroaching on Piled Corpse did not agree.

sentences.zh: 天經又言：「臣於閏八月二十五日夜及九月初一日夜，同體臣陳六韋等，用窺管測，見積屍為數十小星圍聚，木與積屍，共納管中。

translations.literal: Tianjing also said: "On the night of the twenty-fifth of the intercalary eighth month and the night of the first day of the ninth month, together with colleagues including Chen Liuwei, your subject used a sighting tube to observe and saw Piled Corpse as several dozen small stars clustered; Jupiter and Piled Corpse both entered the tube together.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjing also said, "On the night of the twenty-fifth of the intercalary eighth month and the night of the first day of the ninth month, together with colleagues including Chen Liuwei, I used a sighting tube to observe and saw Piled Corpse as several dozen small stars clustered together; Jupiter and Piled Corpse both entered the tube at once.

sentences.zh: 蓋窺圓徑寸許，兩星相距三十分內者，方得同見。

translations.literal: For the tube's circular aperture is about an inch across; only when two stars are within thirty minutes of arc of each other can they be seen together.
translations.idiomatic: The tube's circular aperture is about an inch across; only when two stars lie within thirty minutes of arc of each other can both be seen together.

sentences.zh: 如觜宿三星相距二十七分，則不能同見。

translations.literal: As the three stars of the Turtle Beak lodge are twenty-seven minutes apart, they cannot be seen together.
translations.idiomatic: As the three stars of the Turtle Beak lodge are twenty-seven minutes apart, they cannot be seen together.

sentences.zh: 而文魁但據臆算，未經實測。

translations.literal: Yet Wen Kui relied only on speculative calculation and had not carried out actual observation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wen Kui relied only on speculative calculation and had not carried out actual observation.

sentences.zh: 據雲初二日木星已在柳前，則前此豈能越鬼宿而飛渡乎？

translations.literal: According to him, on the second day of the ninth month Jupiter was already before Willow—how then could it earlier have flown across Ghost in a single leap?
translations.idiomatic: According to him, on the second day of the ninth month Jupiter was already before Willow—how then could it earlier have flown across Ghost in a single leap?

sentences.zh: 」天經又推木星退行、順行，兩經鬼宿，其度分晷刻，已而皆驗，於是文魁說絀。

translations.literal: " Tianjing further computed Jupiter's retrograde and direct motion, twice crossing Ghost; its degrees, minutes, and gnomon marks were afterward all verified, and Wen Kui's theory was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjing further computed Jupiter's retrograde and direct motion, twice crossing Ghost; its degrees, minutes, and gnomon marks were afterward all verified, and Wen Kui's theory was defeated.

sentences.zh: 天經又進《曆書》三十二卷，並日晷、星晷、窺筒諸儀器。

translations.literal: Tianjing further presented thirty-two juan of the Calendar Book, together with sundials, star dials, sighting tubes, and other instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjing further presented thirty-two juan of the Calendar Book, together with sundials, star dials, sighting tubes, and other instruments.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，又上《乙亥丙子七政行度曆》及《參訂曆法條議》二十六則。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of year eight he again submitted the Calendar of the Seven Regulators' Motion in the yihai and bingzi cycles and twenty-six articles for revising calendar methods.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year eight he again submitted the Calendar of the Seven Regulators' Motion in the yihai and bingzi cycles and twenty-six articles for revising calendar methods.

sentences.zh: 某七政公說之議七：一曰諸曜之應宜改。

translations.literal: A certain essay on the public discussion of the seven regulators sets forth seven points: first, the correspondences of the luminaries ought to be revised.
translations.idiomatic: A certain essay on the public discussion of the seven regulators sets forth seven points: first, the correspondences of the luminaries ought to be revised.

sentences.zh: 蓋日月五星平行起算之根則為應，乃某曜某日某時躔某宮次之數。

translations.literal: For the root of parallel motion from which sun, moon, and five planets begin calculation is the correspondence—namely the number of a given luminary on a given day and hour occupying a given palace and lodge.
translations.idiomatic: For the root of parallel motion from which sun, moon, and five planets begin calculation is the correspondence—namely the number of a given luminary on a given day and hour occupying a given palace and lodge.

sentences.zh: 今新法改定諸應，悉從崇禎元年戊辰前，冬至後，己卯日子正為始。

translations.literal: Now the new method revises all correspondences, all taking as start the moment of midnight on the jimao day after the winter solstice before the wuchen year, first year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Now the new method revises all correspondences, all taking as start the moment of midnight on the jimao day after the winter solstice before the wuchen year, first year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 二曰測諸曜行度，應用黃道儀。

translations.literal: Second, in measuring the luminaries' motion in degrees, one ought to use the ecliptic instrument.
translations.idiomatic: Second, in measuring the luminaries' motion in degrees, one ought to use the ecliptic instrument.

sentences.zh: 蓋太陽由黃道行，月星各有本道，出入黃道內外，不行赤道。

translations.literal: For the sun moves along the ecliptic; moon and stars each have their own paths, entering and leaving within and without the ecliptic, and do not move on the equator.
translations.idiomatic: For the sun moves along the ecliptic; moon and stars each have their own paths, entering and leaving within and without the ecliptic, and do not move on the equator.

sentences.zh: 若用赤道儀測之，所得經緯度分，須通以黃、赤通率表，不如用黃道儀，即得七政之本度為便也。

translations.literal: If one measures with the equatorial instrument, the longitude and latitude degrees obtained must be converted through the yellow-red conversion table—not as convenient as using the ecliptic instrument, which immediately gives the seven regulators' fundamental degrees.
translations.idiomatic: If one measures with the equatorial instrument, the longitude and latitude degrees obtained must be converted through the yellow-red conversion table—not as convenient as using the ecliptic instrument, which immediately gives the seven regulators' fundamental degrees.

sentences.zh: 三曰諸方七政行度，隨地不等。

translations.literal: Third, the seven regulators' motion in degrees differs by place.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the seven regulators' motion in degrees differs by place.

sentences.zh: 蓋日月東西見食，其時各有先後，既無庸疑矣。

translations.literal: For east and west see eclipses at different times, each with its own prior and posterior sequence—this is beyond doubt.
translations.idiomatic: For east and west see eclipses at different times, each with its own prior and posterior sequence—this is beyond doubt.

sentences.zh: 則太陽之躔二十四節氣，與月五星之掩食淩犯，安得不與交食同一理乎？

translations.literal: Then the sun's passage through the twenty-four qi and the moon and five planets' occultations, encroachments, and violations—how can they fail to follow the same principle as eclipses?
translations.idiomatic: Then the sun's passage through the twenty-four qi and the moon and five planets' occultations, encroachments, and violations—how can they fail to follow the same principle as eclipses?

sentences.zh: 故新法水成諸表，雖以順天府為主，而推算諸方行度亦皆各有本法。

translations.literal: Therefore the new method's completed tables, though taking Shuntian Prefecture as primary, also each have their own methods for computing motion in degrees for every region.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the new method's completed tables, though taking Shuntian Prefecture as primary, also each have their own methods for computing motion in degrees for every region.

sentences.zh: 四曰諸曜加減分，用平、立、定三差法，尚不足。

translations.literal: Fourth, the luminaries' additive-subtractive parts using the three difference methods of mean, stepped, and fixed are still insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the luminaries' additive-subtractive parts using the three difference methods of mean, stepped, and fixed are still insufficient.

sentences.zh: 蓋加減平行以求自行，乃曆家耍務。

translations.literal: For adding and subtracting parallel motion to seek true motion is the calendar expert's essential task.
translations.idiomatic: For adding and subtracting parallel motion to seek true motion is the calendar expert's essential task.

sentences.zh: 第天實圓體，與平行異類，舊所用三差法，俱從句股平行定者，於天體未合。

translations.literal: But heaven is truly a round body, unlike parallel motion in kind; the old three-difference methods, all fixed from right triangle parallel motion, do not fit the celestial body.
translations.idiomatic: But heaven is truly a round body, unlike parallel motion in kind; the old three-difference methods, all fixed from right triangle parallel motion, do not fit the celestial body.

sentences.zh: 即扣盈縮損益之數，未得其真。

translations.literal: Even when one applies the numbers of surplus, deficit, increase, and decrease, one does not obtain the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Even when one applies the numbers of surplus, deficit, increase, and decrease, one does not obtain the truth.

sentences.zh: 今新法加減諸表，乃以圓齊圓，始可合天。

translations.literal: Now the new method's additive-subtractive tables use circle to match circle—only then can one fit heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Now the new method's additive-subtractive tables use circle to match circle—only then can one fit heaven.

sentences.zh: 五曰隨時隨地可求諸曜之經度。

translations.literal: Fifth, at any time and place one can seek the luminaries' longitude.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, at any time and place one can seek the luminaries' longitude.

sentences.zh: 舊法欲得某日曜經度，必先推各曜冬至日所行宮度宿次，後乃以各段日度比算始得。

translations.literal: The old method, to obtain a given day's luminary longitude, had first to compute each luminary's palace degree and lodge at the winter solstice day, then compare by each segment's daily degrees before obtaining it.
translations.idiomatic: The old method, to obtain a given day's luminary longitude, had first to compute each luminary's palace degree and lodge at the winter solstice day, then compare by each segment's daily degrees before obtaining it.

sentences.zh: 今法不拘時日方所，只簡本表推步即是。

translations.literal: The present method is not bound by time, day, or place; one need only consult the basic tables and compute by steps—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The present method is not bound by time, day, or place; one need only consult the basic tables and compute by steps—that is all.

sentences.zh: 六曰徑一圍三，非弧矢真法。

translations.literal: Sixth, diameter one circumference three is not the true arc-sagitta method.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, diameter one circumference three is not the true arc-sagitta method.

sentences.zh: 蓋古曆家以直綿測圓形，名曰弧矢法，而算用徑一圍三，廖也。

translations.literal: For ancient calendar experts measured circles with straight chords, calling it the arc-sagitta method, yet in calculation used diameter one circumference three—crude indeed.
translations.idiomatic: For ancient calendar experts measured circles with straight chords, calling it the arc-sagitta method, yet in calculation used diameter one circumference three—crude indeed.

sentences.zh: 今立割圓八綿表，其用簡而大。

translations.literal: Now we establish the eight-chord table for circle division; its use is simple yet great.
translations.idiomatic: Now we establish the eight-chord table for circle division; its use is simple yet great.

sentences.zh: 弧矢等綿，但乘除一次，使能得之。

translations.literal: Arc-sagitta and similar chords require only one multiplication and division to obtain them.
translations.idiomatic: Arc-sagitta and similar chords require only one multiplication and division to obtain them.

sentences.zh: 七曰球上三角三弧形，非句股可盡。

translations.literal: Seventh, the three arc forms of spherical triangles are not exhaustible by right triangles.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, the three arc forms of spherical triangles are not exhaustible by right triangles.

sentences.zh: 蓋古法測天以句股為本，然句股能禦直角，不能禦斜角。

translations.literal: For the old method measured heaven with right triangles as foundation; yet right triangles can handle right angles, not oblique angles.
translations.idiomatic: For the old method measured heaven with right triangles as foundation; yet right triangles can handle right angles, not oblique angles.

sentences.zh: 且天為圓球，其面上與諸道相割生多三弧形，句股不足以盡之。

translations.literal: Moreover heaven is a round sphere; on its surface where paths intersect many three-arc forms arise—right triangles are insufficient to exhaust them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover heaven is a round sphere; on its surface where paths intersect many three-arc forms arise—right triangles are insufficient to exhaust them.

sentences.zh: 恆星之議四：一曰恆星本行，即所謂歲差，從黃道極起算。

translations.literal: On fixed stars there are four points: first, fixed stars' proper motion, namely what is called precession, is to be computed from the ecliptic pole.
translations.idiomatic: On fixed stars there are four points: first, fixed stars' proper motion, namely what is called precession, is to be computed from the ecliptic pole.

sentences.zh: 蓋各星距赤極度分，古今不同。

translations.literal: For each star's degrees from the red pole differ between antiquity and the present.
translations.idiomatic: For each star's degrees from the red pole differ between antiquity and the present.

sentences.zh: 其距赤道內外地也，亦古今不同。

translations.literal: Its distance within or without the equator likewise differs between antiquity and the present.
translations.idiomatic: Its distance within or without the equator likewise differs between antiquity and the present.

sentences.zh: 而距黃極或距黃道內外，則皆終古如一，所以知日月五星俱依黃道行。

translations.literal: But distance from the yellow pole or within or without the ecliptic is the same through all ages—whence we know sun, moon, and five planets all follow the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: But distance from the yellow pole or within or without the ecliptic is the same through all ages—whence we know sun, moon, and five planets all follow the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 其恆星本行，應從黃極起算，以為歲差之率。

translations.literal: Fixed stars' proper motion ought to be computed from the yellow pole as the rate of precession.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed stars' proper motion ought to be computed from the yellow pole as the rate of precession.

sentences.zh: 二曰古今各宿度不同。

translations.literal: Second, lodge degrees of each age differ between antiquity and the present.
translations.idiomatic: Second, lodge degrees of each age differ between antiquity and the present.

sentences.zh: 蓋恆星以黃道極為極，故各宿距星行度，與赤道極時近時遠。

translations.literal: For fixed stars take the ecliptic pole as pole; therefore each lodge's distance-star motion in degrees is now near, now far from the equatorial pole.
translations.idiomatic: For fixed stars take the ecliptic pole as pole; therefore each lodge's distance-star motion in degrees is now near, now far from the equatorial pole.

sentences.zh: 行漸近極，即赤道所出過距星綿漸密，其本宿赤道弧則較小。

translations.literal: As motion gradually nears the pole, the equator's lines crossing the distance star grow denser, and that lodge's equatorial arc is comparatively smaller.
translations.idiomatic: As motion gradually nears the pole, the equator's lines crossing the distance star grow denser, and that lodge's equatorial arc is comparatively smaller.

sentences.zh: 漸遠極，即過距星綿漸疏，其本宿赤道弧則較大。

translations.literal: As it gradually departs the pole, the lines crossing the distance star grow sparser, and that lodge's equatorial arc is comparatively larger.
translations.idiomatic: As it gradually departs the pole, the lines crossing the distance star grow sparser, and that lodge's equatorial arc is comparatively larger.

sentences.zh: 此緣二道二極不同，非距星有異行，亦非距星有易位也。

translations.literal: This is because the two paths and two poles differ—not that distance stars have different motion, nor that distance stars change position.
translations.idiomatic: This is because the two paths and two poles differ—not that distance stars have different motion, nor that distance stars change position.

sentences.zh: 如觜宿距星，漢測距參二度，唐測一度，宋崇寧測半度，元郭守敬五分。

translations.literal: As the Turtle Beak lodge distance star: Han measurement was two degrees from Shen; Tang one degree; Song Chongning half a degree; Yuan Guo Shoujing five minutes.
translations.idiomatic: As the Turtle Beak lodge distance star: Han measurement placed it two degrees from Shen; Tang one degree; Song Chongning half a degree; Yuan Guo Shoujing five minutes.

sentences.zh: 今測之，不啻無分，且侵入參宿二十四分，非一症乎？

translations.literal: Today's measurement shows not merely no minutes, but encroachment into the Shen lodge twenty-four minutes—is this not one proof?
translations.idiomatic: Today's measurement shows not merely no minutes, but encroachment into the Shen lodge twenty-four minutes—is this not one proof?

sentences.zh: 三曰夜中測星定時。

translations.literal: Third, determine time by measuring stars at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Third, determine time by measuring stars at midnight.

sentences.zh: 蓋太陽依赤道左行，每十五度為一小時。

translations.literal: For the sun moves leftward along the equator, fifteen degrees per small hour.
translations.idiomatic: For the sun moves leftward along the equator, fifteen degrees per small hour.

sentences.zh: 今任測一星距子午圈前後度分，又以本星經行與太陽經行查加減，得太陽距子午圈度分，因以變為真時刻。

translations.literal: Now measure at will one star's degrees before and after the meridian circle, then check addition and subtraction against that star's longitude motion and the sun's longitude motion, obtaining the sun's degrees from the meridian circle, and thereby convert to true time.
translations.idiomatic: Now measure at will one star's degrees before and after the meridian circle, then check addition and subtraction against that star's longitude motion and the sun's longitude motion, obtaining the sun's degrees from the meridian circle, and thereby convert to true time.

sentences.zh: 四曰宋時所定十二宮次，在某宿度，今不能定於某宿度。

translations.literal: Fourth, the twelve palace stations fixed in Song times at certain lodge degrees cannot now be fixed at those lodge degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the twelve palace stations fixed in Song times at certain lodge degrees cannot now be fixed at those lodge degrees.

sentences.zh: 蓋因恆星有本行，宿度已右移故也。

translations.literal: This is because fixed stars have proper motion and lodge degrees have shifted rightward.
translations.idiomatic: This is because fixed stars have proper motion and lodge degrees have shifted rightward.

sentences.zh: 太陽之議四：一太陽盈縮之限，非冬、夏二至，所謂最高及最高沖出也。

translations.literal: On the sun there are four points: first, the sun's limits of surplus and deficit are not the winter and summer solstices—namely what are called apogee and apogee opposition.
translations.idiomatic: On the sun there are four points: first, the sun's limits of surplus and deficit are not the winter and summer solstices—namely what are called apogee and apogee opposition.

sentences.zh: 此限年年右行，今已過二至後六度有奇。

translations.literal: This limit shifts rightward year by year; now it has passed more than six degrees beyond the solstices.
translations.idiomatic: This limit shifts rightward year by year; now it has passed more than six degrees beyond the solstices.

sentences.zh: 二曰以圭表測冬夏二至，非法之善。

translations.literal: Second, using the gnomon table to measure winter and summer solstice is not a good method.
translations.idiomatic: Second, using the gnomon table to measure winter and summer solstice is not a good method.

sentences.zh: 蓋二至前後，太陽南北之行度甚微，計一丈之表，其一日之影差不過一分三十秒，則一秒得六刻有奇，若測差二三秒，即差幾二十刻，安所得準乎？

translations.literal: For before and after the solstices the sun's north-south motion in degrees is extremely slight; reckoning a ten-chi table, one day's shadow difference is no more than one minute thirty seconds—then one second equals more than six quarters; if measurement errs two or three seconds, the error is nearly twenty quarters—how can one obtain accuracy?
translations.idiomatic: For before and after the solstices the sun's north-south motion in degrees is extremely slight; reckoning a ten-chi table, one day's shadow difference is no more than one minute thirty seconds—then one second equals more than six quarters; if measurement errs two or three seconds, the error is nearly twenty quarters—how can one obtain accuracy?

sentences.zh: 今法獨用春、秋二分，蓋以此時太陽一日南北行二十四分，一日之景差一寸二分，即測差一二秒，算不得滿一刻，較二至為最密。

translations.literal: The present method uses only spring and autumn equinoxes; for at these times the sun moves twenty-four minutes north-south in one day, and one day's shadow difference is one cun two fen—so even an error of one or two seconds in measurement computes to less than one quarter, tighter than at the solstices.
translations.idiomatic: The present method uses only spring and autumn equinoxes; for at these times the sun moves twenty-four minutes north-south in one day, and one day's shadow difference is one cun two fen—so even an error of one or two seconds in measurement computes to less than one quarter, tighter than at the solstices.

sentences.zh: 三曰日出入分，應從順天府起算。

translations.literal: Third, sunrise and sunset parts ought to be computed from Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Third, sunrise and sunset parts ought to be computed from Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蓋諸方北極出地不同，晨昏時刻亦因以異。

translations.literal: For every region's north pole elevation above the earth differs, and dawn and dusk times likewise differ accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: For every region's north pole elevation above the earth differs, and dawn and dusk times likewise differ accordingly.

sentences.zh: 《大統》依應天府算，上以晝夜長短，日月東刃西帶食，所推不準。

translations.literal: The Grand Concordance computed from Yingtian Prefecture; for day-night length above, and sun and moon girdling east and west with eclipses, what was computed was inaccurate.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Concordance computed from Yingtian Prefecture; for day-night length above, and sun and moon girdling east and west with eclipses, what was computed was inaccurate.

sentences.zh: 今依天罕改定。

translations.literal: Now it is revised according to the Tianhan [standard].
translations.idiomatic: Now it is revised according to the Tianhan [standard].

sentences.zh: 四曰平節氣，非上天真節氣。

translations.literal: Fourth, mean qi are not heaven's true qi.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, mean qi are not heaven's true qi.

sentences.zh: 蓋舊法氣策，乃歲週二十四分之一。

translations.literal: For the old method's qi policy was one twenty-fourth of the year's circuit.
translations.idiomatic: For the old method's qi policy was one twenty-fourth of the year's circuit.

sentences.zh: 然太陽之行有盈有縮，不得平分。

translations.literal: Yet the sun's motion has surplus and deficit and cannot be evenly divided.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sun's motion has surplus and deficit and cannot be evenly divided.

sentences.zh: 如以平分，則春分後天二日，秋分先天二日矣。

translations.literal: If evenly divided, then after spring equinox heaven is two days late, and before autumn equinox heaven is two days early.
translations.idiomatic: If evenly divided, then after spring equinox heaven is two days late, and before autumn equinox heaven is two days early.

sentences.zh: 今悉改定。

translations.literal: Now all are revised and fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Now all are revised and fixed.

sentences.zh: 太陰之議四：一曰朔望之外，別有損益分，一加減不足以盡之。

translations.literal: On the moon there are four points: first, beyond new and full moon there are separate surplus-deficit parts; one addition-subtraction is insufficient to exhaust them.
translations.idiomatic: On the moon there are four points: first, beyond new and full moon there are separate surplus-deficit parts; one addition-subtraction is insufficient to exhaust them.

sentences.zh: 蓋舊定太陰平行，算朔望加減，大率五度有奇，然兩弦時多寡不一，即《授時》亦言朔望外，平行數不定，明其理未著其法。

translations.literal: For the old fixed lunar parallel motion, computing new and full moon addition-subtraction, was mostly a little over five degrees; yet at the two quadratures the amounts differ—indeed the Season Granting also says beyond new and full moon the parallel numbers are not fixed, showing the principle but not setting forth the method.
translations.idiomatic: For the old fixed lunar parallel motion, computing new and full moon addition-subtraction, was mostly a little over five degrees; yet at the two quadratures the amounts differ—indeed the Season Granting also says beyond new and full moon the parallel numbers are not fixed, showing the principle but not setting forth the method.

sentences.zh: 今於加減外，再用一加減，名為二三均數。

translations.literal: Now beyond addition-subtraction we apply another addition-subtraction, called the two-three mean numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Now beyond addition-subtraction we apply another addition-subtraction, called the two-three mean numbers.

sentences.zh: 二曰緯度不能定於五度，時多時寡。

translations.literal: Second, latitude cannot be fixed at five degrees—it is sometimes more, sometimes less.
translations.idiomatic: Second, latitude cannot be fixed at five degrees—it is sometimes more, sometimes less.

sentences.zh: 古今曆家以交食分數及交泛等，測量定黃白二道相距約五度。

translations.literal: Calendar experts of antiquity and the present, from eclipse fractions and nodal breadth and the like, measured and fixed the yellow and white paths' mutual distance at about five degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar experts of antiquity and the present, from eclipse fractions and nodal breadth and the like, measured and fixed the yellow and white paths' mutual distance at about five degrees.

sentences.zh: 然朔望外兩道距度，有損有益，大距計五度三公度之一。

translations.literal: Yet beyond new and full moon the two paths' separating distance has deficit and surplus; the greatest distance totals five degrees and three and one-third degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Yet beyond new and full moon the two paths' separating distance has deficit and surplus; the greatest distance totals five degrees and three and one-third degrees.

sentences.zh: 若一月有兩食，其弦時用儀求距黃道度五度，未能合天。

translations.literal: If in one month there are two eclipses, at quadrature using instruments to seek five degrees from the ecliptic cannot fit heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If in one month there are two eclipses, at quadrature using instruments to seek five degrees from the ecliptic cannot fit heaven.

sentences.zh: 三曰交行有損益分。

translations.literal: Third, nodal motion has surplus-deficit parts.
translations.idiomatic: Third, nodal motion has surplus-deficit parts.

sentences.zh: 蓋羅喉、計都即正交、中交行度，古今為平行。

translations.literal: For Rahu and Ketu are the motion in degrees of true node and mean node; antiquity and the present treat them as parallel motion.
translations.idiomatic: For Rahu and Ketu are the motion in degrees of true node and mean node; antiquity and the present treat them as parallel motion.

sentences.zh: 今細測之，月有時在交上，以平求之，必不合算。

translations.literal: Now on fine measurement, sometimes the moon is on the node; seeking by parallel motion, the computation necessarily fails to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Now on fine measurement, sometimes the moon is on the node; seeking by parallel motion, the computation necessarily fails to agree.

sentences.zh: 因設一加減，為交行均數。

translations.literal: Therefore one addition-subtraction is set up as the nodal motion mean number.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one addition-subtraction is set up as the nodal motion mean number.

sentences.zh: 四曰天行無紫氣。

translations.literal: Fourth, celestial motion has no purple qi.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, celestial motion has no purple qi.

sentences.zh: 舊謂生於閏餘，又為木之餘氣。

translations.literal: The old said it arose from intercalary remainder and was also Jupiter's residual qi.
translations.idiomatic: The old said it arose from intercalary remainder and was also Jupiter's residual qi.

sentences.zh: 今細考諸曜，無象可明，知為妄增。

translations.literal: Now on fine examination of the luminaries, no phenomenon can clarify it—knowing it was falsely added.
translations.idiomatic: Now on fine examination of the luminaries, no phenomenon can clarify it—knowing it was falsely added.

sentences.zh: 交食之議四：一曰日月景徑分恆不一。

translations.literal: On eclipses there are four points: first, sun and moon shadow diameters in parts are constantly not one.
translations.idiomatic: On eclipses there are four points: first, sun and moon shadow diameters in parts are constantly not one.

sentences.zh: 蓋日月時行最高，有時行最高，有時行最卑，因相距有遠近，見有大小。

translations.literal: For sun and moon sometimes move at apogee, sometimes at apogee, sometimes at lowest point; because of distance near and far, they appear large or small.
translations.idiomatic: For sun and moon sometimes move at apogee and sometimes at perigee; because of distance near and far, they appear large or small.

sentences.zh: 又因遠近竿太陰過景，時有厚薄，所以徑分不能為一。

translations.literal: Also because of distance, pole, and the moon passing the shadow, sometimes thick, sometimes thin—therefore diameter parts cannot be one.
translations.idiomatic: Also because of distance, pole, and the moon passing the shadow, sometimes thick, sometimes thin—therefore diameter parts cannot be one.

sentences.zh: 二曰日食午正非中限，乃以黃道九十度限為中限。

translations.literal: Second, solar eclipse at noon is not the center limit; rather the ecliptic's ninety-degree limit is the center limit.
translations.idiomatic: Second, solar eclipse at noon is not the center limit; rather the ecliptic's ninety-degree limit is the center limit.

sentences.zh: 蓋南北東西差俱依黃道，則時差安得不從黃道道論其初末以求中限乎？

translations.literal: For north-south and east-west differences all follow the ecliptic—then how can time difference fail to follow the ecliptic path in discussing beginning and end to seek the center limit?
translations.idiomatic: For north-south and east-west differences all follow the ecliptic—then how can time difference fail to follow the ecliptic path in discussing beginning and end to seek the center limit?

sentences.zh: 且黃道出地平上，兩象限自有其高，亦自有其中。

translations.literal: Moreover when the ecliptic rises above the horizon, the two quadrants each have their high point and also their center.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover when the ecliptic rises above the horizon, the two quadrants each have their high point and also their center.

sentences.zh: 此理未明，或宜加反減，宜減反加，凡加進不合者由此也。

translations.literal: This principle not understood, sometimes one ought to add yet subtracts, ought to subtract yet adds—all cases where addition and advance fail to agree arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: This principle not understood, sometimes one ought to add yet subtracts, ought to subtract yet adds—all cases where addition and advance fail to agree arise from this.

sentences.zh: 三曰日食初虧復圓，時刻多寡恆不等，非二時折半之說。

translations.literal: Third, solar eclipse initial obscuration and final fullness—moments and amounts are constantly unequal; it is not the theory of halving the two times.
translations.idiomatic: Third, solar eclipse initial obscuration and final fullness—moments and amounts are constantly unequal; it is not the theory of halving the two times.

sentences.zh: 蓋視差能變實行為視行，則以視差較食甚前後，鮮有不參差者。

translations.literal: For parallax can change true motion into apparent motion; comparing parallax before and after greatest eclipse, rarely is there no discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: For parallax can change true motion into apparent motion; comparing parallax before and after greatest eclipse, rarely is there no discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 夫視差既食甚前後不一，又安能令視行前後一乎？

translations.literal: If parallax before and after greatest eclipse is not one, how can one make apparent motion before and after one?
translations.idiomatic: If parallax before and after greatest eclipse is not one, how can one make apparent motion before and after one?

sentences.zh: 今以視行推變時刻，則初虧復圓，其不能相等也明矣。

translations.literal: Now using apparent motion to compute changing moments, then initial obscuration and final fullness clearly cannot be equal.
translations.idiomatic: Now using apparent motion to compute changing moments, then initial obscuration and final fullness clearly cannot be equal.

sentences.zh: 四曰諸方各依地經推算時刻及日食分。

translations.literal: Fourth, each region according to terrestrial longitude computes moments and solar eclipse parts.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, each region according to terrestrial longitude computes moments and solar eclipse parts.

sentences.zh: 蓋地面上東西見日月出沒，各有前後不同即所得時刻亦不同。

translations.literal: For on the earth's surface east and west see sun and moon rise and set each with different prior and posterior sequence—therefore the moments obtained also differ.
translations.idiomatic: For on the earth's surface east and west see sun and moon rise and set each with different prior and posterior sequence—therefore the moments obtained also differ.

sentences.zh: 故見食雖一而時刻異，此日月食皆一理。

translations.literal: Therefore though the eclipse seen is one, the moments differ—this is one principle for both solar and lunar eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore though the eclipse seen is one, the moments differ—this is one principle for both solar and lunar eclipses.

sentences.zh: 若日食則因視差隨地不一，即太陰視距不一，所見食分亦異焉。

translations.literal: For solar eclipse, because parallax differs by place, the moon's apparent distance differs, and the eclipse fraction seen also differs.
translations.idiomatic: For solar eclipse, because parallax differs by place, the moon's apparent distance differs, and the eclipse fraction seen also differs.

sentences.zh: 五緯之議三：一曰五星應用太陽視行，不得以段目定之。

translations.literal: On the five planets there are three points: first, the five planets ought to use the sun's apparent motion and cannot be fixed by segment entries.
translations.idiomatic: On the five planets there are three points: first, the five planets ought to use the sun's apparent motion and cannot be fixed by segment entries.

sentences.zh: 蓋五星皆以太陽為主，與太陽合則疾行，沖則退行。

translations.literal: For the five planets all take the sun as master; in conjunction they move fast, in opposition they retrograde.
translations.idiomatic: For the five planets all take the sun as master; in conjunction they move fast, in opposition they retrograde.

sentences.zh: 且太陽之行有遲疾，則五星合伏日數，時寡時多，自不可以段目定其度分。

translations.literal: Moreover the sun's motion has slow and fast phases; then the five planets' days of conjunction and hiding are sometimes few, sometimes many—by nature one cannot fix their degrees and minutes by segment entries.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the sun's motion has slow and fast phases; then the five planets' days of conjunction and hiding are sometimes few, sometimes many—by nature one cannot fix their degrees and minutes by segment entries.

sentences.zh: 二曰五星應加緯行。

translations.literal: Second, the five planets ought to add latitude motion.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the five planets ought to add latitude motion.

sentences.zh: 蓋五星出入黃道，各有定距度。

translations.literal: For the five planets entering and leaving the ecliptic each have fixed separating degrees.
translations.idiomatic: For the five planets entering and leaving the ecliptic each have fixed separating degrees.

sentences.zh: 又木、土、火三星沖太陽緯大，合太陽緯小。

translations.literal: Again, when Wood, Earth, and Fire are in opposition to the Sun their latitude is large; in conjunction with the Sun their latitude is small.
translations.idiomatic: Wood, Earth, and Fire likewise have large ecliptic latitude when in opposition to the Sun and small latitude when in conjunction.

sentences.zh: 金、水二星順伏緯小，逆伏緯大。

translations.literal: Venus and Mercury in prograde concealment have small latitude; in retrograde concealment latitude is large.
translations.idiomatic: Venus and Mercury show small latitude during prograde stations and greater latitude during retrograde stations.

sentences.zh: 三曰測五星，當用恆星為準則。

translations.literal: Third: in measuring the five stars, fixed stars should be used as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Third, when measuring the five planets one should take fixed stars as the standard of reference.

sentences.zh: 蓋測星用黃道儀外，宜用弧矢等儀。

translations.literal: For besides measuring stars with the ecliptic instrument, arc-chord and similar instruments should also be used.
translations.idiomatic: Besides the ecliptic instrument, arc-and-chord instruments and the like should also be employed in stellar measurement.

sentences.zh: 以所測緯星視距二恆星若干度分，依法布算，方得本星真經緯度分。

translations.literal: From the measured planet's apparent distance to two fixed stars in so many degrees and minutes, and computing by rule, one then obtains the planet's true longitude and latitude in degrees and minutes.
translations.idiomatic: One measures the planet's apparent distance from two fixed stars in degrees and minutes, applies the prescribed computation, and thereby obtains the planet's true longitude and latitude.

sentences.zh: 或繪圖亦可免算。

translations.literal: Or drawing a diagram can also dispense with calculation.
translations.idiomatic: A plotted diagram can serve the same purpose and avoid lengthy calculation.

sentences.zh: 是時新法書器俱完，屢測交食淩犯俱密合，但魏文魁等多方陰撓，內官實左右之。

translations.literal: At that time the new method's books and instruments were all complete; repeated tests of eclipses and occultations all closely matched, but Wei Wenku and others obstructed in many ways, and eunuchs in fact supported them.
translations.idiomatic: By then the new method's treatises and instruments were complete, and repeated eclipse and occultation tests agreed closely with observation; yet Wei Wenku and others obstructed the reform at every turn, with eunuchs actively siding with them.

sentences.zh: 以故帝意不能決，諭天經同監局虛心詳究，務祈書一。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperor's mind could not decide; he instructed Tianjing together with the observatory bureau to investigate with open minds and earnestly seek a unified book.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore remained undecided and ordered Tianjing and the observatory officials to examine the matter impartially and produce a single authoritative calendar text.

sentences.zh: 是年，天經推水星伏見及木星所在之度，皆與《大統》各殊，而新法為合。

translations.literal: That year Tianjing's predictions for Mercury's stations of concealment and appearance and for Jupiter's degree position all differed from the Grand Concordance, while the new method matched.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tianjing's predictions for Mercury's visibility cycles and Jupiter's position all disagreed with the Grand Concordance but matched the new method.

sentences.zh: 又推八月二十七日寅正二刻，木、火、月三曜同在張六度，而《大統》推木在張四度，火、月張三度。

translations.literal: He also predicted that on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth month at yin proper, two quarters, Wood, Fire, and the Moon would together be at Zhang six degrees, while the Grand Concordance placed Wood at Zhang four and Fire and the Moon at Zhang three.
translations.idiomatic: He further predicted that at the second quarter of the yin double-hour on the twenty-seventh of the eighth month, Jupiter, Mars, and the Moon would stand together at six degrees in Zhang, whereas the Grand Concordance had Jupiter at four degrees and Mars and the Moon at three.

sentences.zh: 至期，果同在張六度。

translations.literal: When the time came, they were indeed all at Zhang six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When the day arrived, all three bodies were indeed at six degrees in Zhang.

sentences.zh: 九年正月十五日辛酉，曉望月食。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, on the fifteenth day of the first month, xinyou, there was a dawn lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine, on the fifteenth of the first month (xinyou), a lunar eclipse occurred near dawn.

sentences.zh: 天經及《大統》、《回回》、東局，各頂推虧圓食甚分秒時刻。

translations.literal: Tianjing and the Grand Concordance, Huihui, and Eastern Bureau each pre-computed the phases of loss, fullness, maximum eclipse, degrees, seconds, and times.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjing, the Grand Concordance calendar, the Huihui calendar, and the Eastern Bureau each computed in advance the phases of first contact, totality, and last contact, together with magnitude, seconds, and times.

sentences.zh: 天經恐至期雲掩難見，乃按裡差，推河南、山西所見時刻，奏遣官分行測驗。

translations.literal: Tianjing feared that at the appointed time clouds would hide the eclipse and it would be hard to see; he therefore applied local difference and computed the times as they would be seen in Henan and Shanxi, memorializing to send officials in separate routes to test.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing clouds at the capital, Tianjing applied terrestrial longitude correction, calculated visibility times for Henan and Shanxi, and memorialized to dispatch observers to test in both provinces.

sentences.zh: 其日，天經與羅雅谷、湯若望、大理評事王應遴、禮臣李焻及監局守登、文魁等赴臺測驗，惟天經所推獨合。

translations.literal: That day Tianjing with Rho, Schall, Court of Judicial Review reviewer Wang Yinglin, ritual official Li Huang, and observatory officers Shoudeng, Wenku, and others went to the terrace to test; only Tianjing's predictions alone matched.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the eclipse Tianjing went to the observatory with Rho, Schall, Wang Yinglin of the Court of Judicial Review, ritual official Li Huang, and observatory officers including Shoudeng and Wenku; only Tianjing's figures proved correct.

sentences.zh: 已而，河南所報盡合原推，山西則食時雲掩無從考驗。

translations.literal: Soon after, Henan's reports all matched the original predictions; Shanxi at eclipse time was cloud-covered and could not be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Reports from Henan soon confirmed the original predictions in full, while Shanxi was overcast at eclipse and could not be checked.

sentences.zh: 帝以測驗月食，新法為近，但十五日雨水，而天經以十三日為雨水，令再奏明。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the lunar-eclipse test showed the new method was closer, yet Rain Water fell on the fifteenth day while Tianjing had it on the thirteenth, ordered a further clear memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that the eclipse test favored the new method, but noted that the old calendar placed Rain Water on the fifteenth while Tianjing placed it on the thirteenth, and ordered him to explain this discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 天經覆言：

translations.literal: Tianjing replied in a further memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Tianjing replied:

sentences.zh: 諭節氣有二法：一為平節氣，一為定節氣。

translations.literal: Explaining that solar terms have two methods: one is mean solar terms, one is true solar terms.
translations.idiomatic: He explained that solar terms are reckoned in two ways: mean solar terms and true solar terms.

sentences.zh: 平節氣者，以一歲之實，二十四平分之，每得一十五日有奇，為一節氣。

translations.literal: Mean solar terms divide the year's true length into twenty-four equal parts; each part of a little over fifteen days is one term.
translations.idiomatic: Mean solar terms take the true length of the year, divide it into twenty-four equal parts, and treat each interval of slightly more than fifteen days as one term.

sentences.zh: 故從歲前冬至起算，必越六十日八十七刻有奇為雨水。

translations.literal: Therefore counting from the winter solstice before the year, one must pass sixty days and eighty-seven-odd quarters to reach Rain Water.
translations.idiomatic: Counting from the winter solstice before New Year, Rain Water on this scheme falls only after sixty days and eighty-seven-odd quarters.

sentences.zh: 舊法所推十五日子正一刻者此也，定節氣者，以三百六十為周天度，而亦以二十四平分之，每得一十五度為一節氣。

translations.literal: The old method's prediction of the fifteenth day, zi proper, one quarter is this. True solar terms take three hundred sixty as the degrees of heaven's circuit and likewise divide into twenty-four, each fifteen degrees being one term.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Concordance date of the fifteenth at the first quarter of zi belongs to this mean-term method. True solar terms treat the celestial circuit as 360° and likewise divide it into twenty-four terms of fifteen degrees each.

sentences.zh: 從歲前冬至起算，曆五十九日二刻有奇，而太陽行滿六十度為雨水。

translations.literal: Counting from the winter solstice before the year, after fifty-nine days and two-odd quarters, when the Sun has traveled a full sixty degrees, that is Rain Water.
translations.idiomatic: From the pre-year winter solstice, once fifty-nine days and two-odd quarters have passed and the Sun has moved sixty degrees, Rain Water has been reached.

sentences.zh: 新法所推十三日卯初二刻八分者此也。

translations.literal: The new method's prediction of the thirteenth day, mao primary, two quarters, eight fen is this.
translations.idiomatic: The new method's Rain Water on the thirteenth at the second quarter of mao and eight fen follows this true-term reckoning.

sentences.zh: 太陽之行胡盈有縮，非用法加減之，必不合天，安得平分歲實為節氣乎？

translations.literal: The Sun's motion has surplus and deficit; without applying the method's additions and subtractions it cannot match heaven—how can one equally divide the year's true length for solar terms?
translations.idiomatic: The Sun's motion is sometimes fast and sometimes slow; without the method's corrective additions and subtractions it cannot match heaven. How, then, can one simply divide the year's true length into equal terms?

sentences.zh: 以春分症之，其理更明。

translations.literal: Testing by the vernal equinox, the principle is still clearer.
translations.idiomatic: The vernal equinox makes the point still clearer.

sentences.zh: 分者，黃赤相交之點，太陽行至此，乃晝夜平分。

translations.literal: The equinox is where yellow and red intersect; when the Sun reaches here, day and night are equal.
translations.idiomatic: The equinox is the intersection of the ecliptic and equator; when the Sun reaches that point, day and night are equal.

sentences.zh: 舊法於二月十四日下，注晝五十刻、夜五十刻是也。

translations.literal: The old method under the fourteenth day of the second month notes day fifty quarters and night fifty quarters—this is it.
translations.idiomatic: The old calendar annotates the fourteenth of the second month with fifty day-quarters and fifty night-quarters, showing that day and night were already equal on that date.

sentences.zh: 夫十四日書夜已平分，則新法推十四日春分者為合天，而舊法推十六日者，後天二日矣。

translations.literal: If on the fourteenth day and night were already equal, then the new method's vernal equinox on the fourteenth matches heaven, while the old method's sixteenth is two days late.
translations.idiomatic: Since equality of day and night had already been reached on the fourteenth, the new method's equinox on that day accords with heaven, whereas the old method's equinox on the sixteenth is two days late.

sentences.zh: 知春分，則秋分及各節氣可知，而無疑於雨水矣。

translations.literal: Knowing the vernal equinox, the autumnal equinox and the other terms can be known, and Rain Water is no longer in doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Once the vernal equinox is fixed, the autumnal equinox and the other terms follow, and Rain Water need no longer be disputed.

sentences.zh: 已而天經於春分屈期，每午赴臺測午正太陽高度。

translations.literal: Then, as the vernal equinox drew near, Tianjing each noon went to the terrace to measure the Sun's altitude at noon.
translations.idiomatic: As the equinox approached, Tianjing went to the observatory each day at noon to measure the Sun's meridian altitude.

sentences.zh: 二月十四日高五十度八分，十五日高五十度三十分。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the second month the altitude was fifty degrees eight fen; on the fifteenth, fifty degrees thirty fen.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth of the second month the altitude was 50°8′; on the fifteenth, 50°30′.

sentences.zh: 末經乃言：

translations.literal: Finally he memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized further:

sentences.zh: 京師北極出地三十九度五十五分，則赤道應高五十度五分，春分日太陽正當赤道上，其午正高度與赤道高度等，過此則太陽高度必漸多，今置十四日所測高度，加以地半經差二分，較赤道已多五分。

translations.literal: At Beijing the north pole stands thirty-nine degrees fifty-five fen above the earth; the equator should then be fifty degrees five fen high. On the equinox the Sun is exactly on the equator, and its noon altitude equals the equator's altitude; past this the Sun's altitude must gradually increase. Now setting the altitude measured on the fourteenth and adding the semidiameter correction of two fen, compared with the equator it is already five fen more.
translations.idiomatic: At Beijing the north celestial pole stands 39°55′ above the horizon, so the equator at meridian passage should be 50°5′ high. On the equinox the Sun lies on the equator, and its noon altitude should equal that of the equator; thereafter the Sun's noon altitude must rise. Yet the altitude observed on the fourteenth, even after adding the two-fen semidiameter correction, already exceeds the equatorial altitude by five fen.

sentences.zh: 蓋原推春分在卯正二五分弱，是時每日緯行二十四分弱，時差二十一刻五分，則緯行應加五分強。

translations.literal: The original prediction placed the equinox at mao proper, two quarters and a little less than five fen weak; at that time the Sun's daily motion in latitude was twenty-four fen weak and the time difference twenty-one quarters five fen, so the latitude motion should add a little more than five fen strong.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier computation had placed the equinox at the second quarter of mao and slightly under 5¼ fen; with the Sun then moving about 24 fen of latitude per day and a time difference of 21¼ quarters, the latitude correction should add slightly more than 5¼ fen.

sentences.zh: 至十五日，並地半徑較赤道高度已多至三十分，況十六日乎？

translations.literal: By the fifteenth, together with the semidiameter, compared with the equatorial altitude the excess had already reached thirty fen—how much more on the sixteenth?
translations.idiomatic: By the fifteenth, even after the semidiameter correction, the noon altitude exceeded the equator by thirty fen; on the sixteenth the discrepancy would be still greater.

sentences.zh: 是春分當在十四，不當在十六也。

translations.literal: Therefore the equinox should fall on the fourteenth, not on the sixteenth.
translations.idiomatic: The equinox therefore belongs on the fourteenth, not the sixteenth.

sentences.zh: 秋風京然。

translations.literal: Receiving the imperial order, it was so.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted this and assented accordingly.

sentences.zh: 又出《節氣圖》曰：

translations.literal: He also produced a "Solar Term Diagram," saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a Solar Term Diagram, explaining:

sentences.zh: 內規分三百六十五度四分度之一者，日度也。

translations.literal: The inner scale, divided into three hundred sixty-five and one-quarter degrees, is the solar degree.
translations.idiomatic: The inner ring, graduated in 365¼°, marks solar motion.

sentences.zh: 外規公三百六十度者，天度也。

translations.literal: The outer scale, together three hundred sixty degrees, is the celestial degree.
translations.idiomatic: The outer ring, graduated in 360°, marks celestial motion.

sentences.zh: 自冬至起算，越九十一日三十一刻六分，而始曆春分者，日為之限敢，乃在天則已逾二度餘矣。

translations.literal: Counting from the winter solstice, passing ninety-one days, thirty-one quarters, and six fen before reaching the vernal equinox by solar reckoning is the solar limit; yet in the heavens it has already exceeded by more than two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: From the winter solstice, the mean solar calendar must pass 91 days, 31¼ quarters, and 6 fen before it registers the vernal equinox; by then the Sun in the sky has already advanced more than 2° beyond that point.

sentences.zh: 又越二百七十三日九十三刻，一十九分，而即交秋分者，亦日為之限也，乃在天不及二度餘。

translations.literal: Again passing two hundred seventy-three days, ninety-three quarters, and nineteen fen before reaching the autumnal equinox is likewise the solar limit; yet in the heavens it falls short by more than two degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Likewise, after another 273 days, 93¼ quarters, and 19 fen the mean calendar reaches the autumnal equinox, while in the sky the Sun still falls more than 2° short.

sentences.zh: 豈非舊法春分每後天二日，秋分先天二日耶？

translations.literal: Is this not the old method's vernal equinox each two days late and autumnal equinox two days early?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not proof that the old method places the vernal equinox two days late and the autumnal equinox two days early?

sentences.zh: 十年正月辛丑朔，日食，天經等預推京師師見食一分一十秒，應天及各省分秒各殊，惟云南、太原則不見食。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, on the xinchou new moon of the first month, there was a solar eclipse. Tianjing and others pre-computed that at the capital the eclipse would be one part and ten seconds; Yingtian and each province differed in parts and seconds, only Yunnan and Taiyuan would not see an eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten, on the xinchou new moon of the first month, a solar eclipse occurred. Tianjing predicted one tenth of the Sun's disk obscured at the capital; Yingtian and the provinces differed in magnitude, and Yunnan and Taiyuan would see no eclipse.

sentences.zh: 其初虧、食甚、復圓時刻亦各異。

translations.literal: The times of first contact, maximum, and last contact also each differed.
translations.idiomatic: The times of first contact, maximum eclipse, and last contact likewise varied by location.

sentences.zh: 《大統》推食一分六十三秒，《回回》推食三分七十秒，東局所推止遊氣侵光三十餘秒。

translations.literal: The Grand Concordance predicted an eclipse of one part sixty-three seconds; the Huihui, three parts seventy seconds; the Eastern Bureau predicted only about thirty-odd seconds of wandering vapor encroaching on the light.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Concordance predicted 1.63 tenths obscured, the Huihui calendar 3.70 tenths, and the Eastern Bureau only about three tenths of atmospheric haze dimming the Sun.

sentences.zh: 而食時推驗，惟天經為密。

translations.literal: But at eclipse time, by test, only Tianjing was close.
translations.idiomatic: At the eclipse, observation showed only Tianjing's prediction to be accurate.

sentences.zh: 時將廢《大統》，用新法，於上管理另局曆務代州知州郭正中言：「中曆必不可盡廢，西曆必不可專行。

translations.literal: At the time they were about to abolish the Grand Concordance and use the new method. Guo Zhengzhong, acting prefect of Daizhou in charge of a separate bureau for calendar affairs, said: "The Chinese calendar must not be wholly abolished, nor may the Western calendar alone be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: As the court was preparing to abandon the Grand Concordance for the new method, Guo Zhengzhong of Daizhou, who headed a separate calendar bureau, argued: "The Chinese calendar cannot be wholly discarded, nor should the Western calendar be enforced to the exclusion of all others.

sentences.zh: 四曆各有短長，當參合諸家，兼收西法。

translations.literal: The four calendars each have strengths and weaknesses; one should combine the schools and adopt Western methods together."
translations.idiomatic: Each of the four systems has its strengths and weaknesses; the proper course is to synthesize them and incorporate Western methods alongside the rest."

sentences.zh: 」十一年正月，乃詔仍行《大統曆》，如交食經緯，晦朔弦望，因年遠有差者，旁求參考新法與回回科並存。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year an edict ordered that the Grand Concordance Calendar still be used; for eclipses, longitudes and latitudes, new and full moons, and quarter moons, where long use had produced error, one might consult the new method and the Huihui section in parallel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year eleven an edict restored the Grand Concordance Calendar, allowing the new method and Huihui section to be consulted where long use had introduced error in eclipses, planetary positions, and lunation phases.

sentences.zh: 上年，進天經光祿寺卿，仍管曆務，十四年十二月，天經言：「《大統》置閏，但論月無中氣，新法尤視合朔後先。

translations.literal: In the preceding year Tianjing was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments while still supervising calendar affairs. In the twelfth month of the fourteenth year Tianjing said: "The Grand Concordance places intercalation merely by a month lacking a mid-term qi; the new method especially considers whether the conjunction falls before or after.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, Tianjing had been promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments while retaining charge of the calendar. In the twelfth month of year fourteen he explained: "The Grand Concordance declares an intercalary month whenever a month lacks a mid-term qi, whereas the new method also weighs whether the conjunction precedes or follows that qi.

sentences.zh: 今所進十五年新曆，其十月、十二月中氣，適交次月合朔時刻之前，所以月內雖無中氣，而實非閏月。

translations.literal: In the new calendar for the fifteenth year now presented, the mid-term qi of the tenth and twelfth months fall just before the conjunction of the following month; therefore although there is no mid-term qi within the month, it is in fact not an intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth-year calendar he now submitted, the mid-term qi of the tenth and twelfth months fall just before the next month's conjunction; those months lack a mid-term qi yet are not truly intercalary.

sentences.zh: 蓋氣在朔前，則此氣尚屬前月之晦也。

translations.literal: When the qi is before the conjunction, that qi still belongs to the last day of the preceding month.
translations.idiomatic: When a qi falls before the conjunction, it still belongs to the last day of the preceding month.

sentences.zh: 至十六年第二月止有驚蟄一節，而春分中氣，交第三月合朔之後，則第二月為閏正月，第三月為第二月無疑。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixteenth year there is only the Awakening of Insects node, while the vernal-equinox mid-term qi falls after the third month's conjunction; then the second month is unquestionably an intercalary first month and the third month the true second month."
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen the second month contains only the Awakening of Insects node, while the vernal-equinox mid-term qi falls after the third month's conjunction; the second month must therefore be an intercalary first month and the third month the true second month."

sentences.zh: 」時帝已深知西法之密。

translations.literal: By then the emperor already deeply knew the Western method's accuracy.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor was already convinced of the Western method's precision.

sentences.zh: 迨十六年三月乙丑朔日食，測又獨驗。

translations.literal: When in the third month of the sixteenth year, on the yichou new moon, there was a solar eclipse, testing again verified it alone.
translations.idiomatic: When a solar eclipse on the yichou new moon of the third month in year sixteen was tested, the new method alone proved correct.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔西法果密，即改為《大統曆法》，通行天下。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict said the Western method was indeed accurate and it was changed to the Grand Concordance Calendar Method, to be used throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict declared the Western method accurate, renamed it the Grand Concordance Calendar Method, and ordered its use throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 未幾國變，竟未施行。

translations.literal: Before long the dynasty changed; it was in the end not put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the dynasty fell, and the reform was never fully implemented.

sentences.zh: 本朝用為憲曆。

translations.literal: Our dynasty has used it as the constitutional calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty has adopted it as the official calendar.

sentences.zh: 按明制，曆官皆世業，成、弘間尚能建修改之議，萬曆以後則皆專己守殘而已。

translations.literal: According to Ming institutions, calendar officers all held hereditary posts; in the Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns they could still propose revisions, but after Wanli they only clung to their own ways and guarded the obsolete.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming institutions calendar officers held hereditary posts; during Chenghua and Hongzhi some still urged reform, but after Wanli they merely defended their own methods and resisted change.

sentences.zh: 其非曆官而知曆者，鄭世子而外，唐順之、周述學、陳壤、袁黃、雷宗皆有著述。

translations.literal: Among those who were not calendar officers yet knew calendrics, besides the Prince of Zheng there were Tang Shunzhi, Zhou Shuxue, Chen Rang, Yuan Huang, and Lei Zong, all of whom left writings.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the hereditary corps, Tang Shunzhi, Zhou Shuxue, Chen Rang, Yuan Huang, and Lei Zong also wrote on calendrics, besides the Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 唐順之未有成書，其議論散見周述學之《曆宗通議》、《曆宗中經》。

translations.literal: Tang Shunzhi left no completed book; his discussions are scattered through Zhou Shuxue's Calendar School General Discourse and Calendar School Central Classic.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shunzhi produced no finished treatise; his views appear scattered in Zhou Shuxue's Calendar School General Discourse and Calendar School Central Classic.

sentences.zh: 袁黃著《曆法新書》，其天地人三元，則本之陳壤。

translations.literal: Yuan Huang wrote New Book of Calendar Methods; its heaven-earth-man three origins derive from Chen Rang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huang's New Book of Calendar Methods, especially its doctrine of the three origins of heaven, earth, and man, derives from Chen Rang.

sentences.zh: 而雷宗亦著《合壁連珠曆法》皆會通回回曆以入《授時》，雖不能如鄭世子之精微，其於中西曆理，亦有所發明。

translations.literal: Lei Zong also wrote Combined Luminaries Linked Pearls Calendar Method; all harmonize the Huihui calendar with the Season Granting system. Though they cannot match the Prince of Zheng's subtlety, in Sino-Western calendrical principle they also made discoveries.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Zong's Combined Luminaries and Linked Pearls Calendar Method likewise seeks to reconcile the Huihui calendar with the Season Granting system. None equals the Prince of Zheng in refinement, yet each advanced understanding of Chinese and Western calendrics.

sentences.zh: 邢雲路《古今律曆考》，或言本出魏文魁手，文魁學本慮淺，無怪其所疏《授時》，皆不得其旨也。

translations.literal: Xing Yunlu's Investigation of Calendrics and Pitch Pipes Through the Ages is said by some to have come from Wei Wenku's hand; Wenku's learning was shallow throughout, so it is no wonder his commentary on the Season Granting system misses its intent.
translations.idiomatic: Some attribute Xing Yunlu's Investigation of Calendrics and Pitch Pipes Through the Ages to Wei Wenku; Wenku's learning was shallow, which explains why his commentary on the Season Granting system so often misses the point.

sentences.zh: 西洋人之來中土者，皆自稱甌羅巴人。

translations.literal: Westerners coming to China all call themselves men of Europa.
translations.idiomatic: Westerners who came to China called themselves men of Europa.

sentences.zh: 其曆法與回回同，而加精密。

translations.literal: Their calendar methods are the same as the Huihui's, but more precise.
translations.idiomatic: Their calendrical methods share a common origin with the Huihui system, but with greater refinement.

sentences.zh: 嘗考前代，遠國之人言曆法者多在西域，而東南北無聞。

translations.literal: Examining former ages, men of distant lands who spoke of calendar methods were mostly in the Western Regions, with nothing heard to east, south, or north.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back through history, experts in calendrics from distant lands appear chiefly in the Western Regions; the east, south, and north produced nothing comparable.

sentences.zh: 唐之《九執律》，元之《萬年曆》，及洪武間所譯《回回曆》，皆西域也。

translations.literal: The Tang's Nine Executions Pitch Standards, the Yuan's Ten-Thousand-Years Calendar, and the Hongwu-era translation of the Huihui Calendar are all from the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Nine Executions pitch standards, the Yuan Ten-Thousand-Years Calendar, and the Huihui Calendar translated in the Hongwu reign all came from the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 蓋堯命義、和仲叔分宅四方，義仲、義叔、和叔則以隅夷、南交、朔方為限，獨和仲但曰：「宅西」，而不限以地，豈非當時聲教之西被者遠哉。

translations.literal: Yao ordered Yi and He and Zhong and Shu to dwell in the four quarters; Yi Zhong, Yi Shu, and He Shu were bounded by Yuyi, Nanjiao, and Shuofang, but He Zhong alone is said to "dwell west" without being bounded by place—is this not because civilization's westward reach was then very far?
translations.idiomatic: Yao charged Yi, He, Zhong, and Shu to establish observatories in the four quarters; Yi Zhong, Yi Shu, and He Shu were assigned to Yuyi, Nanjiao, and Shuofang, but He Zhong was told only to "dwell in the west" without a territorial limit—surely because the civilizing influence had already extended far to the west.

sentences.zh: 至於週末，疇人子弟分散。

translations.literal: By the end of Zhou the astronomers' families dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Zhou period the hereditary astronomers had scattered.

sentences.zh: 西域、天方諸國，接壤西陲，百若東南有大海之阻，又無極北嚴寒之畏，則抱書器而西征，勢固便也。

translations.literal: The Western Regions and the lands of Tianfang border the western marches; if the southeast had the barrier of a great sea and there were no dread of extreme northern cold, then carrying books and instruments westward would naturally be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Regions and the lands of Tianfang adjoin the western frontier; had the southeast not been blocked by ocean and the far north not been forbiddingly cold, carrying astronomical learning westward would have been the easier path.

sentences.zh: 甌羅巴在回回西，其風俗相類，而好奇喜新競勝之習過之。

translations.literal: Europa lies west of the Huihui lands; their customs are similar, but the habit of curiosity, novelty, and rivalry in excellence goes further.
translations.idiomatic: Europa lies west of the Islamic lands; the peoples resemble one another, but the appetite for novelty and competitive mastery runs even stronger there.

sentences.zh: 故則曆法與回回同源，而世世增修，遂非回回所及，亦其好勝之慾為之也。

translations.literal: Therefore their calendar methods share the same origin as the Huihui's, yet generation after generation they revised and increased refinement until they surpassed the Huihui—this too was the work of that competitive desire.
translations.idiomatic: Their calendars therefore share the Huihui origin yet were refined generation after generation until they surpassed it—another fruit of that competitive spirit.

sentences.zh: 義、和既失其守，古籍之可見者，僅有《周髀》範圍，亦可知其源流之所自矣。

translations.literal: Once Yi and He lost their charge, of ancient books still visible only the scope of the Zhou Gnomon remains, from which one may also know whence the tradition sprang.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi and He lost their posts, the Zhou Gnomon alone survives among early texts to show how the tradition began.

sentences.zh: 夫旁搜採以續千百年之墜緒，亦禮秀求野之意也，故備論也。

translations.literal: To search widely and gather material to continue a thousand years' fallen thread is also the meaning of Confucius's "seeking in the countryside"; therefore it is fully discussed here.
translations.idiomatic: To gather widely and revive a thousand years of broken transmission is the spirit of "seeking knowledge in the villages"—hence this full account.
